entry.title: Attribution Through the Decoder: Prediction-Space Explanations for Structured Outputs

author.name: Zaer Bin Zaqy, Brinnae Bent

entry.summary: Shows that standard attribution applied to raw network outputs can credit inputs for changes a fixed decoder discards, and proposes attributing through the decoder differential instead, which for normalization decoders reduces to a scaled tangent projection. The paper characterizes invariance properties and zero-sensitivity points on spheres.

entry.title: Teaching What to Look For: Privileged Perception Questions for Agentic On-Policy Distillation in Video Captioning

author.name: Yifan Xu, Ruopeng Gao, Zhixiao Wang, Jiafu Tang, Yichun Yang, Zihao Wang, Yuanxing Zhang, Limin Wang

entry.summary: PQ-OPD trains video captioning agents that actively seek relevant moments and inspect regions, using training-only Perception Questions that specify what evidence should be gathered without revealing answers. This on-policy distillation approach encourages teacher exploration toward fine-grained visual evidence that fixed-frame sampling misses.

entry.title: CAST: Calibrating Correspondences for Training-Free Biomedical In-Context Segmentation

author.name: Mingze Jiang, Jiashu Han, Haonan Chen, Zhiyi Li, Yilun Du, Kunzan Liu

entry.summary: CAST is a training-free in-context segmentation framework for biomedical images, built on a frozen DINOv3 backbone, that calibrates fine-grained correspondences via a stability test to handle similar adjacent structures and cross-subject variation. New anatomical structures are specified by a few annotated exemplars at inference time, avoiding dense expert annotation. This addresses a major bottleneck in clinical translation.

entry.title: PAIR: Bringing Household Robots into the Smart Home

author.name: Junseong Pyo, Hyeongjin Kim, Jongwook Han, Seungwon Kook, Sungjib Lim, Yohan Jo

entry.summary: Introduces PAIR, a smart-home simulation environment grounded in the Matter protocol, providing 84 smart-device assets with functional control panels, APIs, and shared device state with evolving ambient conditions. It includes a benchmark of 40 tasks from 1,443 surveyed requests plus 340 human demonstrations for policy learning.

entry.title: Honest Brokers in AI Regulation: How Public Comments Introduce Evidence to Regulators

author.name: Sarah Tran, Anna-Maria Gueorguieva, Eva Maxfield Brown, Nicholas Weber

entry.summary: The authors build a corpus of 40 potential US AI regulations and 2,664 public comments, computationally extracting citations and informal references to study evidence flow to regulators. They find business commenters supply systematically different types and amounts of evidence, quantifying channels of potential regulatory capture.

entry.title: Big Brains, Tiny Board: Pupavision, an Agentic Physical AI Instrument for Monitoring Drosophila Pupariation and Lifecycle Transitions

author.name: Joel Sadler, Daniel Graham, Melanie Worley

entry.summary: Pupavision is a low-cost physical AI instrument (roughly $45-75 in parts) built on a single-board Linux computer that autonomously monitors Drosophila pupariation timing, with a frontier coding agent running its harness on the device while the model thinks in the cloud. The agent assists image capture, repairs its own code errors, and checks the experiment, demonstrating embedded agentic AI for biology instrumentation.

entry.title: Fidelity Regret: Measuring Simulator Misspecification in Verifiable Design

author.name: Noah Flynn

entry.summary: The paper introduces fidelity regret — the reference simple regret incurred when a cheap simulator selects a design instead of ground truth — and measures it in genetic-circuit design over a 21,362-design subspace spanning five gate libraries and three organisms. Mean normalized regret of 0.369 with only 6 of 72 cells at zero regret shows exact verifiers can still mis-rank physical performance, with strong dependence on the reference axis.

entry.title: Proximal Targets: Training Looped Refiners on Problems with Many Correct Answers

author.name: Syed Affan Daimi

entry.summary: The paper proves that looped refiners like HRM and TRM trained with deep supervision toward a single stored answer incur an irreducible loss floor when puzzles have multiple correct answers, with the loss-minimizing pass blending answers into invalid outputs. It proposes proximal targets that train each pass toward the correct answer nearest its current input, making correct answers fixed points. The method uses the same small parameter budget as prior looped refiners.

entry.title: WoRD: Diffusion-Based Posterior Inference for Online Goal Recognition

author.name: Almog Anschel, Sarah Keren

entry.summary: WoRD (Waypoint Recognition with Diffusion) infers an agent's goal from partial trajectory observations using a learned trajectory prior and warm-started denoising at each step. It avoids the limitations of purely symbolic goal recognition and of methods requiring explicit, hard-to-transfer dynamics models. This improves accuracy on ambiguous trajectory prefixes, where goal inference is hardest.

entry.title: Fragmented Markers, Mixed Results: A Systematic Review of AI Coding Assistants and Developer Productivity

author.name: Annemarie Wittig, Alina Mailach, Norbert Siegmund

entry.summary: This systematic literature review synthesizes evidence on how AI coding assistants affect developer productivity, finding the core problem is lack of comparability: studies use heterogeneous productivity markers, settings, and reporting styles. Using a staged review and the SPACE framework as a theory-informed lens, it consolidates both explicit productivity studies and broader human-centered developer outcomes. It offers the field a clearer map of what is and is not known.

entry.title: TIBECG: Temporal Information Bottleneck for Lead-Specific Demographic Privacy in ECG Waveform Release

author.name: Tsai-Min Chen (Research Center for Information Technology Innovation, Academia Sinica, Taipei, Taiwan, RIKEN Center for Interdisciplinary Theoretical and Mathematical Sciences), Jun Seita (RIKEN Center for Interdisciplinary Theoretical and Mathematical Sciences)

entry.summary: TIBECG applies a temporal information bottleneck to ECG waveforms so that leads can be released for diagnosis while limiting leakage of demographic attributes like age and sex. Across 6,386 hospital recordings, the method retained at least 95 percent of diagnostic macro-F1 per lead while substantially reducing demographic inference compared to conventional transformations.

entry.title: PromptPack: Training-Free Augmentation of Diffusion Editors for Intent-Aligned Spatial and Semantic Control

author.name: Sophia Zalewski, Mustafa Munir, Enting Liu, Anjul Patney, David Dynerman

entry.summary: PromptPack equips diffusion-based image editors with training-free Edit Guides: an edit-role partition labeling pixels as Keep, Permit, or Modify, and regional prompt assignment mapping spatial regions to text prompts. This lets users confine edits to intended regions while exactly preserving designated content, addressing underspecified intent in instruction-driven editing.

entry.title: ThermLeT: Transformer-based Temperature Prediction for 2.5D Chiplet Architecture

author.name: Varun Darshana Parekh, Anusha Devulapally, Sivani Devarapalli, Cassius Henderson, Shimeng Yu, Vijaykrishnan Narayanan

entry.summary: ThermLeT is a multimodal transformer surrogate that predicts steady-state temperatures in 2.5D chiplet packages from power density maps, spatial coordinates, material properties, and heat transfer rates, running in about 13 ms versus hours for finite element solvers. The authors also release a dataset of 6,221 chiplet layouts and report ~3.16C RMSE on a held-out test set.

entry.title: EGS: A Complementary Safety Framework for Educational LLMs

author.name: Zexuan Fei, Zhengnan Guo, Yiming Luo, Kaiyi Huang, Aimin Zhou, Bo Jiang, Fei Tan

entry.summary: EGS is a lightweight, model-agnostic runtime guardrail framework for adolescent-facing educational LLMs that goes beyond binary refusal by triaging query risk, redirecting gray-zone queries with pedagogical interventions, and auditing outputs. It argues educational safety requires contextual guidance rather than simple blocking. The system complements intrinsic alignment for a deployment setting with distinct risk profiles.

entry.title: Perception into Imagination: Executable Memory for World Models

author.name: Xianyao Li, Ruitong Tian, Rui Min, Fang Xu, Jing Du

entry.summary: Executable perceptual memory (EPM) is a world-model framework that advances explicit perceptual state alongside neural latent dynamics during imagination, with an evolving read-out informing reward prediction, value estimation, and policy learning. On Memory Maze 13x13, EPM reaches 30.37 return at 1M interactions versus 23.37 for a baseline using the same read-out only for policy and value. The work targets how agents use remembered perceptual facts after visibility or contact is lost.

entry.title: Encoding, Decodability, and Use: A Five-Layer Framework for Benchmark Measurement Audits with Evidence from UAV Intent Recognition

author.name: Zhirong Su, Tian Zhang

entry.summary: The authors propose a five-layer framework decomposing benchmark accuracy into observation, representation, decoding, use, and behavior, instantiated on the AeroIntent UAV intent recognition benchmark. The audit reveals unreliable observations in 7 of 20 drone programs and floors on the visual correlate of radial velocity, with some optical-flow features showing nominal signals. The framework provides a template for auditing whether benchmark scores actually measure the intended construct.

entry.title: Testing World Models on Actions They Have Never Seen: Held-Out Plans, Forecast Accuracy and Price Rules in Retail

author.name: Karthik Iyer

entry.summary: Proposes a general evaluation protocol for action-conditioned world models based on deliberately held-out actions scored against known answers, applied to retail price and promotion planning across 2,853 fitted models. Findings show forecast accuracy ranks model families reasonably (correlation 0.32-0.66) but can reverse within a single world model (down to -0.69) when planning into high-demand weeks. This challenges the common practice of trusting forecast accuracy as a proxy for counterfactual reliability.

entry.title: StitchRAG: Constructing Compact and Evidence-Preserving Contexts for RAG with Diffusion-Based Stitching

author.name: Minsang Kim, Junpyo Lim, Heeje Cho, Seungjun Baek

entry.summary: Proposes StitchRAG, which builds compact, information-dense RAG contexts by adapting a per-passage size reduction ratio via utility maximization trading retained information against computation cost, then extracting answer candidates and query keywords as anchors and using diffusion-based stitching to assemble evidence-preserving sentences. This reduces the computational overhead and noise degradation that long retrieved contexts cause. It targets RAG factuality without long-context costs.

entry.title: When Do Typed Decision Models Work in Transportation? Evidence from Travel Choice and Traffic Signal Control

author.name: Hongyang Zhang, Boyuan Deng, Siyuan Feng, Kai Chen, Junbo Zhang

entry.summary: Systematically evaluates typed decision models that combine natural-language understanding with structured action outputs on travel-mode choice prediction and traffic signal control, benchmarking TypeSafe Jev and GPT-6 Luna Decisions against conventional methods, RL algorithms, and chat LLMs. It maps when their low-latency, low-cost structure helps versus hurts.

entry.title: CodeReel: Accelerating Code-to-Video Agents with Exact Frame Reuse and Blocking-Aware Scheduling

author.name: Junyi Shen, Yao Lu

entry.summary: Analyzes inefficiencies in coding agents that generate video via build-inspect-edit loops, finding that 37.5 percent of frames in later builds were drawn before and half of builds only need a check verdict. CodeReel is a training-free execution layer with exact frame reuse keyed by drawing commands and blocking-aware scheduling.

entry.title: Learning Calibrated and Samplable Predictive Distributions of Surface-Ocean $\Delta p$CO$_2$ Using Tabular Diffusion Models

author.name: Gabriele Accarino, Mohammad M. Amirian, Thea H. Heimdal, Amanda R. Fay, Galen A. McKinley, Viviana Acquaviva

entry.summary: The authors apply Treeffuser, a conditional diffusion model with gradient-boosted-tree score functions, to learn full predictive distributions of surface-ocean CO2 partial pressure difference from 13 environmental, spatial, and temporal predictors. Unlike deterministic ML estimates with post hoc uncertainty, this yields calibrated, samplable distributions per observation on a held-out SOCAT test set. Better uncertainty quantification matters for estimating the ocean carbon sink, which absorbs roughly 30 percent of anthropogenic CO2 emissions.

entry.title: KVUse: Reusable-KV User Memory for Efficient LLM Recommenders

author.name: Xin Guo, Qiang Zhang, Xiang Zhou, Arushi Rai, Siyu Lin, Yifan Wu, Xiang Shen, Lei Huang, Qunshu Zhang, Xiangjun Fan, Lizhu Zhang

entry.summary: KVUse targets the serving cost of memory-augmented LLM recommenders, where repeatedly re-prefilling per-user natural-language profiles dominates latency because profiles sit at different prompt positions, defeating prefix caching. The method precomputes and reuses the KV cache of user memory so ranking LLM calls can consume it without re-prefill. The same group behind multimodal speculative decoding work addresses a distinct and practical inference-efficiency problem.

entry.title: How Much Distribution Shift Can a Clustering Withstand? Exact Split and Merge Certificates for Structured Transports

author.name: Alisina Bayati, Srinivasa Salapaka, Shahriar Talebi

entry.summary: This paper quantifies clustering robustness to distribution shift by providing exact certificates for when a committed clustering will require splits or merges. It builds a local stability criterion on phase-transition analysis from deterministic annealing, allowing precise characterization of how much shift a clustering can withstand before its structure must change.

entry.title: ReMoE: An Interpretable Mixture-of-Experts Framework for Human Mobility Recovery Forecasting Across Disasters

author.name: Yilin Lyu, Kang Liu, Wei Wang, Qifan Zhang, Ling Yin, Yushi Bai

entry.summary: ReMoE is an interpretable mixture-of-experts framework for forecasting post-disaster human mobility recovery, using a feature-guided router to combine specialist experts across different disaster events. The work targets transferability beyond individual disasters and produces interpretable expert assignments that map to recurring recovery types.

entry.title: LoopPrune: Recurrent Pruning for Looped Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Weizhong Huang, Huaijia Kou, Yan Zhang, Fei Chao, Xiawu Zheng, Liujuan Cao

entry.summary: LoopPrune is a pruning and recovery framework for looped diffusion transformers, which reuse shared blocks to deepen computation at low parameter cost. It combines recurrent importance estimation of shared-removal effects and position variation with shared reconstruction pools to bound position-specific errors on later inputs. This reduces the substantial repeated attention and MLP computation these architectures incur.

entry.title: Pareto-Informed Smart "Predict, then Optimize" for Multi-Objective Combinatorial Problems

author.name: Aabhash Dhakal, Tim Lachner

entry.summary: The authors extend the SPO+ decision-focused learning loss to multi-objective combinatorial optimization problems, arguing that standard scalarization fails to capture Pareto frontier trade-offs. Their Pareto-aware formulation targets applications like logistics and resource allocation where conflicting objectives must be balanced.

entry.title: Data-Driven Variable-Length Compression of 3D Representations

author.name: Yvette Y. Lin, Sai Karthikey Pentapati, Sarvesh Sundaram, Guandao Yang, Sara Fridovich-Keil

entry.summary: The authors propose a learned variable-length compression method for general 3D latent representations that adapts compressed size to per-shape complexity while exploiting dataset-level structure via feed-forward inference. It improves rate-distortion on both meshes and signed distance fields, with released code.

entry.title: Deciding Without Pointing: A Case Study of Whether a Decision Model Localizes the Anomalies It Detects

author.name: Hsiang-Hung Lee

entry.summary: A case study testing whether Clef-flash, a decision-mode vision-language model built on a Qwen3.5-9B backbone, actually localizes the industrial defects it detects. Results are mixed: detection AUROC is strong on MVTec AD but weaker on MVTec AD 2, and the routing attention that drives decisions does not reliably point at defect pixels, while backbone attention is fragile to question wording.

entry.title: Centroid Spectral Coupling: Implicit Alignment and Representation Diversity in Self-Supervised Learning

author.name: M. Hadi Sepanj, Benyamin Ghojogh, Saed Moradi, Paul Fieguth

entry.summary: Introduces Centroid Spectral Coupling, a single-term self-supervised objective that implicitly handles view alignment, representation diversity, and collapse prevention via a ridge-based spectral objective on centroid second-moment matrices. The paper provides an exact decomposition into nonnegative alignment and diversity components.

entry.title: Propose with the Gradient, Accept with the Loss: One Hedged Attack for Pixel-Sparse Robustness

author.name: Hon Ming Yan, Chun Pong Lau

entry.summary: Reframes pixel-sparse adversarial attacks (sPGD, Sparse-RS) as local searches composed of proposal distributions plus acceptance rules, and derives gradient-usage rules from Taylor bounds and measurements at visited states. The resulting hedged attack combines gradient proposals with loss-based acceptance to strengthen the sparse-AutoAttack ensemble for measuring robustness to few-pixel modifications.

entry.title: LoopZip: Visual Token Compression for Efficient Looped Vision-Language Models

author.name: Weizhong Huang, Zhicheng Liu, Yan Zhang, Fei Chao, Xiawu Zheng, Liujuan Cao

entry.summary: Proposes LoopZip, a training-free visual token compression method tailored to looped vision-language models that reuse shared layers. Unlike existing selection- or aggregation-based approaches, it accounts for how token importance changes across loop iterations, preserving information needed in later calls. This reduces compute and memory costs for parameter-efficient VLM architectures.

entry.title: Multimodal Masked Diffusion Autoencoder for Modeling Impaired Driving

author.name: John Gideon, Anshul Gupta, Megan Applegate-Kenton, Kayli Battel, Todd J Rowell, Patricio Reyes Gomez, Laporsha Dees, Emily Sumner, Avinash Balachandran, Guy Rosman

entry.summary: Proposes ID-MAE, a multimodal masked-diffusion autoencoder that augments impairment prediction with self-supervised reconstruction of masked gaze and trajectory data. Accompanied by DIVERT, a new driving-simulator dataset of 103 hours from 109 participants spanning ten cognitive, visual, and emotional impairment inductions. Addresses the scarcity of ground-truth cognitive-state labels in driver-assistance applications.

entry.title: The Shared Word: Evaluating Language Models on Dutch Word Puzzles

author.name: Rik van Noord, Maurice Voors

entry.summary: Introduces TSW-NL, a Dutch word-puzzle benchmark that is language-specific, open-vocabulary, human-curated, and deterministically scored, where each puzzle provides three clues to different senses of one word. Built from Wikipedia disambiguation pages with manual curation, the 222-instance dataset includes three independent human answers per item.

entry.title: It's My Turn! Interpretable Methods Reveal Developmental Differences from Mother-Child Conversational Dynamics

author.name: A'di Dust, Anura Deshpande, Pat Levitt, Maja Matari\'c

entry.summary: The authors build an interpretable computational framework combining sequence analysis, information-theoretic measures, and Bayesian hierarchical modeling to study temporal dynamics in mother-child conversations across 94 dyads with two-year-olds. They find that dyads with lower language development scores show distinct turn-taking patterns. The work demonstrates how rigorous interpretable ML can yield insights in developmental and behavioral science.

entry.title: CueSplat: Learning to Schedule Sparse Deformation for Dynamic Gaussian Splatting on Edge Devices

author.name: Qingyuan Tang (Shanghai Jiaotong University), He Zhu (Shanghai Jiaotong University), Shixuan Sun (Shanghai Jiaotong University), Anbang Wu (Shanghai Jiaotong University), Jingwen Leng (Shanghai Jiaotong University), Minyi Guo (Shanghai Jiaotong University), Yu Feng (Shanghai Jiaotong University)

entry.summary: CueSplat is a post-training framework for 4D Gaussian splatting that predicts Gaussian attributes from recent temporal history and uses a lightweight learned router to decide which Gaussians receive exact deformation updates within a calibrated per-scene budget. This exploits local temporal predictability to cut deformation-network compute on edge devices while keeping the pretrained backbone frozen. It targets the practical constraint of rendering dynamic 3D content on resource-limited hardware.

entry.title: CEVA: Complementary Evidence Verification via Frame-Level Reorganization for Short-Video Fake News Detection

author.name: Wenshen Yang, Junfeng Hao, Jing Li, Decheng Liu, Yangkunfei, Shuyu Jiang, Haizhou Wang

entry.summary: CEVA is a framework for detecting fake news in short videos by organizing frames according to their evidential roles before multimodal fusion, recognizing that similar frames may repeat misleading claims while less prominent frames may contradict them. It claims to be the first short-video fake news detector with explicit evidential frame organization.

entry.title: When Neural Collapse Fails to Route: Routing Drift in Continual Learning

author.name: Nicolas Larue

entry.summary: Identifies routing drift as the failure mode of progressive neural-collapse classifiers in continual learning: samples can remain separable within their own task block yet receive their highest global score from another block, yielding high task-incremental but low class-incremental accuracy. The paper formalizes route accuracy to decompose within-task discrimination from cross-task score comparability and suggests classifier-level corrections.

entry.title: PlaceTally: A Test-Time Memory Model for Constructing Place Graphs

author.name: Alibay Osmanli, Shaogang Gong

entry.summary: Proposes PlaceTally, a question-blind test-time memory that builds a place graph per video, exploiting the observation that video segments grouped by place share almost no distinct objects, enabling robust counting of distinct objects when the camera revisits locations. This avoids vocabulary constraints and double-counting across video parts.

entry.title: Let Samples Sing in Chorus: Mitigating Spurious Correlations via Cross-view Consensus

author.name: Weiwei Li, Junzhuo Liu, Tong Chu, Hengfu Yu, Yinjie Lei, Wen Li

entry.summary: CHORD is a multi-view debiasing framework that aggregates evidence across multiple representation spaces to identify and counter spurious correlations, based on the insight that a bias hidden in one feature space may be visible in another. It aims to improve robustness on underrepresented groups without relying on annotated bias attributes.

entry.title: Kolibri: Color Finds the Place, Refinement Sets the Pose for RGB-D Localization in Colored Point Clouds

author.name: Leonel Aguilar, Bartu Tuncay, Christoph Hoelscher

entry.summary: Kolibri is a tiny 55,712-parameter graph network for camera localization in unseen buildings that only needs to identify the place, letting geometric refinement converge nearby initial poses to the correct final pose. It matches a much larger baseline (GeDi) on 96 unseen ScanNet rooms and runs at 82 ms per frame on an RTX 2080 Ti.

entry.title: BRepA: Graph-Based B-Rep Pretraining for Unified CAD Understanding and Generation

author.name: Dekai Zhu, Zhaiyu Chen, Stefan Gavranovic, Slobodan Ilic

entry.summary: BRepA is a self-supervised pretraining framework for boundary-representation (B-Rep) CAD data that reconstructs both geometry and topology via graph-based modeling. Pretraining once on large-scale unlabeled CAD data supports multiple downstream tasks like segmentation and novel shape generation. This is valuable because labeled B-Rep data is scarce and task-specific architectures have dominated the field.

entry.title: Any2Building: Unifying Point Clouds and Images for Building Reconstruction via Shared Spatial Queries

author.name: Hongye Hou, Zhuoxiao Li, Liu Xiangyu, Tengxi Wang, Jing Ou, Dongli Wu, Shuai Zhang, Tongyan Hua, Wufan Zhao

entry.summary: Any2Building is a unified model for LoD2 building reconstruction from partial point clouds, overhead images, or both, using an occupancy-grounded shared spatial query representation to align geometric and visual cues in 3D. It targets 3D urban modeling and digital twin applications.

entry.title: Evolving Neural Solvers for Multi-objective Combinatorial Optimization

author.name: Ya-Hui Jia, Le-Xin Wen, Yang Wang, Wei-Neng Chen, Yi Mei

entry.summary: The Evolving Neural Solver (ENS) trains a small set of preference-specific neural models and uses evolutionary computation to evolve them into a diverse collection of solvers, improving solution quality and Pareto front coverage in multi-objective combinatorial optimization. This avoids the cost of dedicated per-preference models and the duplication issues of a single shared model.

entry.title: DGV-DLIVO: Degeneracy-Guided Visual Fusion for Direct LiDAR-Inertial-Visual Odometry in Degenerate Tunnel Environments

author.name: Junrui Zhang

entry.summary: DGV-DLIVO is a LiDAR-inertial-visual odometry system for underground tunnels where LiDAR degeneracy and poor visual texture coincide. It explicitly detects LiDAR-degenerate directions and uses vision selectively along those axes, enabling continuous longitudinal localization in hydropower spillway tunnels and drainage galleries.

entry.title: Risk Density RRT$^*$: Planning in the Space of Probability

author.name: Lorenzo Paiola, Giorgio Grioli, Antonio Bicchi

entry.summary: RD-RRT* extends RRT* to make collision probability, or risk defined as probability times severity, the direct planning objective rather than a constraint, via a Risk Density functional that evaluates continuous paths holistically. A hybrid variant balances risk against path length using a penalty term.

entry.title: Lyapunov-Inspired Sustained Balance on Dynamically Responsive Supports

author.name: Changyan Li, Guiyin Tian, Jing Xia, Shiyan Hu

entry.summary: Introduces LISST, a learning framework for sustained robot balance on mechanically responsive supports, treating stabilization and support-motion suppression as a coupled regulation problem. It uses Lyapunov-inspired ideas and history-aware policies so that earlier corrective actions inform later ones. This addresses an often-ignored gap where conventional balance assumes rigid ground.

entry.title: Making sense of Recursive Self Improvement

author.name: invertedpassion

entry.summary: A linkpost analyzing whether recursive self-improvement is imminent, centered on a recent METR report suggesting Anthropic's rate of AI R&D progress has roughly doubled since October 2025, attributed partly to Anthropic's own use of AI in research. The author flags caveats such as redacted data and Anthropic's IPO incentives, then argues a crude form of recursive improvement is already underway.

entry.title: What do kill switches actually buy us?

author.name: Jacob Brinton

entry.summary: This analysis evaluates what mandatory kill switches in US datacenters would actually achieve against three AI failure routes: loss of control, extreme power concentration, and societal destabilization. It concludes kill switches mainly help against destabilization and reckless early AIs via indirect effects, carry risks of complacency and suppressed warning shots, but may seed broader verification and transparency infrastructure.

entry.title: California State Politics AI Safety Overview

author.name: Felix Moses

entry.summary: A landscape review of California state-level AI safety legislation, covering SB 53's safety framework and incident reporting requirements, SB 813's Independent Verification Organization auditors, AB 1405's auditor registry, and a recent executive order. The author, motivated by reports that only about 15 FTE work on AI safety in CA state politics, maps the current legal terrain to identify high-leverage engagement opportunities.

entry.title: KV-LTM: Persistent Per-Session KV Caches as Long-Term Memory for Personal Assistants

author.name: Ziv Kfir, Ido Kfir

entry.summary: KV-LTM proposes storing each session's raw text plus its KV cache under a fixed reader model, answering questions by restoring cached sessions and appending the query, thereby avoiding lossy derivation steps between memory write and read. Text remains the memory of record while the cache acts as a recompute-free prefill accelerator that degrades gracefully.

entry.title: Outcome-Balanced PPO and Policy-Induced Flow Rectification for Flow-Based VLA Policies

author.name: Yuhan Wang, Ruiyang Wang, Jiaguan Zhu

entry.summary: The paper introduces an RL post-training framework for flow-based vision-language-action policies combining Outcome-Balanced PPO, which reweights advantages using task success-rate estimates, with policy-induced flow rectification to protect the velocity-field geometry during policy updates. This tackles sparse multi-task rollouts and the instability of applying PPO to flow models in robotics. It is relevant to the growing use of flow-matching policies in robot learning.

entry.title: LLMs as Validators for Cross-Chain Bridges: Evaluating Source-Level and Transaction-Level Attack Detection on Solana

author.name: Yasir Rahman, Ishraq Samiha, Shahnewaz Karim Sakib, Anindya Bijoy Das

entry.summary: The paper evaluates whether LLMs can diagnose vulnerabilities in Solana cross-chain bridge programs from source code and transaction records, using a native Rust lock-and-mint bridge with four exploitable variants modeled on real incidents like Cashio and Wormhole. Paired vulnerable and secure programs enable rigorous assessment of LLM-based attack detection at both source and transaction level.

entry.title: FaceRiff: Data-Efficient Unified Text-to-3D Face Asset Synthesis via Geometric Conditioning

author.name: Elly Akhoundi, Mathieu Lamarre, Thibault Goyallon, Patrick Anderson, \'Etienne Danvoye

entry.summary: FaceRiff generates complete 3D face assets including mesh, albedo, and displacement from text in a shared UV space, adapting a pretrained SDXL backbone with LoRA adapters and geometric conditioning. It is data- and parameter-efficient compared to existing methods that are slow, single-modality, or require large specialized datasets.

entry.title: RICoT: Recurrent Interleaved Chain-of-Thought for Page Stream Segmentation

author.name: Prashant Khatri, Bhavana Malagavalli, Saiful Haq, Niyati Chhaya

entry.summary: RICoT is a prompting framework that recasts page stream segmentation as a sequential process over the whole document stream, reasoning page by page within sliding windows and carrying forward a compact record of prior content across windows to keep per-call cost bounded. This mirrors how a human reader commits boundary decisions before moving on. It improves on prior LLM approaches that classify boundaries over only a few neighboring pages.

entry.title: ForceBody: Force-Paired Parametric Body Motion with Torque Uncertainty

author.name: Joonwoo Kwon, Yufei Zhang, Xiaoming Liu, Zijun Cui

entry.summary: Introduces ForceBody, the first dataset pairing ground-truth force supervision with parametric body representations for human motion, including per-torque reliability estimates that prior inverse-dynamics-derived datasets lack. This bridges biomechanics force data and modern learning-based motion pipelines for reconstruction and generation. It supports physics-aware animation, biomechanics, and robotics applications where forces and torques drive motion.

entry.title: Mind the Gap: A Deployed Multi-Agent System for Documentation Maintenance

author.name: Lorenzo Masoero

entry.summary: Describes a deployed multi-agent system for keeping customer-facing documentation in sync with fast-evolving code, built around a triage of explicit signals (support tickets) and implicit signals (code-documentation discrepancies). It argues the documentation gap is worsening as users rely on LLM agents consuming docs as their primary interface.

entry.title: SilverSpoon-KD: A General-Purpose Toolkit for Knowledge Distillation

author.name: Xaver R. Davey, David Broman

entry.summary: SilverSpoon-KD is an open-source PyTorch toolkit that unifies many knowledge distillation paradigms and architectural relationships behind a single API, including what the authors say is the first general-purpose blockwise distillation implementation with scalability features. It is validated across vision, masked language modeling, and causal language modeling workloads. The toolkit aims to close the gap between distillation research and available tooling.

entry.title: Polylogarithmic Regret via Certainty Equivalence in Degenerate LQR

author.name: Luca Vignola, Melanie Zeilinger, Bruce D. Lee

entry.summary: This theory paper proves that singular input penalties, as in minimum variance control, relax the identifiability conditions under which certainty-equivalence control achieves polylogarithmic regret in online LQR, expanding the class of systems where logarithmic regret is attainable with a short initial exploration phase.

entry.title: REEL: Brain-Guided Video Generation and Selection by Reranking Encoder Embeddings with Linear Decoding from fMRI data

author.name: Fabrizio Spera, Tommaso Boccato, Moein Khajehnejad, Nicola Toschi, Matteo Ferrante

entry.summary: REEL tackles video reconstruction from fMRI using a Bayesian-inspired proposal-and-rerank strategy: a linear semantic decoder proposes candidates, a pretrained video generator creates videos, and ridge-regressed neural encoding streams rerank them. Evaluated on CC2017 and the BOLD Moments Dataset, it addresses the temporal mismatch between fast video stimuli and slow BOLD dynamics. This advances visual brain decoding beyond static images.

entry.title: Unsupervised Multi-modal Medical Image Registration via Invertible Translation

author.name: Mengjie Guo, Jinming Duan

entry.summary: INNReg performs unsupervised registration of multi-modal medical images by first translating them to mono-modal counterparts with an invertible neural network, then registering the translated images. Invertibility helps ensure information preservation during translation, which is critical for image-guided therapies.

entry.title: Where Demand Meets Supply: Spatial Elastic Consensus for Low-Bandwidth Collaborative Perception

author.name: Linshan Yan

entry.summary: Proposes Spatial Elastic Consensus, a bandwidth-adaptive framework for collaborative 3D perception in connected vehicles that replaces sender-driven selection with a bilateral demand-supply consensus, avoiding wasted bandwidth on ego-visible targets and masked-token convolution artifacts that violate low-bandwidth constraints.

entry.title: SpatialCast: Reading the 3D World via Cast Shadows

author.name: Enhan Li, Jinghao Zhou, Jiaze Zhang, Hongyang Du

entry.summary: Introduces SpatialCast, a benchmark that uses cast shadows to probe whether multimodal LLMs connect physical scene conditions with visual observations, evaluating how object geometry, illumination, and viewpoint manifest in shadow appearance across three complementary task types. It targets a physical-reasoning gap not covered by existing spatial benchmarks.

entry.title: ConserveEdit: Source-Anchored Transactions for Drift-Bounded Iterative Image Editing

author.name: Shuyang Jiang, Fucheng Deng, Yuchuan Luo, Zhenyu Wu

entry.summary: ConserveEdit frames iterative instruction-driven image editing as transactions against a contract compiled from the source image, separating regions that may change from protected content with explicit tolerances. Edits from a frozen editor are committed only if they pass progress, drift, and quality checks, preventing unintended changes from accumulating across refinement steps.

entry.title: SlideJev: Order-Stable and Tissue-Grounded Jev Decisions for Whole-Slide Pathology

author.name: Lei Wu, Jiashuai Liu, Di Zhang, Chunze Yang, Jiusong Ge, Junbo Lu, Yongqi Liang, Wenjie Zhao, Ni Zhang, Chen Li, Zeyu Gao, Qidong Liu

entry.summary: SlideJev targets whole-slide visual question answering in pathology, where current VLMs are sensitive to candidate answer ordering and can reach answers through shortcuts bypassing tissue evidence. The framework separately verifies each candidate against the slide and grounds judgments in visual evidence by scoring candidates via support-versus-rejection log-likelihood differences.

entry.title: SpikWM: Efficient End-to-End Spiking World Modeling for Visual Planning

author.name: Shuhan Ye, Hongbin Yu, Chong Wang, Hui Lu, Jiaming He, Yi Yu, Jiangbo Qian, Xudong Jiang

entry.summary: SpikWM is an end-to-end spiking neural network world model built on a joint-embedding predictive architecture for goal-conditioned visual planning. It introduces Spiking Regional Encoding, Bi-Spike Action Encoding, and Causal Membrane Prediction to preserve motion cues and distinguish actions in a sparse-computation regime. This targets efficient planning with image observations and goals.

entry.title: CADENCE: Learning Acyclic Gaits for Model-Based Quadruped Locomotion

author.name: Owen Sullivan, Sourav Selvaraj, Mahdi Agheli

entry.summary: CADENCE is a reinforcement-learned step planner atop a convex MPC controller for quadrupeds that every 40 ms selects from at most 65 discrete options (no step or a single-leg step to a safe foothold) plus a swing time. With no gait schedule or gait reward, the policy spontaneously develops an acyclic gait while maintaining stability.

entry.title: The Power Constraint is Political

author.name: Christopher Dzierzanowski

entry.summary: Christopher Dzierzanowski argues that US power grid capacity is not a physical limit on AI progress, claiming the grid could support at least 100 GW of AI data centers by 2030 given existing capacity and planned additions, and that perceived constraints stem from regulatory malaise. The post further argues AI safety benefits from concentrating compute under a single US regulatory regime, since dispersed global compute makes international governance harder.

entry.title: WebAgents: Unbundling Agent Creation, Hosting, and Execution for an Agent-Native Web

author.name: Dario Fenoglio, Martin Gjoreski, Marc Langheinrich, Pradyumna Chari, Ramesh Raskar

entry.summary: WebAgents proposes a portable, signed agent package format (agent.pkg) carrying workflows, skills, schemas, and resource requirements, decoupled from execution environments via an agent-native browser/runtime that verifies packages and binds user-controlled resources at run time. This aims to enable an open Agentic Web where agent behavior moves across creators, hosts, and runtimes without transferring authority over user resources.

entry.title: PhysScope: Agentic Multimodal Physics Reasoning with Grounded Visual Memory

author.name: Haoyang Liu, Kecheng Liang, Xinyu Li, Weixing Chen, Yang Liu

entry.summary: PhysScope is an inference-time visual harness that helps vision-language models self-correct scope mismatches in physics reasoning, where constraints are applied outside the states or conditions in which they hold. It links physical scopes to visual observations, constructs derived views, checks agent-proposed revisions against sources, and invalidates dependent conclusions when revisions are accepted — all without weight updates. This addresses a specific and common failure mode in multimodal scientific reasoning.

entry.title: TUSI: A Citation-Grounded Graph-Based Benchmark

author.name: Marzieh Karimi, Mehran Safayani, Alireza Basiri

entry.summary: TUSI-Bench is a structured Persian legal benchmark for evaluating retrieval-augmented generation, built on a multi-layered legal knowledge framework of 7,261 legal articles with explicit linkage to authoritative legal documents. It addresses the lack of realistic, grounded benchmarks for legal RAG outside English.

entry.title: Learning Optimal Transport Plans Via Autoregressive Token Regression

author.name: Ivan Jaen Marquez, Sotirios Panagiotis Chytas, Vikas Singh

entry.summary: ToR-OT is a transformer model that learns to predict discrete optimal transport plans via autoregressive token regression, reframing OT as structured sequence generation rather than optimization. Optimal transport serves as an ideal testbed because ground-truth solutions exist and constraints are explicit. The work explores whether amortized models can internalize structured mathematical problem structure.

entry.title: How Web Research Agents Interpret User Priorities

author.name: Robin Sharma, Parisa Suchdev

entry.summary: Examines how two web research agents built on OpenAI and Anthropic models interpret stated user priorities across 36 runs comparing Microsoft and Alphabet, finding priorities are usually followed but interpreted with highly variable criteria. It highlights that a stated priority underdetermines the evaluation criteria an agent chooses.

entry.title: Physics-informed neural networks for spacecraft trajectory optimization with exact boundary conditions

author.name: Samuel Sch\"onherr, G\"unther Waxenegger-Wilfing, Sascha Ranftl

entry.summary: The paper applies neural networks to spacecraft trajectory optimization by modeling position as a function of time and minimizing thrust over network parameters, with exact boundary conditions enforced via a problem-specific transformation rather than weighted penalty losses. This removes the multi-objective weight-tuning sensitivity that plagues standard physics-informed neural network formulations for initial and terminal constraints. The approach is unsupervised and embeds physical laws directly in the objective.

entry.title: Better Calibrated, Better Planned: Uncertainty-Aware Multi-ASV Informative Path Planning for Oil Spill Monitoring

author.name: Alejandro Casado-P\'erez, Marija Popovi\'c, Daniel Guti\'errez-Reina, Sergio L. Toral., Samuel Yanes

entry.summary: This work studies how uncertainty calibration affects multi-vehicle informative path planning for oil spill monitoring, introducing Evidential Deep Learning as a calibrated uncertainty source replacing typical Gaussian Processes in a shared-map fleet coordination setting with autonomous surface vehicles.

entry.title: Sleep2Word: Peripheral-to-EEG Translation via Duration-Aware Wordization

author.name: Keondo Park, Arthur Delhaye, Younghoon Na, Hyun-Woo Shin, Hyung-Sin Kim

entry.summary: Introduces Sleep2Word, a framework translating respiration, ECG, or PPG signals into full-night EEG spectrograms using duration-aware physiological words: variable-duration chunks with content and duration jointly quantized into modality-specific wordbooks, decoded by a block-autoregressive translator. This extends EEG-informed sleep analysis to recordings made without EEG hardware. Potentially broadens access to sleep monitoring.

entry.title: Rethinking Perceptual Similarity for Remote Sensing: Multi-Layer Attention Scoring and Human Preference Benchmarking

author.name: Eli Underwood, Marc Bosch, Neil Joshi, Jeffrey Wen, Myron Brown

entry.summary: The authors develop a human-aligned perceptual quality metric for generated remote-sensing imagery, showing that natural-image perceptual metrics transfer poorly to this domain. Through controlled perturbation studies using layer-wise Aligned Attention Score responses in RemoteCLIP, they find different artifacts are best captured at different network depths, leading to the Remote Sensing Perceptual Distance metric. This matters for evaluating satellite imagery generation where subtle geospatial errors can be visually plausible but mission-critical.

entry.title: SRED: Sparse Regional Evidence Distillation Across Magnifications in Whole-Slide Imaging

author.name: Zhiyuan Yang, Jiahao Cheng, Vincent Quoc-Huy Trinh, Mahdi S. Hosseini

entry.summary: SRED transfers knowledge from high-magnification to low-magnification analysis in computational pathology by distilling sparse regional event occurrences rather than raw features, using a sparse autoencoder dictionary learned from teacher features. This avoids slide-level labels and encodes only interactions reachable at lower magnification.

entry.title: Fast Training-Free Low-Light Video Enhancement with a Frozen Image Diffusion Prior

author.name: Hon Ming Yam, Chun Pong Lau

entry.summary: Builds a causal, training-free low-light video enhancement pipeline on a frozen image diffusion prior, using temporal input fusion with motion compensation and late-start offset propagation so full sampling runs only on key frames. It dramatically accelerates the only prior training-free method (from over a minute per 256x256 frame) while retaining quality.

entry.title: GaussianMamba: Geometric and Relational State Space Scanning of 3D Gaussian Primitives

author.name: A. Enes Doruk, Ozgur Erkent

entry.summary: GaussianMamba is a dual-branch Mamba framework for 3D semantic occupancy prediction that treats 3D Gaussian primitives as sequences, using Gaussian-specific geometric and feature-semantic relationships to design complementary scanning strategies. This addresses the challenge that Gaussian primitives are irregular and unordered, making conventional sequence ordering inadequate.

entry.title: Refin3R: Geometry-Guided Refinement for Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Jongmin Lee, Jaeyeong Kim, Seungryong Kim

entry.summary: Refin3R refines feed-forward point-map predictions using Structure-from-Motion points, propagating SfM geometry over the image grid via a dual-branch architecture: a 2D branch extends SfM coverage with geometry-aware features while a 3D branch reasons over reconstructed geometry. This addresses cross-view inconsistency and fine-grained precision limits of single-pass 3D reconstruction models. It improves on methods that use geometric priors only as auxiliary inputs.

entry.title: EM-SDTrack: Efficient Multi-Scale Spike-driven Tracking for Event Cameras

author.name: Yimeng Shan, Haodi Wu, Wei Zheng, Xiaowei Ye, Shuai Wang, Yu Liang, Wei Hua, Chenxiao Dou, Malu Zhang

entry.summary: EM-SDTrack introduces Spike-driven Multi-Scale Interaction, enabling cross-scale feature interaction in a single spiking forward pass for event-camera object tracking, avoiding floating-point multiplication and repeated backbone computation. It targets multi-scale representation, previously missing in spike-driven trackers, for neuromorphic edge deployment.

entry.title: Sideslip-Conditioned Drift Trajectory Planning with Flow Matching and Control Barrier Functions

author.name: Seokjun Lee, Seung-Hyun Kong

entry.summary: Proposes the first generative drift trajectory planner explicitly conditioned on a requested peak sideslip angle, using conditional flow matching trained on demonstrated drift laps with hindsight-derived labels and reinforcement fine-tuning. A control barrier function correction enforces safety constraints on the generated trajectories.

entry.title: COSI: A Framework for Robustly Valid Inference

author.name: Arun K. Kuchibhotla, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, Larry Wasserman

entry.summary: COSI (COnfidence from Scale Invariance) constructs confidence sets for statistical functionals by batching data and retaining candidate parameter values for which batch estimates pass a scale-invariance test. Building on HulC, it achieves asymptotic validity under weaker assumptions than Wald or bootstrap procedures with often better small-sample coverage.

entry.title: How Much of SAR Vehicle Recognition Is the Vehicle? Background Shortcuts, Angle Gaps and Partial Libraries on MSTAR and ATRNet-STAR

author.name: Mousa Shaya

entry.summary: This analysis shows that near-perfect reported accuracy on SAR vehicle recognition benchmarks (MSTAR, ATRNet-STAR) relies heavily on background shortcuts: with the vehicle removed, accuracy far exceeds chance, and under scene-change splits background cues actually hurt performance. It reveals that models, including a SAR foundation model, lean on spurious context rather than the target signature.

entry.title: CorrectCast: Selective Multimodal Context for Scale-Aware Residual Correction in Precipitation Nowcasting

author.name: Henan Wang, Shengwu Xiong, Yifang Zhang, Pengfei Duan

entry.summary: CorrectCast is a decoupled residual-correction framework that refines outputs of frozen precipitation nowcasting backbones using a lightweight corrector conditioned on the base nowcast, historical QPE, and precipitable water vapor. This avoids costly backbone retraining and provides a unified correction interface across different nowcasting models.

entry.title: Symbolic Abstraction Refinement

author.name: Daniel Bryce (Smart Information Flow Technologies, LLC), Robert P. Goldman (Smart Information Flow Technologies, LLC), David J. Musliner (Smart Information Flow Technologies, LLC), Jeremy Gottlieb (Smart Information Flow Technologies, LLC), John Skovbekk (Smart Information Flow Technologies, LLC)

entry.summary: This paper addresses verification of probabilistic timed automata, where symbolic states pair discrete locations with clock-value regions but behavior can vary within a region. The authors refine the PRISM verifier's region-splitting approach, rebuilding transitions and propagating splits backward through the state graph to more precisely bound goal-reaching and hazard probabilities for autonomous system controllers.

entry.title: COTTI: Contrastive Training and Time-Aware Inference for Robust Industrial Recommendation under Promotional Drift

author.name: Maolei Huang, Jing Tian, Dexuan Duan, Fangfang Lin, Huawei Cao, Shuhan Song

entry.summary: COTTI is an industrial recommendation framework addressing promotional drift, combining cross-period contrastive alignment, active re-weighting of promotional examples, and adaptive boundary alignment for time-aware score adjustment. It separates historical representation learning from event-time adjustment, keeping predictors parametrically unchanged while correcting logits.

entry.title: EDA: Observe, Verify, and Assess for Evidence-Grounded Multimodal Depression Analysis

author.name: Changzeng Fu, Ming Shang, Xinyi Zhang, Jiadong Wang, Runhao Zeng, Shiqi Zhao

entry.summary: EDA is an evidence-grounded framework for multimodal depression assessment that localizes acoustic and visual cues into source-linked evidence records, verifies each record with frozen multimodal agents, and then performs reference-based behavioral assessment. This improves inspectability of which observations drive a mental-health assessment. It addresses a real trust and explainability gap in clinical multimodal AI.

entry.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Heat Pump and Underfloor Heating Control: An End-to-End Case Study

author.name: Antonio Manjavacas, David Su\'arez-Caro, Alejandro Campoy-Nieves, Guillermo Rey, Gonzalo Satr\'ustegui, Miguel Molina-Solana

entry.summary: An end-to-end case study applying deep reinforcement learning to control heat pumps coupled with underfloor heating, a challenging setting due to high thermal inertia and slow dynamics. The work covers simulation-based pilot studies, algorithm comparison, and real-world deployment in an occupied building, jointly optimizing energy use and thermal comfort. Its main value is demonstrating DRL control under genuine operating conditions, which remains rare.

entry.title: Can an LLM dream? Testing the overfitted brain hypothesis on an agent with text memory

author.name: Eric Zou

entry.summary: This paper tests Hoel's overfitted brain hypothesis — that dreams distort replayed experience to prevent overfitting — on an LLM agent (Claude Opus 5.5, an existing model) that stores learnings in a text memory rewritten nightly from conversation transcripts. Over ten simulated days built from LongMemEval, the authors corrupt 5-40 percent of transcript turns in structured ways before memory rewrites to emulate dream-like distortion. It is a creative crossover between neuroscience theory and LLM agent memory design.

entry.title: Stop Early, Stay Simple: Evidence Acquisition for Power System Fault and Attack Diagnosis

author.name: S M Zia Ur Rashid, Sazidul Islam Hira, Rupesh Sah, Suman Rath

entry.summary: ActiGrid is a benchmark framework for active evidence acquisition in cyber-physical power systems, pairing a missing-modality-tolerant classifier with a Double DQN that decides when to request additional telemetry sources or stop and diagnose. The paper critically evaluates when learned evidence-selection policies are worth their complexity against simpler baselines on public substation and attack benchmarks.

entry.title: Evaluating the Evaluation of Music Generation Models with Generative Psychometrics

author.name: Jo\~ao Carlos Santana Silveira, Caio Von Rondow Morais, Frederico Pedrosa, Lucas N. Ferreira

entry.summary: The authors map subjective evaluation methods in ISMIR music generation papers from 2020-2025, extracting 284 evaluation items and applying psychometric techniques such as Unique Variable Analysis and Bootstrap Exploratory Graph Analysis to assess their stability and latent structure. The work targets reproducibility problems in subjective evaluation of generative music models.

entry.title: A Temporal Algebraic Framework for Data Stream Evaluation Under Delayed Labels and Distribution Shifts

author.name: Ronaldo C. Prati, Elaine Ribeiro de Faria

entry.summary: The authors extend an algebraic evaluation framework that decomposes pooled (micro) and per-class (macro) metrics from a single confusion matrix to data streams, weighting counts over time with exponential fading or sliding windows. The framework treats delayed and selectively reported labels as an observation mask, enabling principled evaluation when class prevalence drifts and labels arrive late or are model-selected.

entry.title: From Imperfective Paradox to Moorean Absurdity: Single-Chain Reasoning Lock-In and Multi-Candidate Verbalization Across Aspectual and Pragmatic Ambiguity

author.name: An-Sheng Jhang

entry.summary: Four preregistered experiments on a quantized Qwen3-8B test whether single-chain reasoning locks in prematurely on linguistically ambiguous entailment and coherence judgments. Across 16,640 formal units, 15 of 16 hypothesis slots retained confirmatory status, with large differences between direct chain-of-thought and multi-candidate verbalization conditions. The work connects formal linguistics and pragmatics to LLM reasoning failure modes.

entry.title: FIRE-Drive: Feasibility-Informed Risk Evaluation for End-to-End Diffusion Planning

author.name: Qifeng Xie, Kai-Yuan Feng, Wenkang Wan, Yue Wu, Maoguo Gong, Kai Sheng

entry.summary: FIRE-Drive improves diffusion-based end-to-end autonomous driving through dynamic feasible anchor initialization and risk evaluation for mode selection among geometrically similar candidate trajectories. It addresses weakly constrained noisy initialization that produces infeasible proposals and the challenge of selecting safe modes. The framework targets safety-critical trajectory planning quality.

entry.title: LeViT-UNet++: Towards Balanced Fine-Grained Details and Context for Efficient Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Guoping Xu, Jinling Zhu, Liuyue Li

entry.summary: Proposes LeViT-UNet++, an efficient encoder-decoder segmentation architecture for clinical settings like surgical navigation and real-time image-guided intervention, balancing local detail preservation against global context modeling. It introduces a Haar wavelet multi-scale component to retain fine structure while keeping computation low. The work targets the persistent accuracy-efficiency trade-off in medical segmentation under constrained resources.

entry.title: Right Labels, Wrong Reasons: Signed Feature Attribution for Multi-Label Explainability

author.name: Kenton White

entry.summary: Proposes FLEX, a global surrogate explanation method that fits a single multi-label Fisher LDA over the full binary label matrix, producing signed feature attributions per label in one coherent coordinate system. It shows high-fidelity reproduction of black-box predictions across benchmarks and classifier families, with pooled covariance especially beneficial when labels are numerous and positive examples scarce. The work addresses explainability for multi-label classifiers specifically.

entry.title: PANO: Parallel Latent Space Neural Operator for Solving PDEs

author.name: Zijiang Yang, Xiaomeng Wu, Chen Kuang, Dongmei Fu

entry.summary: Proposes PANO, a Transformer-based neural operator for PDEs that aggregates observations through multiple parallel patterns rather than a single latent-token aggregation, formulating physical interactions as an additive combination of interaction types. This addresses the limitation that information not captured by a single aggregation pattern becomes invisible to the latent space. The design improves physical fidelity for large-observation scientific machine learning problems.

entry.title: A tiny object detection dataset for high-altitude open-water search and rescue

author.name: Hui Xu, Chenfei Hou, Henglai Wei, Hao Wang, Yidong Jin, Xiulin Niu, Haoyang Zhang, Hui Zhang, Tianshi Xu

entry.summary: Presents TinyWOD, a dataset of 11,359 manually annotated aerial images with 19,505 instances of lifebuoys imaged from 1.5-2.0 km altitude for open-water search and rescue. Existing datasets only cover low-altitude scenarios, so this fills a real gap for extreme small-object detection.

entry.title: BugGen 2.0: Rethinking the Roles of LLMs for Scalable RTL Bug Synthesis

author.name: Minh Luu, Michael Quinn, Aakash Tyagi, David Houngninou, Jiang Hu

entry.summary: Redesigns LLM-based RTL bug generation by assigning deterministic algorithms to structural analysis, target selection, and validation while the LLM handles only localized semantic rewriting, reducing inference cost and invalid mutations. It demonstrates the approach across OpenTitan IP blocks and FabScalar with three LLMs.

entry.title: DeltaHarness: Self-Evolving Harnesses for Resource-Adaptive Tool Execution

author.name: Lecheng Yan, Jianze Lin, Xicheng Han, Xiantao Xu, Wenxi Li, Chenyang Lyu

entry.summary: DeltaHarness is an execution-guided policy-search method that adapts agent execution harnesses based on cold-start runtime measurements, since task descriptions alone cannot reveal conditions that reverse the latency ordering of valid plans. Its QHI loop uses observed responses to update runtime dispatch, revise plans, and select experiments, with an independent confirmation panel controlling policy replacement. It reports a 30 percent reduction in complete-delivery latency on a video-editing task.

entry.title: Adaptive Memory for Online Reinforcement Learning under Sparse Model Changes

author.name: Sreejeet Maity, Sukanya Modak, Leonardo F. Toso

entry.summary: The paper studies discounted RL in non-stationary environments where the MDP changes between deployments, with at most an epsilon fraction of reward and transition entries changing per deployment. The proposed algorithm adaptively selects, per state-action pair, how much history to reuse, balancing the bias of pooling stale data against the variance of learning from scratch. This gives a principled middle ground for reuse in sparsely changing environments.

entry.title: Spatially local mini-batching for implicit neural representations

author.name: Minseok Choi, Swarup Dhar, Heejae Kwon, Kookjin Lee, Donsub Rim

entry.summary: The authors show that low-rank neural representations (LRNRs), INRs with weight matrices built from shared hypernetwork-emitted bases, can be trained with spatially local mini-batches rather than domain-wide batches. This enables training on individual cells of adaptive-mesh numerical solutions, attributing the capability to the structural shared-basis property of LRNRs.

entry.title: DDSL: Iterative Self-Labeling for Financial Market States

author.name: Xianbin Gu, Qingyue Zhu, Yuhong Geng

entry.summary: DDSL constructs financial market state labels iteratively by coupling a price- and grammar-guided Viterbi labeler with a Transformer classifier through model feedback, addressing the absence of ground truth for market states. It builds a nine-state representation encoding current and future trends with structured price emissions and temporal constraints. Experiments on SSE50, CSI300, CSI500, and NASDAQ100 show improved held-out performance over conventional labeling.

entry.title: Bias-Reduced and Parallel Heavy-Tailed Stochastic Convex Optimization in $\ell_p$ Geometries

author.name: Zhengyun Nie, Anant Shyam, Brian Bullins

entry.summary: This paper extends parallel stochastic convex optimization theory to l_p geometries (p greater than 2) under heavy-tailed noise, introducing a new class of optimal-distance-convergence algorithms built on bias-reduced estimation techniques, moving beyond the standard variance-bounded Euclidean setting.

entry.title: Sparse Integer Fourier Transform and Its Application In Machine Learning

author.name: Jinyang Li, Jie Chen

entry.summary: The paper proposes SIFT, a sparse integer reformulation of the Fast Fourier Transform that decomposes the Radix-n DFT matrix into four sparse integer matrices and approximates twiddle factors via optimization, leveraging sparsity and small-integer arithmetic for efficiency, with applications to machine learning feature extraction.

entry.title: Bandit Online Submodular Minimisation Using Zeroth-Order Oracles

author.name: Amir Ali Farzin, Philipp Braun, Iman Shames

entry.summary: Proposes the first bandit online submodular minimization method with guarantees for tracking a moving minimizer, rather than only static regret. The zeroth-order approach uses a two-point oracle on the Lovasz extension whose evaluations are playable subsets, with a shared random-threshold rounding scheme.

entry.title: PVTSizing 2.0: A Fast and Reliable Analog Circuit Sizing Operator for Agentic EDA Workflows

author.name: Zichen Kong, Minghuan Song, Xiyuan Tang, Ziming Wei, Yi Zhong, Yuan Wang

entry.summary: Presents a human-agent workflow for analog circuit sizing across process, voltage, and temperature corners, combining an independently usable numerical optimizer with an LLM-based agent for task execution and review. The optimizer uses loss-guided updates and critic-guided local refinement to handle cross-corner conflicts, with an optional LLM adviser supplying parameter relationships.

entry.title: From Constraints to Causality: Petri net Encodings for Explaining Binary Neural Network Inference

author.name: Alex Chan (Newcastle University), Mohamed Tarraf (Newcastle University), Alex Yakovlev (Newcastle University), Rishad Shafik (Newcastle University)

entry.summary: Provides a compositional translation from the inference semantics of a trained binary neural network to a 1-safe Petri net, giving a discrete-event, causal view of computation that complements monolithic SAT/SMT verification. Each computation step becomes an explicit traceable transition, aimed at safety-relevant autonomous-system components.

entry.title: Balancing Exploration and Exploitation in Constrained Combinatorial Optimization with U(1)-Symmetric Tensor Trains

author.name: Sergei Iudin, Mikhail Podobrii, Dmitry Zheltkov, Stanislav Moiseev

entry.summary: Develops a tensor-train-based framework for constrained combinatorial optimization built on U(1)-symmetric tensor networks, ensuring hard linear constraints are respected by construction so sampling never leaves the feasible set. The method adds an expressibility-enhancement mechanism and balances exploration and exploitation when feasible points are rare.

entry.title: Magflow: Differentiable Simulation of Industrial-Grade 6D Magnetic Levitation

author.name: Philipp Hartmann, Jannick Strangh\"oner, Klaus Neumann

entry.summary: Presents Magflow, a differentiable simulation of six-degree-of-freedom magnetic levitation that computes electromagnetic physics directly rather than relying on hand-crafted force approximations from hardware-software co-design. This relaxes the conservative workspace and mover-topology constraints of industrial systems while keeping control tractable at kilohertz rates. Relevant to frictionless transport and micrometer-scale positioning applications.

entry.title: Amortizing Tempered Sampling with Corrected Self-Training

author.name: Hoang-Viet Nguyen, Hai-Dang Dau, Alexandre H. Thi\'ery

entry.summary: Develops a corrected self-training scheme for learning neural samplers across sequences of tempered targets, using importance sampling and MCMC corrections stored in replay buffers. The proposed Sequential Score Sampler (SSS) trains a score-based diffusion proposal via regression on energy gradients, amortizing the cost of repeated sampling from unnormalized distributions. This is relevant to simulation-based inference and sampling from hard targets.

entry.title: Contract-Explicit Evaluation: From Auditing Learned Readers to Scoped Certificates

author.name: Hao Lu, Weixing Zhu, Ruiyang Li

entry.summary: Shows that document-level relation extraction rankings reverse across evaluation contracts (gold version, scoring function, threshold) and proposes a preregistered five-step contract-explicit evaluation protocol that scopes certifiable regions using Kendall rank-correlation decomposition. It demonstrates the approach with an audit of 44 training runs and distribution-free census certificates.

entry.title: ClearTalk: Data-Driven Mandarin Articulation Analysis and Personalized Communication Support for Children with Dysarthria

author.name: Ben Xiaolu Huang

entry.summary: Presents ClearTalk, a smartwatch-based system that converts Mandarin speech-recognition differences into interpretable articulatory profiles for children with dysarthria, aligning target and recognized utterances at the syllable level across seven articulatory positions. On 13 speakers from the Mandarin Dysarthria Speech Corpus, syllable accuracy correlated 0.908 with expert intelligibility, and selected targets achieved high improvement rates.

entry.title: SignAligner: Dual-Granularity Span Generation for Sign Language Alignment

author.name: Jongbhin Woo, Youngjoon Jang, Joon Son Chung

entry.summary: SignAligner is a prompt-conditioned visual-language span generator that predicts temporal start/end intervals in sign-language videos for both subtitle alignment and word-level sign spotting. It is trained jointly on both granularity levels and refined with overlap-based rewards, evaluated on the BBC-Oxford British Sign Language dataset. Joint multi-granularity training improves sign-language corpus annotation, which is a bottleneck for accessibility research.

entry.title: DEFTS: Data-Efficient, Training-Free Few-Shot Learning for CLIP in the Text Subspace

author.name: Yijin Zeng

entry.summary: DEFTS is a training-free few-shot classification method for CLIP that operates entirely in the text subspace, exploiting the observation that although raw text embeddings are suboptimal classifiers, the linear subspace they span is highly discriminative. It projects image embeddings into this subspace to reduce modality gap and improve few-shot accuracy without any training. This offers a simple, compute-free alternative to prompt-tuning approaches.

entry.title: RetiDual-Select: Reliability-Aware Specialist-Generalist Routing for Retinal OCT under Image-Quality Shift

author.name: Zihao Han, Philippe De Wilde

entry.summary: RetiDual-Select combines the retinal specialist RETFound with MedSigLIP's image encoder via calibrated product-of-experts fusion, adding a small routing gate, a validation-frozen harm guard, and a selective-review policy to safely adapt under image-quality shifts. At a clean 2% accepted-error target it achieves 94.3% coverage on Kermany-4 at 99.89% selective accuracy. The work addresses adaptive fusion's risk of overturning correct specialist decisions.

entry.title: FrameSeg3D: Learned Local Frames for Segmenting Small Parts on High-Resolution 3D Scans

author.name: Xinwen Zhang, Tongyan Wang, Huawei Lin

entry.summary: This paper addresses segmentation of tiny parts (like nails on hand scans or teeth on intraoral scans) in high-resolution 3D data, where parts occupy a small fraction of the scan and boundaries are subtle. FrameSeg3D introduces learned local frames to overcome the memory limitations of whole-scan processing and the coarseness of multi-view methods. It is relevant to dental and medical 3D scanning applications.

entry.title: SIDUMN: Self-Supervised Image Denoising Under Symmetric Multiplicative Noise

author.name: Nyan Htet Naing, Gyeongha Hwang

entry.summary: SIDUMN is a symmetric noisier framework for self-supervised denoising of multiplicative, signal-dependent noise, constructing complementary noisier images from antithetic synthetic noise factors and training the network to map between them. The paper derives the population target of the training loss analytically, showing it relates to the clean conditional mean.

entry.title: CutAgent: Creative-Gene-Driven Planning and Experience-Guided Self-Refinement for High-CTR E-commerce Advertising Video Creation

author.name: Xuyue Huang, Guanbo Huang, Jiasong Feng, Run Ling, Ao Ma, Xi Zhao, Yaoyu Li, Jie Gao, Ke Cao, Wei Feng, Zhanjie Zhang, Hao Wang, Jinghe Hu

entry.summary: Presents CutAgent, a dual-agent framework that treats advertising video creation as a Plan-Execute-Self-Evolve loop, using a structured creative gene to connect product understanding with video production and reusing past production failures for refinement. The system targets click-through-rate-oriented e-commerce video generation.

entry.title: Semantic-Guided Geometric Decoding for Token-Efficient Visual Grounding

author.name: Zhaojie Chen, Junyan Yang, Le Yang, Qi Dang, Yucheng Huang, Qianyi Che, Zhaoqiang Chen, Xinqi Zhu, Qiang Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces SemGeo, a visual grounding framework that represents each instance with a single grid token for coarse localization and uses a geometric decoder that reuses visual features and hidden states to recover box coordinates in parallel, avoiding costly autoregressive coordinate generation. A Gaussian-based objective jointly trains proposal generation and localization.

entry.title: SlopeGuard: Towards Generalizable AI-Generated Image Detection via Radial Spectral Slope Guidance

author.name: Cheng Fu, Yiheng Li, Yang Yang, Wenzheng Liu

entry.summary: SlopeGuard targets generalization in AI-generated image detection using Radial Spectral Slope, a compact descriptor of global spectral decay that captures transferable trends while suppressing generator-specific artifacts. The analysis shows slope differences are systematic but generator-dependent, so the method combines spectral slope with semantic representations.

entry.title: Propose & Verify: Fast Reflection Symmetry Detection via Harmonic Fields

author.name: Yishai Lavi, Shai Avidan

entry.summary: FAST is a training-free framework for detecting multiple reflection symmetries in 3D shapes that combines geometric pair voting with spectral computation, representing votes as a signal over plane orientations computed efficiently in the spherical-harmonic domain. Centroid constraints, consistency filtering, and independent witnesses suppress unreliable hypotheses, avoiding expensive voting over the full plane space.

entry.title: You Only Encode Once: Sub-Pixel-Shifted Frames for Arbitrary-Scale Remote Sensing Super-Resolution with 2D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Canjie Liu, Liuqian Wang, Qi Ming, Wei Lu, Xiaohan Hao, Yuefei Wu, Wentao Chao, Lei Shi

entry.summary: SPS-GS is an encode-once framework for arbitrary-scale super-resolution of remote sensing images that learns from sub-pixel-shifted multi-frame observations synthesized from single high-resolution images, avoiding real multi-frame training data. It uses Phase-Coherent Aliasing Demodulation and 2D Gaussian splatting to reduce data acquisition and compute costs. This addresses a practical bottleneck in remote sensing SR.

entry.title: When a Larger Guidance Scale Repairs Text-to-Video Failures and When It Does Not

author.name: Taewon Kang, Matthias Zwicker

entry.summary: This measurement study on Mochi characterizes when raising classifier-free guidance scale repairs text-to-video failures: it helps rare compositions, does not fix negations (where regeneration is better), and does nothing for late-occurring events. The authors propose a cheap prompt-based score called demand that predicts in advance which regime applies. This gives practitioners a principled alternative to blindly increasing guidance.

entry.title: EviSlide-MIL: Multi-Query Pooling and Shared Prediction for Class-Incremental Whole-Slide Image Classification

author.name: Zhouhan Qian, Sicheng Chen, Chad Wong, Tianyi Zhang, Enhui Chai, Zeyu Liu, Fei Xia

entry.summary: EviSlide-MIL tackles class-incremental learning in multiple-instance learning for whole-slide histopathology images, where adding new tumor subtypes risks catastrophic forgetting. It introduces multi-query pooling and shared prediction to retain knowledge of prior classes with limited historical data.

entry.title: A high-dimensional spatial-physical coupling operator for generalizable super-resolution of three-dimensional turbulent flows

author.name: Zengyuan Zuo, Junjun Jiang, Fei Mu, Xubo Wang, Xianming Liu

entry.summary: The paper proposes a neural operator for super-resolution of 3D turbulent flows that explicitly models nonlinear coupling between physical quantities like velocity and density, rather than treating them as independent channels. It aims for high-fidelity reconstruction under sparse, low-resolution data conditions.

entry.title: Haptic Probing for Subsurface-Aware Force Distribution on Layered Soft Tissue

author.name: Lei Shi, Xiaoyu Wang, Cheng Zhou, Yongjian Liu, Jing Wang, Dongsheng Zhang, Yonghui Zhu, Xiong Li

entry.summary: The paper proposes active haptic probing that discriminates muscle from bone-backed soft tissue before task force is applied, removing the lag in force-regulated contact control over layered tissue. A force- and tactile-driven distribution law then allocates contact forces based on the identified subsurface regime.

entry.title: Learning Accurate End-Effector Trajectory Tracking with Inertial Feedback for a Quadruped Manipulator

author.name: Dohyeon Kim, Seungyong Han, Yeongtae Jung

entry.summary: This work uses reinforcement learning with end-effector inertial feedback to achieve accurate trajectory tracking on quadruped manipulators, addressing actuator, contact, and geometric uncertainties that joint encoders cannot observe. It targets local high-accuracy manipulation while maintaining nominal body pose.

entry.title: Fly as Instructed: Refining World-Action Policies for UAV Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Zhexuan Zhou, Yanke Sun, Yuhan Zong, Youmin Gong, Jie Mei

entry.summary: Proposes a world-action learning framework for language-guided UAV navigation combining a language-conditioned action interface with post-training, recurrent instruction-consumption prediction for progress tracking and termination, and Gaussian-scene post-training for obstacle avoidance. It improves reliable instruction following and safe flight over existing world-action models.

entry.title: Satisfiability Modulo Theories for Robust Synthesis of Signal Temporal Logic Specifications

author.name: Philip Smith, Kevin Leahy

entry.summary: Introduces an SMT-based synthesis method for Signal Temporal Logic specifications, with encodings for STL constraints and discrete-time signals, to overcome the poor scaling of MILP-based sound and complete synthesis on long horizons and large environments. The approach scales better for long deployments and adapts more quickly to environmental changes.

entry.title: Epoch's newly Bayesian ECI is sensitive to how 100% scores are clipped

author.name: Tim H

entry.summary: Based on the title, this post critiques Epoch AI's newly Bayesianized version of the ECI benchmark aggregation metric, showing that results are sensitive to how perfect 100% task scores are clipped. This is a methodological critique relevant to how AI capability progress is quantified.

entry.title: Jensen Huang Really Liked Selling China Advanced AI Chips

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi's analysis of a major scandal in which Jensen Huang reportedly resigned following affairs, including with an alleged Chinese spy involved in chip smuggling, layered on top of a longer-running argument that Nvidia lobbied aggressively to sell advanced chips to China. The post contends this behavior compromised US national security and complicated sane AI policy.

entry.title: Why do AIFP forecasters disagree so much on the gap between SARs and TED-AIs?

author.name: Roman Ross

entry.summary: This post analyzes why AI Futures Project forecasters disagree on the interval between superhuman coding/research systems and transformative AI milestones, in light of a METR report showing Anthropic-internal progress rates running ahead of even bullish predictions like AI 2027. It examines how milestone definitions and takeoff modeling choices drive the disagreement.

entry.title: Fine-Grained Japanese Clinical Named Entity Recognition: A Controlled Comparison of BERT and Open-Weight Large Language Models

author.name: Feng Han, Ayako Yagahara, Kenji Hirata, Atsushi Yoshida, Kohsuke Kudo

entry.summary: A controlled comparison of fine-tuned BERT-CRF baselines against nine open-weight LLMs on fine-grained Japanese clinical NER over 113 entity categories in the iCorpus dataset, evaluating zero-shot prompting, JSON Schema constraints, and three-seed QLoRA fine-tuning under varying output-token limits. The study clarifies when generative LLMs match encoder baselines on non-English clinical extraction and how generation settings affect results.

entry.title: Synergizing Evidence Retrieval and Utilization for Self-Improving Multimodal Scientific Document Reasoning

author.name: Frank Nie, Ethan B. Liu, Yuan Zhu, Jindong Han

entry.summary: The paper presents an agentic Retriever-Perceiver-Reasoner framework for multimodal scientific document reasoning, where retrieval selects source-aligned evidence under a context budget, a perceiver builds a question-conditioned latent ontology of the evidence, and a reasoner combines this with the original query. It also couples evidence acquisition with utilization feedback for self-improvement. This targets a key error-attribution problem in document QA agents.
