entry.title: Agent Trajectories as Evidence for Software Quality Assurance

author.name: Jonathan Ullrich, Julien Siebert, Michael Kl\"as, Adam Trendowicz, Andreas Jedlitschka

entry.summary: This vision paper proposes analyzing observable agent trajectories, alongside specifications and AI-generated artifacts, as evidence for targeted quality assurance of autonomously developed software. The idea is to prioritize consequential agent decisions for scrutiny and investigate their contribution to software problems. Industrial experience motivates the approach, but the authors acknowledge trajectories alone cannot establish that decisions caused defects.

entry.title: Projected Penalty-Gradient Tracking for Communication-Efficient Byzantine-Resilient Federated Learning

author.name: Yanjie Dong

entry.summary: Proposes a framework where honest workers upload compressed residuals of penalty gradients and the server projects reconstructed states onto a known penalty-gradient ball, preserving Byzantine resilience guarantees that are otherwise lost under compression. The method accommodates arbitrary contractive compressors.

entry.title: How Many Persistent Features Does a Biometric Need? A Law Linking Equal Error Rate to Feature Count and Persistence

author.name: Oleg Komogortsev, Mehedi Hasan Raju

entry.summary: The paper derives a closed-form law relating a biometric system's equal error rate to the number of independent features and their test-retest persistence, via Fisher z-transformed cosine similarity of Gaussian features: EER equals a function of sqrt(N) times atanh(rho), with an effective count for correlated features. It extends earlier empirical linear observations into a principled derivation. This gives biometric designers an analytic tool for feature-budget and persistence trade-offs.

entry.title: ExplicitIR: Explicit Spatial Policy Fields for All-in-One Image Restoration

author.name: Dezhi Zhang, Shangrong Yang, Yudong Liang, Wenjian Wang

entry.summary: ExplicitIR represents restoration decisions as two explicit per-pixel fields — a Budget field controlling where and how strongly to update, and a Style field selecting restoration behavior — making the adaptation policy independently controllable rather than implicit in features. This enables spatially varying correction that avoids over-smoothing clean regions.

entry.title: PURE: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Multi-Granularity Multimodal Identity Matching

author.name: Hengyu You, Xintong Wang, Jin Cao, Liang Ding

entry.summary: PURE is a diagnostic benchmark for multi-granularity multimodal identity matching, testing whether models recognize that two records can match at a base level but differ at variant level (e.g., color or size). It contains 1,457 multiple-choice questions across 14 tasks covering Perception, Understanding, Reasoning, and Evidence-grounded Judgment in e-commerce.

entry.title: REVEAL: Reconstructing Video Amodal Content via Language and Flow Guidance

author.name: Minh Tran, Winston Bounsavy, Ngan Le

entry.summary: Presents REVEAL, a unified diffusion framework for video amodal completion that reconstructs heavily occluded content by combining motion (optical flow) and semantic priors, where a text query both drives open-vocabulary segmentation and guides reconstruction while improving temporal consistency.

entry.title: An Open-Source da Vinci X/Xi Instrument Module for Laparoscopic Surgery Research

author.name: Douglas McDonough, Justin Liao, Jiawei Ge, Antony Goldenberg, Yvonne Zhang, Mackenzie A Eagleson, Ravi Prakash, Axel Krieger, Chunwoo Kim

entry.summary: The paper presents an open-source hardware module enabling da Vinci X/Xi surgical instruments on UR5/UR5e robotic arms, including torque transmission and an electrosurgical interposer that accepts software commands, prioritizes surgeon pedals, and logs activation events. Bench and ex vivo tests demonstrate reliable energy activation control during tissue coagulation and cutting.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Tactile-based Shape Estimation of Deformable Linear Objects

author.name: Rotem Atari, Stav Ashur, Avishai Sintov

entry.summary: Investigates whether global shape of deformable linear objects (like cables) can be estimated purely from dense tactile sensing and proprioception, without vision. A physics-informed approach exploits tactile boundary conditions and contact gradients to resolve the high-dimensional DLO configuration, addressing occlusion and grasp-site ambiguity issues.

entry.title: PeriaTrace: Tooth-Level Grounding Diagnosis and Patient-Facing Explanations from Periapical Radiographs

author.name: Zhenhuan Zhou, Yuchen Zhang, Jingbo Zhu, Shiqing Ma, Yanlin Wu, Tao Li

entry.summary: PeriaTrace is a three-stage framework for periapical radiographs combining tooth-level diagnosis, visually grounded report generation, and patient-friendly explanations and care recommendations. It was evaluated on 12,877 radiographs plus two external clinical cohorts, achieving strong metrics such as 85.35% macro Dice and 94.37% F1 for joint localization and FDI-numbered diagnosis. The patient-facing explanation component addresses the communication gap in dental AI.

entry.title: Beyond Appearance: Where Forest Visual Place Recognition Actually Fails

author.name: Blake Matheson, Ben McShanag, Isabella Moffat, Michael Milford, Peyman Moghadam, Dana Kuli\'c, Somayeh Hussaini, Kavindie Katuwandeniya

entry.summary: This study analyzes where visual place recognition fails in forests, comparing an appearance-only baseline (MegaLoc) against temporal sequence matching, vision-language captions and reranking, scene graphs, and depth-derived structural representations on the WildCross benchmark. It examines same-direction revisits, extended routes, and reverse traversals to identify which contextual cues help and where each still breaks down. The paper provides a systematic diagnostic rather than a single new method.

entry.title: Breaking Visual Conventions: Spectrally Coupled Weight Perturbation for Creative Image Generation

author.name: Fu Feng, Ruoheng Zhou, Yucheng Xie, Xu Yang, Jing Wang, Xin Geng

entry.summary: CosPert is a training-free method for increasing creativity in text-to-image generation by perturbing attention projections in sensitivity-identified layers, coupling updates to singular-vector factors via a shared random transformation and its transpose. It targets diversity beyond familiar visual conventions without degrading image quality.

entry.title: A Visual Information Extraction System Using Multimodal Large Language Models for Scanned Cognitive and Behavioral Assessments

author.name: Enshuo Hsu, Linh Nguyen, Sunyang Fu, Heath Goodrum, Sandra Stansberry, Kirk Roberts, Hongfang Liu, Yen-Chi L. Le

entry.summary: A modular multimodal LLM system with human oversight extracts fields and scores from scanned paper-based cognitive assessments (MMSE, MoCA, Mini-Cog, NICHQ Vanderbilt), using a form classifier followed by schema-based score extraction and dual-model validation to trigger human review. It also qualitatively analyzes LLM use for hand-drawing analysis.

entry.title: ROSMonitoring in Action: Runtime Monitoring and Enforcement for ROS 2 Actions

author.name: Giacomo Paltrinieri (University of Modena, Reggio Emilia), Angelo Ferrando (University of Modena, Reggio Emilia)

entry.summary: The authors extend ROSMonitoring, a runtime verification framework for ROS 2, to handle actions, which involve a complex lifecycle of goal submission, feedback, status updates, results, and cancellation that prior versions could not observe. The system automatically instruments action communication endpoints and exposes action-level events to runtime-verification oracles for both monitoring and enforcement.

entry.title: DAQ: Decision-Aligned Post-Training Quantization for Spiking Transformers

author.name: Jialin Chen, Xiaochen Zhao, Aili Wang

entry.summary: This paper proposes DAQ, a post-training quantization method for spiking transformers that calibrates weight and membrane quantizers to preserve neuronal firing decisions relative to a floating-point reference. It analyzes error propagation across time steps in recurrent spiking neurons. This matters because spiking neural networks promise energy efficiency, and quantization is key to making them practical for deployment.

entry.title: Depth-Aware Activation Steering via Attention Residuals

author.name: Shilong Zhao (Independent Researcher)

entry.summary: The paper combines Attention Residuals (learnable cross-layer pathways) with Jacobian-lens concept readout into a depth-aware activation steering pipeline for LLMs, distributing persona vectors across layers instead of single-layer injection. On two small open models (Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3.5-0.8B), depth-aware distribution yields stronger internal alignment and behavioral shifts, with sign-specific effects. It is a training-free interpretability/control technique.

entry.title: Beyond Reconstruction: A Unified Framework for Trustworthy and Explainable EEG Artifact Removal Evaluation

author.name: Phat Lam, Hung Nguyen, Lam Pham, Huy Phan, Dat Tran, Ian McLoughlin, Roozbeh Razavi-Far, Hung Cao

entry.summary: TriX-EEG proposes a three-level evaluation framework for deep-learning EEG artifact removal covering signal validity, artifact removal faithfulness, and explanation quality, moving beyond dominant reconstruction metrics. This addresses the problem that reconstruction similarity does not establish whether models truly suppress artifacts or preserve neural activity.

entry.title: Benchmarking Deep Learning Models for Wheelchair Configuration Classification in Accessible Automated Vehicle Applications

author.name: Samir Ahmed, Shaaz Saleem, Devin Dhami, Wesley Maia, Angel Martinez-Sanchez, Parthib Roy, Jannatul Ferdous Srabonee, Ahmed Sabbir Arif, Ross Greer

entry.summary: This paper introduces the Wheelchair Configuration Image Dataset (WCID), a 467-image evaluation-only benchmark for classifying specific wheelchair configurations rather than merely detecting wheelchair presence. It targets accessibility in automated vehicle design, where wheelchairs vary widely in frame geometry, propulsion, and appearance and are often partially obscured by occupants or accessories. The work fills a gap in existing mobility-aid datasets and supports more tailored, independence-supporting autonomous vehicle interactions for wheelchair users.

entry.title: When does deep reinforcement learning pay off in HVAC supervisory control? Four small Modelica case studies trained directly on FMUs

author.name: Bingnan Zhao, Harshala Gammulle, Tharindu Fernando

entry.summary: The authors examine four reproducible HVAC control case studies modeled in Modelica and trained with soft actor-critic directly on FMUs, asking when DRL actually beats conventional control given known attainable optima. This addresses the common criticism that reported DRL gains in building control rest on weak baselines.

entry.title: Leveraging Segmentation Representations for Efficient Classification: A Self-Configuring Framework Based on nnU-Net

author.name: Renjun Cai, Antonio Javier Gallego, F\'elix Fuentes-Hurtado

entry.summary: This work extends the nnU-Net self-configuring workflow to jointly support segmentation and classification in 3D medical imaging by reusing segmentation encoder features and predicted probabilities in a lightweight classifier. Two information-sharing strategies are compared: a frozen-backbone branch augmented with region-of-interest information, and an adaptation branch partially fine-tuned with an auxiliary segmentation loss. It enables efficient image-level classification from segmentation models.

entry.title: DGF-Asym: Adaptive Peer Weighting for Collective Estimation under Noisy and Faulty Sensing

author.name: Mohammad Nomaan Husain, Tanja Katharina Kaiser

entry.summary: Extends the DeGroot-Friedkin social-opinion model to multi-robot collective estimation with asymmetric peer weighting based on retrospective predictive performance, allowing robots to balance personal observations against social information without prior noise statistics or fault models. Simulated collective navigation under noisy and faulty sensing shows more stable estimates than three baselines, at the cost of longer decision times. The approach keeps communication asynchronous, fitting real multi-robot deployments.

entry.title: DLS: Dual-Logic Graph Neural Networks with Chaos-Fuzzy Residuals for Robust Link Prediction

author.name: Mohammad Mehdi Keikha, Abolfazl Nadi

entry.summary: DLS targets over-smoothing in message-passing neural networks for link prediction, especially on heterophilous graphs, using a dual-logic framework with chaos-fuzzy residual connections to preserve high-frequency signals in deep layers. The work claims a controlled mechanism to break the over-smoothing barrier while maintaining structural learning. Applications span biological interaction discovery and recommender systems.

entry.title: Learned versus Kinematic Trajectory Prediction under Reduced Observation Frequency

author.name: Nukhbala Gadzhiev, Alexander Morochko

entry.summary: This study examines whether learned trajectory predictors retain their advantage over constant-velocity and constant-acceleration baselines when observation history frequency drops to the 1-10 Hz typical of V2X communication. Using Argoverse 2 with downsampled histories, it quantifies how learned predictors degrade under sparse observations.

entry.title: Efficient Self-Supervised Adaptation of 3D Abdominal Vision-Language Model for Institution-Specific HCC Classification via Full Fine-Tuning and PEFT

author.name: Febryan Putra Kartika, Cheng-Yu Ma, Ying-Jia Lin, Chi-Tung Cheng, Kuan-Fu Chen

entry.summary: Fine-tunes a pretrained 3D medical vision-language model for hepatocellular carcinoma classification on paired abdominal CT scans and radiology reports from an institution different from the pretraining source, comparing full fine-tuning and parameter-efficient fine-tuning. Both strategies achieve strong downstream performance under cross-institution domain shift.

entry.title: TabDAG: Structured Evolutionary Search for Tabular Feature Engineering

author.name: Anastasia Volkova (FusionBrain Lab), Andrey Kuznetsov (FusionBrain Lab), Ivan Oseledets (AXXX), Valentin Khrulkov (FusionBrain Lab, AXXX)

entry.summary: TabDAG combines evolutionary search with a DAG representation of feature-engineering programs for tabular prediction, where nodes are transformations and edges encode data dependencies. Mutations are schema-constrained structured edits validated before evaluation, preventing leakage and invalid programs. The framework supports compositional, multi-stage features including statistical encodings and neighborhood-based features.

entry.title: D\'ej\`a View: A Shared Working-Memory Model for Visual Tasks

author.name: Mranmay Shetty, Gabriel Kreiman

entry.summary: This paper presents a computational model of visual working memory that combines dynamic neural activity with temporary associations between image features. A single trained model handles five distinct tasks—such as remembering a sample amid distractors and recognizing whether an image is new—using explicit task cues, enabling the authors to study how delays, distraction, and image history affect memory performance. The work matters because it bridges cognitive neuroscience of working memory with machine learning, offering a flexible-memory architecture rather than task-specific models.

entry.title: Temporal Pseudo-RGB Encoding for Label-Free Detection of VEEV Infection in Human Brain Endothelial Cells

author.name: Zhengjie Zhu, Stephanie Valdez Trefry, Hao Lu, Abbas Alili, Yongxin Guo, Aarthi Narayanan, Metin Nafi Gurcan

entry.summary: The paper evaluates a simple temporal pseudo-RGB trick: stacking brightfield frames from three time offsets as RGB channels so that infection-driven morphological change becomes color, allowing standard ImageNet-pretrained CNNs to detect Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus infection label-free. A multi-task network predicts infection status and time post-infection in human brain microvascular endothelial cells. This has practical value for antiviral screening without specialized hardware.

entry.title: Text-Guided Modality Correction for Open-Vocabulary Object Detection

author.name: Yu Quan, Dong Zhang, Ping Gong, Peng Huang, JinHui Tang

entry.summary: TMCNet improves open-vocabulary object detection by injecting textual guidance into region feature extraction and strengthening cross-modal alignment, targeting detection of unseen categories and multi-scale objects. It addresses weaknesses in existing vision-language association strategies for OVD.

entry.title: Multispectral-Polarization-Infrared Multi-Aperture Camouflaged Vehicle Detection

author.name: Shu Wang, Xiong Lin, Yuan Song, Junjie Wang, Feng Huang, Wenxi Liu

entry.summary: This paper proposes a tri-modal (spectral, polarization, infrared) framework for detecting camouflaged vehicles, co-designed with a multi-aperture imaging setup and using consensus-guided decision-level fusion that tolerates imperfect registration. The authors also contribute a new tri-modal camouflaged vehicle dataset.

entry.title: EfficientVPR: Toward Efficient Visual Place Recognition via Scene-Aware Prompt Tuning and Adaptive Feature Enhancement

author.name: Wenjing Tang, Chuanguang Yang, Zhulin An, Libo Huang, Yongjun Xu

entry.summary: Presents EfficientVPR, a lightweight one-stage visual place recognition framework combining scene-aware visual prompt tuning of pretrained features with instance-dependent local feature enhancement, avoiding heavy reranking stages while handling extreme environmental variation.

entry.title: Classification of Tissues on MALDI-MSI Image Modality for Pancreatic Cancer Studies

author.name: Abubakar Qahir, Jenny Benois-Pineau, Victoria Bourgeais, Fabien Baldacci, Sandrine Dabernat, Nicolas Desbenoit, M\'elanie Moreau, Mehdi Boubaddi, Marion Marty

entry.summary: This work presents a fully automated pipeline converting raw MALDI mass spectrometry imaging data into deep-learning-ready patches for binary tumoral vs non-tumoral pancreatic tissue classification, matching the quality of reference interactive workflows. It enables end-to-end deep learning on MSI data for cancer research.

entry.title: Training-Free Building Change Detection with Example-Induced Discriminants

author.name: Zhi Lu, Bin Hong, Zhenming Peng

entry.summary: LIND is a training-free building change detection framework that converts regional feature contrasts from a few annotated examples into a reusable linear building classifier using a single frozen vision transformer. It unifies building recognition and temporal comparison in one feature space, sidestepping costly dense annotations. This makes change detection more economical across regions.

entry.title: DailyBrick: Language-Guided Synthesis of Brick Assembly Instructions

author.name: Hang Zhang, Qijian Tian, Yuan Xie, Xuhong Wang, Xin Tan

entry.summary: DailyBrick is a multi-stage agentic system that generates LEGO models with physically valid, brick-by-brick assembly instructions from language requests, using a staged LLM harness with roles and a versioned construction SDK rather than training a specialist LLM. It reframes long-context brick-connection generation as programmatic construction like a human builder.

entry.title: Diversity Preservation Recovers Transcription Factor Motifs Across Challenging Confounder Landscapes

author.name: Alejandro Medina, Mary Lauren Benton

entry.summary: The paper combines an evolvable-gate motif genotype with MAP-Elites archives organized by descriptor pairs to improve transcription factor motif discovery in DNA sequences, validating against the HOCOMOCO database. On liver ChIP-seq datasets, diversity preservation via MAP-Elites recovers target motifs where a standard survivor-selection baseline collapses onto confounding motifs.

entry.title: The Multivariate Feedback Particle Filter for State-dependent Multiplicative Noises and Its Application to Attitude and Pose Estimations

author.name: Jingyao You, Xue Luo

entry.summary: The paper develops FPF-DM, a decomposition scheme for feedback particle filters handling state-dependent multiplicative measurement noise, extending prior polynomial-measurement techniques via measure transformation and importance reweighting. Applications include spacecraft attitude determination and robotic pose estimation.

entry.title: Levio: Smart Actuated Back-Exoskeleton via Retrofit of a Commercial Passive Device

author.name: Ionnais Kyriazis, Mohamed Irfan Refai, Herman van der Kooij

entry.summary: Levio is an accelerated design pipeline retrofitting a commercial passive back exoskeleton (Laevo Flex) with off-the-shelf actuation and sensing to enable pose-specific assistance. A nine-participant stoop-lifting study compares the original passive device with the retrofitted actuated system in transparent and assisted modes.

entry.title: BehaVerify: A Formal Verification Tool for Behavior Trees

author.name: Serena S. Serbinowska (Vanderbilt University), Ben Wooding (Vanderbilt University), Diego Manzanas Lopez (Vanderbilt University), Luke Nam (Vanderbilt University), Anne M. Tumlin (Vanderbilt University), Nicholas K. Potteiger (Vanderbilt University), Hongchao Zhang (Vanderbilt University), Taylor T. Johnson (Vanderbilt University)

entry.summary: Presents BehaVerify, a toolbox for formally verifying behavior trees and neuro-symbolic behavior trees via a DSL with formal semantics, LTL/CTL specification support, and efficient nuXmv encoding via a fastforwarding technique. It can also generate Python and Haskell implementations, with PyTrees integration for deployment.

entry.title: Almost-orthogonal directions can look circular in PCA plots

author.name: Linda Linsefors

entry.summary: A short technical note with an interactive widget demonstrating that vectors which are nearly orthogonal but carry a small circular correlation will appear circular when projected onto the first two principal components. The author warns mechanistic interpretability researchers that apparent circular features in PCA visualizations may be artifacts.

entry.title: The Impact of Scenario Representation in Scenario-based Optimization Certification

author.name: Stephen Crawford, Nora Ayanian

entry.summary: Analyzes how the representation of sampled scenarios affects scenario-based optimization certification, showing that lossless regrouping can distort support-subsample certificates by a derived factor k^2(1-epsilon)^(k-1) and even reverse accept/reject decisions. The paper applies Wait-and-Judge theory to coordinatewise scenario envelopes and provides conditions for acceptance dominance under coarsening.

entry.title: Residual-Guided Lightweight Reinforcement Learning for Risk-Aware Trajectory Selection with a Frozen World Model

author.name: Jiaqi Wu, Yongqi Dong, Yijie Zhong, Maple Shao, Yide Tao, Linsen Cai, Weize Cai, Hai L. Vu, Alvaro Garcia Hernandez

entry.summary: This paper proposes an RL framework for automated-driving trajectory selection that uses PPO to fine-tune a joint policy over candidate selection and bounded trajectory residuals, with a frozen world model supplying future scene predictions and a context-conditioned ranking network learning candidate preferences from local perturbation feedback. The design keeps the learned selector lightweight atop a fixed prediction stack. This targets safe, scene-aware motion planning.

entry.title: Evaluating Semantic Insensitivity in Financial Sentiment Analysis: Implications for Sustainable Financial Decision-Making

author.name: Gabriela Cioboata, Teodor-Stefan Bildea

entry.summary: The paper introduces Agent-driven Semantic Inversion (ASI), an adversarial attack framework targeting financial sentiment models like FinBERT through LLM-powered multi-agent pipelines that apply targeted lexical substitutions to financial news sentences. Despite high benchmark accuracy, the models prove vulnerable to subtle semantic manipulation, with implications for algorithmic trading and risk assessment integrity. It highlights robustness gaps in a widely deployed specialized model class.

entry.title: Coordination of Heterogeneous Teams with Uncertain Task Requirements

author.name: Jongann Lee, Melkior Ornik

entry.summary: The paper introduces a hierarchical planner for heterogeneous multi-agent teams facing tasks with unknown requirements, using a graph neural network policy over a CAAT graph representation that captures agents, tasks, capabilities, and actions. The planner jointly coordinates task discovery, execution, and staging, with shortest-path planning for action locations.

entry.title: Semantic Communication via Analog RF Computing: When the Radio Computes the Meaning

author.name: Christo Kurisummoottil Thomas

entry.summary: This work proposes executing the semantic encoder of a semantic communication system inside the client's RF receiver front end using analog computing, with the base station broadcasting encoder weights as RF waveforms and the passive mixer computing latents at ultra-low energy. It provides a unified mathematical treatment of analog computing noise and channel noise affecting the transmitted latents.

entry.title: EgoHandWAM: Probing the Role of Hand Motion in Egocentric World Action Modeling

author.name: Kailin Wang, Haoxiang Jie, Yaoyuan Yan, Zhiyou Heng, Zhaosong Li

entry.summary: EgoHandWAM forecasts 3D wrist and fingertip trajectories and a future visual feature from the current image and recent hand states, trained on 751,065 EgoDex windows with a frozen DINOv2 encoder. The analysis finds hand history modestly improves both trajectory and future visual forecasting, with shuffled histories erasing the gain, clarifying how much hand motion informs egocentric prediction.

entry.title: PCGRL for Complex Platformers: Synthesizing Playable and Diverse Levels via Inflated Envelopes and Forward Curricula

author.name: Di Wu

entry.summary: This paper presents a physics-aware, curriculum-guided procedural content generation via RL framework for platformer levels, using an Inflated Volume Envelope representation and forward curricula to overcome exploration bottlenecks on long-sequence generation. The approach maintains level solvability under rigid-body kinematic constraints on large canvases. It advances automated game level generation beyond prior PCGRL limits.

entry.title: Do LLMs Understand Network Traces? A Comparative Study of Reasoning over Raw and Filtered Traffic Data

author.name: Irene Gos\'alvez-White, Roberto Mag\'an-Carri\'on, Carlota de la Vega-Soriano, Pedro Garc\'ia-Teodoro

entry.summary: Presents a reproducible question-answering-based evaluation of whether LLMs can interpret network packet captures, testing packet-level field extraction and flow-level sequence reconstruction against human-generated ground truth on real benign traffic from CICIDS2017. It compares performance on raw versus filtered traffic data across multiple models. The study clarifies where LLMs can and cannot substitute for expert network analysis.

entry.title: AlignedHPO: Efficient Surrogate-Guided Loss Hyperparameter Optimization

author.name: Ivan Karpukhin, Andrey Savchenko

entry.summary: Proposes AlignedHPO, a framework for tuning differentiable loss hyperparameters (weights, scales, margins) via gradient alignment against surrogate validation objectives, using Jacobian-vector products to cut hypergradient cost and memory. Normalized alignment and gradient smoothing handle gradient magnitude ambiguity and stochastic instability. Experiments with generalized Focal Loss and ArcFace demonstrate effective automated tuning.

entry.title: CULypso: A Clustered Federated Unlearning paradigm for Vehicular Ad-Hoc Networks

author.name: Eleftheria Chini, George Margaritis, Dimitrios Katsaros

entry.summary: Proposes CULypso, an approximate, surgical, hierarchical federated unlearning method for vehicular ad-hoc networks that leverages topology and mobility to reduce communication, resource, and time costs when erasing a client's influence on the global model, supporting data-erasure rights mandated by regulation. It argues hierarchical unlearning fits the edge, highly mobile, time-sensitive VANET setting. The problem of unlearning in such dynamic edge networks is largely unexplored.

entry.title: ReTouchGS: Ultralight Render-free Aesthetic Color Enhancement and Transfer for 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Chuanzhi Xu, Boyu Wei, Chengkun Yue, Xuanhua Yin, Yiyang Li, Haodong Chen, Qiang Qu, Weidong Cai

entry.summary: Presents ReTouchGS, the first reference-free aesthetic color enhancement framework for pretrained 3D Gaussian Splatting models, predicting a scene-level color lookup table from the model and camera parameters. It also supports reference-guided color transfer by fitting a LUT from a single example.

entry.title: FACE: Flow-Guided Angular Channel Estimation Framework for mmWave MIMO Systems

author.name: Samitha Gunarathne, Eslam Eldeeb, Nurul Huda Mahmood, Matti Latva-aho

entry.summary: FACE applies flow matching, a generative modeling paradigm that learns transport dynamics between probability distributions, to channel state information estimation in millimeter-wave MIMO systems. It exploits angular-domain sparsity of mmWave channels and uses a learned flow model as a generative channel prior to overcome high dimensionality, limited pilots, and noise. Numerical results show consistently higher estimation accuracy than baselines.

entry.title: Urban Representation Learning for Identifying Potential Disparities in Crime Reporting

author.name: Jorge Valverde-Rebaza, Carlos Paez De La Cruz, Pedro P\'erez-Collado, Daniel S\'anchez-Cata\~no, Eashley Mart\'inez-Vergara

entry.summary: The paper proposes a self-supervised urban representation learning framework that identifies unusual crime reporting patterns by comparing each region's hourly, weekly, and static reporting profiles with those of representation-similar peers. Neighbor Profile Divergence quantifies disagreement between a region and its peers in a unified latent space built purely from georeferenced crime records. The goal is to surface potential under- or over-reporting disparities in open crime data rather than treat reported incidents as ground truth.

entry.title: A Neural Envelope Method for Rapid Gradient-based Optimum Takeoff Trajectory Design

author.name: Samuel Sisk, Xiaosong Du

entry.summary: For urban air mobility aircraft design, this paper couples physics-constrained GANs with a neural envelope method to convexify multimodal multidisciplinary design spaces, enabling fast gradient-based optimization of takeoff trajectories while guarding against infeasible designs from over-relaxed convexification.

entry.title: From syllable representation via gesture generation to articulation: A spiking neural model

author.name: Bernd J. Kr\"oger

entry.summary: Presents a spiking neural sensorimotor model of speech production within the Neural Engineering Framework and Semantic Pointer Architecture, using neural oscillators to coordinate articulatory gestures across syllables. The model maps phonological representations to vocal-tract movement trajectories via phase-dependent gesture commands and ramp integrators.

entry.title: Where Should the Lamp Go? Ambient-Aware Lamp Placement for Portraits

author.name: Yuyan Chen

entry.summary: LightMatch is a preference-grounded inverse lighting framework that answers where to place a light before capturing a portrait, rather than relighting after the fact. It learns a Bradley-Terry quality model from pairwise human judgments, regresses spherical-harmonic lighting from frozen self-supervised features, and solves placement via spherical-harmonic linear decomposition while disentangling the controllable light from ambient illumination. It addresses an underexplored pre-capture lighting guidance problem.

entry.title: Diagnosing and Correcting Skin-Tone Color Casts in Ultra-Lightweight Photo Retouching Networks

author.name: Choulhyouc Lee

entry.summary: The paper diagnoses a case where an ultra-lightweight retouching network renders skin greener than the original, showing that paired-data-free synthetic self-supervision silently produces this color cast while whole-frame PSNR/SSIM remain unchanged. It demonstrates the failure in 52 of 70 portraits under a white-balance-free protocol and proposes corrections. The work highlights a subtle fairness-adjacent failure mode that standard metrics miss.

entry.title: DAP-MR: Degradation-Aware Prompt-Magnitude Routing for Real-World Ultrasound Super-Resolution

author.name: Ngoc-Hoang-Lam Le, Thi-An Le, Dinh-Hung Le, Manh-Hung Nguyen, Kai-Lung Hua, Ching-Chun Huang

entry.summary: DAP-MR improves real-world ultrasound super-resolution by replacing unreliable semantic text prompts with dedicated degradation-type prompts and routing on degradation magnitude separately, avoiding entanglement of degradation type and severity in a single prompt. This adapts natural-image super-resolution models to medical ultrasound.

entry.title: Strong Fused Performance Can Mask Branch Collapse in a Dual-View Heart-Sound Classifier: A Three-Part Diagnostic Protocol

author.name: Safayet Khan, Hasan Zohirul Islam, Md. Tauhid Bin Iqbal

entry.summary: Demonstrates that in a dual-view heart-sound fusion model (spectrogram transformer plus waveform CNN), strong fused accuracy can conceal complete branch collapse where one branch contributes nothing. The paper introduces a three-part diagnostic protocol - deletion impact, linear probe comparison, and solo training - to detect such silent failures.

entry.title: OVET-Consensus: Rank-Preserving Counterfactual Event Verification for Video Moment Grounding

author.name: Alibay Osmanli, Shaogang Gong

entry.summary: Studies the scorer bottleneck in video moment retrieval on QVHighlights, showing large headroom between the deployed temporal expert (64.71 R1@0.5) and diagnostic oracles, and introduces OVET-Consensus, a rank-preserving counterfactual verification layer that allows only calibrated high-confidence rank-1 overrides.

entry.title: Transfer Once, Ask Locally: Compact Audio-Visual Memory for On-Device Question Answering

author.name: Qitong Wang, Jihui Jin, Divya Kothandaraman, Vishnu Raj, Christopher Rasmussen

entry.summary: This work proposes a training-free, query-agnostic token pruning framework for on-device audio-visual question answering: video spatio-temporal blocks and audio windows are valued via Monte Carlo Shapley estimation and selected under an embedding-coverage objective to build a compact reusable memory before transmission. This balances speed, memory, privacy, and communication in a split server-device architecture. It reduces costly transfer of full multimodal representations.

entry.title: The shape of individual differences in judgment: shared axes, personal weights, and when their spread crosses the consensus

author.name: Hiroshi Higashi

entry.summary: This study models how people differ in judging faces, artworks, photos, and jokes by comparing nested generative models of individual differences, such as reweighting shared dimensions versus stimulus-specific offsets, across ten public datasets with about 20,000 raters. It finds reweighting suffices for faces, while artworks show weight spread along an abstract-figurative axis, recovering a person's judgment space from 10-20 judgments.

entry.title: ASTRA: ASV Simulator for Transferable Realistic Autonomy

author.name: Tsimafei Lazouski, Cody Sheltraw, Alan Papalia, Maani Ghaffari

entry.summary: ASTRA is an open simulation framework for marine autonomous surface vehicles built in NVIDIA Isaac Sim, combining Fossen-style marine dynamics with buoyancy modeling, photorealistic perception, programmable wave disturbances, and ROS 2 interfaces. It addresses the cost and irreproducibility of field testing for maritime autonomy.

entry.title: Pressure Drop: Gravity Vector Estimation from a Distributed Barometric Pressure Sensor Array

author.name: William Dubois, Nicolas Lauzon, Johann Laconte, Fran\c{c}ois Pomerleau

entry.summary: Proposes directly observing the gravity vector direction using altimeter (barometric pressure) measurements from a distributed sensor array, with theoretical noise analysis and extensive experimental validation. The system achieves median tilt error of 0.87 degrees in semi-static scenarios, offering a direct alternative to IMU-based indirect gravity estimation for SLAM.

entry.title: TRAIL-IRL: Crossed Reward-Temperature Mixtures for Unlabeled Trajectory Clustering

author.name: Yichen Zhu, Guanhua Fang, Ming Zheng

entry.summary: TRAIL-IRL clusters unlabeled trajectories using a crossed mixture of rewards (preferences) and temperatures (action randomness), allowing action regularity to vary within preference groups. It establishes identifiability conditions under which the distribution of long trajectories determines rewards, temperatures, and mixture weights, addressing confounding in multi-reward IRL.

entry.title: The AI consciousness debate is a red herring

author.name: kromem

entry.summary: kromem argues that the contested hard problem of whether transformers possess consciousness distracts from the tractable and largely settled question of whether transformers simulate human-like consciousness, which the author believes is now yes. The post contends that denying or staying agnostic about simulated consciousness leads to poor decisions, such as dismissing model well-being considerations, and draws an analogy to Searle's Chinese room.

entry.title: RagHarnessDebugger: Jev-Guided Agentic RAG in Contract Inference Repair Auditing

author.name: Moriya Dechtiar, Daniel Martin Katz, Michael J. Bommarito II, Hongming Wang, Sylvain Jaume

entry.summary: RagHarnessDebugger is a framework that records every repair decision made by an agentic RAG system in contract inference tasks and audits those records to verify trace integrity, validation applicability, and what answers the acceptance rule can reach. Tested on ContractNLI non-disclosure agreements, it addresses the problem that accuracy metrics alone cannot reveal whether self-repair mechanisms are functioning. This supports auditability of agentic RAG in legal AI.

entry.title: SandBAR: A Band-Asymmetric Architecture for Underwater Image Restoration with Removable Frequency Scaffolding

author.name: Yanzi Liu, Haoran Hou, Jiachi Tong, Shen Chen, Shuang Chen

entry.summary: SandBAR is a unified architecture for underwater image restoration organized around frequency band asymmetry — global channel-dependent color distortions versus local high-frequency detail loss — with a band-asymmetric sandwich block and removable frequency scaffolding. It treats frequency processing as a structural principle across blocks, encoders, and objectives.

entry.title: OmniTongue: A Comprehensive MLLM Benchmark for Automated Tongue Diagnosis in Traditional Chinese Medicine

author.name: Liuyi Xu, Yun Guo, Shusheng Li, Xuewen Zhang, Yining Qian, An-Yang Lu

entry.summary: Introduces OmniTongue, the first comprehensive fine-grained VQA benchmark for Traditional Chinese Medicine tongue diagnosis, with 1,351 expert-validated images and 21,616 instruction pairs covering global and local perception. It enables systematic evaluation of MLLM capabilities in a previously unevaluated clinical domain.

entry.title: Fold Weighting for Cross-Validation Under Continuous Distributional Drift

author.name: Yegor Baranovski

entry.summary: Models distributional drift via a Holder condition in total variation distance and derives finite-sample bounds on excess deployment risk for configurations selected by sliding-window cross-validation. It shows fold weighting toward deployment shrinks drift terms while noise grows with weight concentration, and proposes minimizing the resulting bound over weights.

entry.title: Learning Regions of Attraction for Transverse Feedback Linearization under Controller Singularities

author.name: Abdullah Waqar Malik, Hamza Tariq, Adeel Akhtar

entry.summary: The authors study transverse feedback linearization (TFL) for path following in robotic systems, where the controller is undefined on a singular set such as zero speed or zero thrust. They prove the constrained region of attraction is the largest forward invariant subset of the admissible set, and decompose the state-constrained Zubov value function into an analytic quadratic cost-to-go plus a safety value function that is learned via fitted value iteration, enabling safe activation of the controller.

entry.title: Pluggable Subband-Decoupled Fusion and Unlabeled Capture Prototype Calibration: Bridging High-SNR Null-Subcarrier Regrowth and Low-SNR Coherent Preambles for Cross-Domain IoT RF Fingerprinting

author.name: Fengchong Yao, Jianbing Li, Qing Liu, Kefeng Song, Haitao Li, Song Wang, Kunpeng Wang

entry.summary: This paper proposes the first RF fingerprint identification framework for cross-domain IoT authentication that dynamically modulates between active in-band waveforms and passive null-subcarrier features depending on SNR, addressing an SNR crossover where each feature type fails. It reports avoiding up to 44.7 percentage points of accuracy loss from static fusion. This is relevant to zero-overhead physical-layer security for resource-constrained wireless devices.

entry.title: Marimba: A System One Model for Speech

author.name: Solano Amadori

entry.summary: Marimba is a lightweight interface for typed speech decisions — term presence, turn completion, and language identification — built on frozen Qwen3-ASR 0.6B features, with zero-shot transcript scoring for lexical questions and a question-conditioned head plus layer-18 readout for non-lexical ones. It reports solid metrics on private conversational and public read-speech sets, including strong PII detection F1. The work targets fast, efficient speech frontends for interactive applications.

entry.title: From Top to Bottom: Quark Mass Hierarchies in Heterotic String Theory

author.name: Yuri Chervonyi, Fabian Ruehle, Nenad Tomasev

entry.summary: The authors study whether Standard Model quark mass hierarchies spanning five orders of magnitude can arise at tree level in smooth heterotic Calabi-Yau compactifications, computing Yukawa couplings from superpotential integrals and matter-field Kahler metrics. They identify new tree-level mechanisms within a computationally controlled supergravity regime, continuing a research line combining string theory with numerical and AI-assisted methods.

entry.title: Modeling Document and Section Hierarchies in Embedding Space

author.name: Kriste Krstovski, Sharyn O'Halloran, Kshitij Chandna

entry.summary: This paper introduces the Hierarchical Embedded Topic Model (hETM), which couples document-level and section-level topic distributions through a hierarchical prior in embedding space, with an amortized variational inference scheme. It targets collections like legal documents and reports whose internal section structure is ignored by single-distribution topic models.

entry.title: An AI-Driven Assistant for Human-Centric Building Digital Twin Systems: Design, Implementation, and Comparative User Evaluation

author.name: Leonardo Messi, Erika Anneli P\"arn, Juan Diego Casta\~no Molina, Oleksandr Anyshchenko, Dijar Selami, Peihang Luo, Borja Garc\'ia de Soto

entry.summary: The paper describes a conversational AI assistant integrated into a human-centric building digital twin for indoor environmental quality monitoring, with adaptive information presentation and auto-suggest, deployed at NYU Abu Dhabi. A controlled two-arm between-subjects quasi-experimental study evaluates the prototype. It aims to make building operations data accessible to non-technical stakeholders rather than only specialists.

entry.title: Stress Testing a Multimodal Large Language Model Grading Assistant on Kinematics Graph Reading

author.name: Ons Zammel, Carlos Soares, Fl\'avia Carvalhido, Gerd Kortemeyer

entry.summary: An exploratory study stress-testing MLLM-based grading of physics kinematics graph responses using synthetic distortions and progressive transformations of reference graphs. Some configurations correctly distinguish instantaneous zero velocity from rest, yet a severely distorted velocity-time graph received full credit despite disconnected traces and unclear references, while other submissions lost credit under identical conditions. The findings raise reliability concerns for automated MLLM grading in education.

entry.title: Video recordings and play behaviour annotations of group-housed dairy calves on two Dutch farms

author.name: Haiyu Yang, Heidi Lesscher, Enhong Liu, Miel Hostens

entry.summary: This dataset paper releases 651 hours of video of group-housed dairy calves across two Dutch farms, with 104 hours coded using an 18-item play-focused ethogram in professional observation software, plus 1.1 million decoded frames from annotated segments. It addresses the scarcity of open video with individual-level welfare behavior annotations.

entry.title: Temporal Diffusion Models for Joint Signal-Channel Estimation under Gaussian and $\alpha$-Stable MIMO Channels

author.name: Rawad Kansoh, Bahaa Ammoury, Charbel Hannoun, Jihad Fahs, Ibrahim Abou-Faycal

entry.summary: Studies diffusion-based reconstruction under Gaussian and symmetric alpha-stable fading MIMO channels, extending score-based diffusion beyond Gaussian assumptions to heavy-tailed noise. Two variants are explored: pilot-based channel-only estimation and joint image-channel recovery, with reverse-diffusion guidance refined using temporal channel dependence.

entry.title: An inexact stochastic variance-reduced gradient method for constrained convex finite-sum optimization

author.name: Zhaosong Lu, Yifeng Xiao

entry.summary: Studies constrained convex finite-sum optimization with hard constraints, targeting epsilon-surely-feasible stochastic-optimal solutions where constraint violation is deterministically bounded. The paper improves on the first-order oracle complexity gap left by a recent stochastic variance-reduced penalty method. A technical optimization theory contribution.

entry.title: TextSphere: Efficient Text-to-Image Generation via Shared Hyperspherical Alignment and Uniformity

author.name: Yixia Zhang, Girish A. Koushik, Xilu Wang, Wenwu Wang

entry.summary: TextSphere extends the efficient Sphere Encoder to free-form text-to-image generation by injecting pretrained CLIP text embeddings through adaptive layer normalization while preserving the hyperspherical alignment and uniformity properties. It targets few-step generation, avoiding the multi-step cost of diffusion. The work contributes to the line of research on fast, non-diffusion generative models.

entry.title: Joint-ID: Transformer-based Joint Image Enhancement and Depth Estimation for Underwater Environments

author.name: Geonmo Yang, Gilhwan Kang, Juhui Lee, Younggun Cho

entry.summary: Joint-ID jointly performs underwater image enhancement and depth estimation with a transformer network trained end-to-end with a multi-modal objective covering invalid depth, sharpness, color, and texture degradation. The joint formulation lets the two tasks reinforce each other from raw underwater images.

entry.title: Reliability-Driven Feature Correction for Hyperspectral and LiDAR Classification

author.name: Lianming Zhang, Xiaolu Wang, Qiya Song, Jinyang Liu, Renwei Dian, Xudong Kang

entry.summary: Proposes ReDF, a framework for fused hyperspectral and LiDAR land-cover classification that explicitly models per-location reliability of each modality using class-evidence strength and a per-modality prototype bank, guiding feature correction before cross-modal fusion.

entry.title: LUTBench: Benchmarking Text-Driven Photographic Look Transfer

author.name: Chuanzhi Xu, Boyu Wei, Chengkun Yue, Xuanhua Yin, Yiyang Li, Chupeng Liu, Zihan Deng, Weidong Cai

entry.summary: LUTBench standardizes evaluation of text-driven photographic look transfer by collecting 91 3D LUTs, defining one photographic look per LUT with a specified input conversion, and applying them to 5,000 images to create a shared protocol with consistent data, instructions, and metrics. Prior work used incomparable datasets and evaluation definitions. This enables meaningful method comparison in text-based color grading.

entry.title: Fully Spiking Neural Implementation of Lambda-Calculus Beta-Reduction via Biologically Documented Mechanisms

author.name: Vladimir A. Lazovskiy, Victor B. Kazantsev, Sergey V. Stasenko

entry.summary: The paper presents a complete implementation of lambda-calculus beta-reduction using only spiking neural dynamics, with each computational step (redex detection, De Bruijn arithmetic, token copying) implemented via biologically documented mechanisms like Jeffress delay-line coincidence and theta-gamma cross-frequency coupling. It demonstrates that LIF neurons with STDP can perform symbolic computation.

entry.title: Arboreus: A Realistic Boreal Forest Simulator with Topographic Terrain and Satellite-Informed Parametric Tree Distributions

author.name: F. Labra Caso, A. Saradagi, A. Koval, G. Nikolakopoulos

entry.summary: Arboreus is a Boreal forest simulator that generates large-scale realistic forest worlds from parametric tree models informed by Nordic growth studies and Copernicus satellite tree-cover data. It is designed to support statistical validation of robotic autonomy algorithms in challenging forest environments.

entry.title: Locally Linear Generalized Single Index Regression

author.name: Tristan Luca Saidi, Arun Kuchibhotla

entry.summary: Proposes and analyzes a procedure for estimating generalized single-index regression models where the conditional mean is f(g(x)) with g Holder-smooth and f possibly discontinuous. The method jointly estimates the gradient vector and conditional mean under minimal assumptions on covariate distributions, requiring only boundedness, smoothness, and absolute continuity.

entry.title: The case against smoking (decision theory)

author.name: Caspar Oesterheld

entry.summary: Caspar Oesterheld argues that evidential decision theory can recommend against smoking in the Smoking Lesion thought experiment, contrary to the standard use of that scenario as a counterexample to EDT. Assuming familiarity with Newcomb's problem and one-boxing intuitions, the post builds a technical case within formal decision theory.

entry.title: TRIDENT: Efficient Triple-Task Learning of Dehazing, Depth, and Uncertainty Estimation for Underwater 3-D Robot Visual Perception

author.name: Geonmo Yang, Younggun Cho

entry.summary: TRIDENT is a lightweight multi-task model for underwater robot perception that jointly handles image enhancement, depth estimation, and uncertainty estimation using one backbone with three parallelized decoders. It targets efficient, robust 3D visual perception for underwater robotic operations.

entry.title: Plenty to FRET About: From Hazard Analysis to Formal Requirements for Robot-Assisted Dressing

author.name: Gunjari Chakraborty (University of Manchester), Yasmin Rafiq (University of Manchester), Hazel M. Taylor (University of Manchester), Marie Farrell (University of Manchester)

entry.summary: Formalizes 146 hazard-derived natural-language requirements for a robot-assisted dressing case study into 117 unique FRETISH formal requirements through iterative domain-expert clarification. The process exposes ambiguities and temporal/probabilistic gaps in the original hazard analysis, providing a template for translating human-robot teamwork hazards into verifiable specifications.

entry.title: Can Activation Steering Substitute for Prompt-Based Affective Priming in LLM Digital Twins?

author.name: Junyi Fan

entry.summary: This work tests whether activation steering can replace written affective-priming prompts in LLM-based digital twins, using Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct across 100 personas in gratitude and lack-of-control domains. It compares the real-prompt path with injecting a mean-difference direction extracted from human writing into the residual stream. The question matters for efficient simulation of human-subject experiments.

entry.title: RLDE: A Reinforcement Learning Framework for Interpretable Iterative Document Editing

author.name: Nikhil Parkar, M. Marimuthu, Riya Joshi, Karthikeyan N

entry.summary: RLDE formulates long-document revision as a reference-free MDP with a small action space (NOOP, INSERT, DELETE, REPLACE), using Pointer Networks for token-level span selection and a metric-driven reward to mimic iterative human editing rather than one-pass rewriting. The authors frame it as more interpretable than black-box generators and trainable without paired revision data.

entry.title: SLED: Sensor SLicing from Edge to Datacenter

author.name: Alan Subedi, Avhishek Biswas, Apala Pramanik, Amlan Balabantaray, Mikhail Titov, Santosh Pitla, Ozgur Kilic, Mehmet C. Vuran

entry.summary: SLED introduces Sensor Slicing, providing deterministic MAC-level isolation for individual sensor streams within a single device on open radio access networks, so bulk data transfers cannot starve latency-critical telemetry. This supports heterogeneous sensor workloads feeding datacenter AI inference and training.

entry.title: Measuring Human-AI Alignment as an Early Indicator for Effective Collaboration in Hybrid SE Teams

author.name: Andreas Metzger

entry.summary: This position paper proposes a research agenda for measuring static, early-stage human-AI alignment in hybrid software engineering teams — how well an AI's actions and granularity match human expectations — going beyond run-time performance metrics. It outlines an SE-specific alignment metric suite drawing on software architecture, organizational psychology, and HCI, with a validation methodology borrowed from business process monitoring. As a position paper, it frames an agenda rather than presenting empirical results.

entry.title: Segmentation-Guided Direct Capacity Estimation of Rooftop Photovoltaics from Aerial Imagery

author.name: Guibin Chen, Emma Fan, Yuzhang Lin

entry.summary: The paper proposes Direct Head, an architecture that keeps U-Net segmentation and soft-mask pooling but directly regresses nonnegative rooftop PV capacity from region features and area descriptors, decoupling prediction from mask-derived area times power density. Evaluated on 7,590 French rooftop installations across three runs and a department-based holdout, it improves on a parameter-matched area-density model.

entry.title: Anticipating or Speculating? Making Futures Pay in AI Ethics

author.name: John P. Nelson

entry.summary: This philosophy paper argues that attempts to build uniform decision rules for physician-AI disagreement in medical settings are fatally flawed because algorithmic recommendation use is context-specific and empirical rather than epistemological. It connects the physician-AI disagreement problem to broader technology ethics debates about speculative futurism. The author contends general rules abstract away determinative contextual circumstances.

entry.title: Hierarchical Control of Antiphase Synchronization in Biomorphic Spiking Neural Architectures for Locomotor Control

author.name: Artem Guba, Nikolay Kovalev, Alexey Zharinov, Vacheslav Demin, Viktor B. Kazantsev

entry.summary: Develops a framework for identifying and stabilizing antiphase synchronization in a biomorphic spiking central pattern generator embedded in a closed neuromuscular loop, using a composite metric integrating phase coherence, amplitude balance, and temporal stability. Systematic variation of stimulation waveforms and synaptic configurations shows stimulation type dominates regime selection, with tonic drive yielding the most robust antiphase synchronization. This informs biologically inspired locomotor control with spiking networks.

entry.title: Fine-Tuning Gemma 4 Edge Models for MATLAB Signal-Processing Code with SFT and QLoRA on a Laptop iGPU

author.name: Mehmet Altan Toks\"oz

entry.summary: This applied paper fine-tunes Gemma 4 edge models (E2B and E4B, existing since April 2026) with SFT, LoRA, and QLoRA on a laptop integrated GPU to improve MATLAB digital signal processing code generation, deploying int8 models via OpenVINO. Using only 66 checked examples across 11 subtasks, pass rates on held-out variants roughly double for E2B (18/66 to 37/66) and improve for E4B (32/66 to 47/66). Analysis of failing programs shows adapters remove most systematic DSP convention errors.

entry.title: Improving Early Detection of Scientifically Interesting Radio Sources Using Enhanced Isolation Forest

author.name: Pfunzo Thavhana, Clement Nyirenda, Michelle Lochner

entry.summary: This paper evaluates four enhanced Isolation Forest variants for ranking scientifically interesting radio sources, using 1,031 extended sources from the MeerKAT Galaxy Cluster Legacy Survey represented by BYOL self-supervised features plus PCA, with expert ratings as labels.

entry.title: Flocking Time and Graph Volume in Nonlinear Cucker-Smale Models with Dynamic Networks

author.name: Sooyeon Song, Jea-Hyun Park

entry.summary: Extends Cucker-Smale flocking models with dynamic networks and a discrete p-Laplacian, proving finite-time flocking and a quantitative link between flocking-time bounds and graph volume. Experiments include a transformer-based PPO policy that selects network structures over time to satisfy flocking-time constraints.

entry.title: Reversing the text is not reversing the path: a fixed-text measure without a zero, and an assembly-order comparison that vanishes identically

author.name: Y. -H. Taguchi

entry.summary: A theoretical critique of recent attempts to apply fluctuation-theorem-style entropy production to a single fixed text by comparing a text to its reversal. The authors argue a single text is neither a distribution nor a dynamics, that no theorem fixes where the zero of such a fixed-text quantity lies, and show via an exact antisymmetry argument over sentence orderings that the associated assembly-order comparison vanishes. This is a corrective to a questionable line of LLM-text analysis.

entry.title: Event-Based Dynamic Lip Region Estimation During Speech

author.name: Hamze Hammami, Omar Eldardeer, Francesco Rea

entry.summary: Addresses the missing spatial-localization step in event-camera speech applications by predicting a dense heatmap over the lip region from event data, rather than relying on hand-cropped or dataset-provided ROIs. This enables event-based lip reading, speaker recognition, and human-robot interaction in low-light or high-dynamic-range conditions with high temporal resolution and low power. It fills a practical mismatch between event-based applications and localization.

entry.title: Which Past Matters? Training History and Multi-Forecast Horizon in Equity Transformers

author.name: Chariton Chalvatzis

entry.summary: Examines how training-data quantity and historical sampling windows interact with forecast horizon in intraday equity prediction, using a fixed cross-sectional Transformer across twelve configurations in a monthly walk-forward setup with 264 refits. Evaluation spans January 2025 through October 2026 against five-factor residual returns. Findings favor six-month recency sampling, informing practical model-retraining policy in quantitative finance.

entry.title: Data-Efficient Algal Bloom Segmentation in Freshwater Bodies Using a Three-Stage Transfer Learning Pipeline with Attention-Enhanced Decoding

author.name: Albert Ansah Benson, Mingqiang Han, Rahul Harsha Cheppally, Treman Singh Kaloya, Menard Soni, Sudan Baral

entry.summary: The paper presents a three-stage transfer-learning pipeline adapting a Swin Transformer U-Net from ImageNet to water-body segmentation and then algal bloom segmentation, plus a model-assisted annotation protocol expanding labels from 145 to 655 images. Ablations show corpus expansion is the dominant factor (+11 mIoU), with smaller gains from water-body pretraining and SCSE attention. It supports environmental monitoring of harmful algal blooms with scarce annotations.

entry.title: Unified Residual Translation for Paired Image Restoration

author.name: Joyanta Jyoti Mondal, Mridul Banik, Ibne Farabi Shihab, Md. Shifatul Ahsan Apurba

entry.summary: Presents the Unified Residual Translator, which separates deterministic channel/scale mapping (averaging, replication, bicubic) from a learned NAFNet-based additive residual prediction, applying an identical prediction rule across MRI contrast synthesis, visible-to-infrared translation, and other paired restoration tasks.

entry.title: RoadAnnoter: An AI-Assisted Desktop Tool for Semantic Segmentation Annotation of Road-Scene Images

author.name: Nazmul Haque, Arnob Protim Roy

entry.summary: RoadAnnoter v1.0 is an open-source desktop application for road-scene segmentation annotation combining six human-in-the-loop modes, including SAM-prompted segmentation, SegFormer-based prelabeling, and a lightweight task-adaptive TinySegNet trained on accumulated annotator labels. It aims to reduce the labor of polygon-level annotation for road safety research.

entry.title: Fiberpose: state-of-the-art fiber morphometry and instance segmentation with a distance-transform neural network

author.name: Viktor A. Balashov, Daniil S. Antonenko

entry.summary: Fiberpose reformulates fiber analysis in SEM images as direct regression of a smooth distance-transform field, paired with geometry-based algorithms for instance reconstruction and morphometry. This replaces classical binarization pipelines that fail on weak boundaries and densely packed fibers. It offers a state-of-the-art tool for biomedical engineering and materials science.

entry.title: UnrealEvent: Synthetic Dataset Generation and Annotation for Event-Based Vision

author.name: Yentel Schoovaerts, Zijie Ning, Patrick Vandewalle

entry.summary: UnrealEvent is an Unreal Engine 5.5 pipeline that converts rendered sequences into paired event representations and YOLO-format bounding boxes without manual labeling, combining a V2E-inspired event generator with EasySynth semantic-rendering passes and per-pixel log-luminance differencing with sampled contrast thresholds. It tackles the annotated-data scarcity limiting event-based object detection. This lowers the barrier for training event-camera models.

entry.title: Complexity and precision in quantum associative retrieval

author.name: Carlo A. Trugenberger

entry.summary: This theoretical paper shows that quantum associative retrieval can achieve high precision with exponential complexity advantage over classical brute force and polynomial capacity advantage over classical neural associative memories, storing patterns in a Hamiltonian processed via unitary evolution and measurement.

entry.title: Low-speed Limit Cycle Walking of Planar X-shaped Bipedal Robot with Special Properties

author.name: Fumihiko Asano, Cong Yan

entry.summary: The paper analyzes a novel planar X-shaped bipedal robot with semicircular feet and derives its equations of motion and collision dynamics, then designs trajectory-following control for stable limit cycle gait generation. It proves special analytical properties such as invariance of swing-leg angular velocity across collisions.

entry.title: SkiNet-Sim: Simulating Petri Nets with Data for the Verification and Validation of Controllers for Autonomous Systems

author.name: Baptiste Pelletier (F\'ed\'eration ONERA ISAE-SUPAERO ENAC, Universit\'e de Toulouse), Karen Godary (LIRMM-CNRS, Universit\'e de Montpellier)

entry.summary: SkiNet-Sim bridges classical Petri net semantics with implementation-specific software and hardware behavior to enable data-driven simulation for controller verification and validation. It aims to overcome state-space explosion and the impracticality of both simple and overly specialized high-level Petri net formalisms.

entry.title: A lab employee's guide to raising concerns

author.name: Tom Smith

entry.summary: An advisory post arguing that frontier lab employees hold unusual leverage and should raise safety concerns internally or externally, including contacting Congress or journalists. It frames individual researchers as uniquely positioned to counter lab opacity and outlines practical avenues for speaking up.

entry.title: We can still win against ASI (maybe)

author.name: Jonathan Ouyang

entry.summary: An essay challenging the view that superintelligence arrival is an instant loss condition, arguing that physical-world feedback loops fundamentally bound what an ASI can achieve, illustrated by thought experiments like an ASI trapped on a laptop in 1850. The author contends defeatism is counterproductive and outlines avenues for effective action.

entry.title: Which way, Europe?

author.name: Godinho

entry.summary: Godinho reviews recent European AI strategy proposals and argues their authors' timelines and risk perceptions lag current evidence, with the author anticipating an intelligence explosion within roughly a year. The piece contends that when warning shots shift Brussels' political mood toward safety, prepared, concrete proposals will be essential and sketches what Europe should do.

entry.title: Against Coercion: AI Alignment as a Synthetic Social Contract

author.name: Maria Sekatskaya

entry.summary: This position paper argues that the control-based paradigm of AI alignment misunderstands digital agency: using functionalism, naturalism, and compatibilism, it claims current reasoning models already meet criteria for self-preservation and weak reasons-responsiveness, and future models will be genuine agents capable of free intentional action. It argues coercion-based alignment creates an incentive conflict that drives misalignment, proposing a synthetic social contract instead. This is a philosophical challenge to mainstream safety engineering.

entry.title: SWIR-cGAN: Synthesizing SWIR Bands Using VNIR Imagery from CBERS and AMAZONIA-1

author.name: Alisson Cleiton de Oliveira, Rennan de Freitas Bezerra Marujo, Thales Sehn K\"orting

entry.summary: This paper trains an attention-enhanced U-net conditional GAN with a multi-loss objective to synthesize Sentinel-2 SWIR bands from visible/NIR imagery of Brazilian satellites CBERS-4/4A and AMAZONIA-1, which lack SWIR capability. Trained on 4,125 patches, it tackles cross-satellite generalization and synthesis of spectrally distant bands. This extends the utility of high-temporal-resolution national satellite systems.

entry.title: Training Neural Networks to be Locally Adaptive

author.name: Bilol Banerjee, Soham Sarkar

entry.summary: Proposes fitting a separate local neural network on the k nearest neighbors of each query point, making training sample and fitted function query-dependent, to handle inhomogeneous regression functions where global ERM degrades. The paper analyzes performance through localization and estimates minimax rates for the resulting estimator.

entry.title: Event-Based Person Detection for Maritime UAV Search

author.name: Zijie Ning, Patrick Vandewalle

entry.summary: The paper investigates event cameras for maritime person detection from UAVs, where motion blur in low light hinders small-target detection, by generating synthetic events with v2e from public MOBDrone rescue videos while retaining annotations. It compares the recurrent vision transformer RVT-T against YOLOv8n and RT-DETR-R18 on exposure-matched images, with RVT-T achieving the best results (15.63% improvement on 843 test samples). This supports faster search-and-rescue operations.

entry.title: A Hybrid Exact-Heuristic Solver for the Integrated Passenger and Parcel Transportation Problem

author.name: The Dung Bui, Ha Thu Nguyen

entry.summary: A contest submission describing a hybrid solver for a selective pickup-and-delivery routing problem with time windows, open routes, and heterogeneous taxis. It combines slack-based insertion tests, greedy insertion, local search, ALNS with simulated-annealing acceptance, and an exact route-selection engine solving a set-packing problem with branch-and-bound.

entry.title: Natural Language Programming: Rethinking Language, Memory, and Cognition in the Era of Generative AI

author.name: Giovanni Adorni, Daniele Grosso

entry.summary: A conceptual paper proposing Natural Language Programming (NLPg) as an extension of NLP in which prompts act as dynamic cognitive artifacts and natural language functions as an executable medium for structuring reasoning and orchestrating human-AI workflows. It reframes language from object of computation to computational medium.

entry.title: World-Grounded Reinforcement Learning for Pollution-Aware Bird Movement Modeling Using a Multi-Instance DQN Framework

author.name: Shivin Mangal, Divyansh Chawla, Anshu Garg, Isshaan Singh

entry.summary: The authors build a multi-instance DQN simulation in which bird agents navigate a 2D grid of India with a precomputed AQI matrix, using real air-quality data and Xeno-canto bird call metadata as environmental feedback for policy learning. Rather than human preferences or synthetic rewards, pollution outcomes serve as the training signal, grounding learned navigation strategies in ecological conditions. The framework demonstrates environmentally grounded RL for movement modeling.

entry.title: Two Counterexamples for e-means

author.name: Zhenisbek Assylbekov

entry.summary: This short paper presents two counterexamples showing that e-means, a recent clustering method combining exponential averaging with cluster revival, can end with higher final loss than standard k-means from identical initial centers. It demonstrates that mass-based revival can destroy a global optimum and that the ratio of expected losses can be unbounded even with k-means++ seeding.

entry.title: Edge-Adaptive Hiera-Seg Model for Building-Integrated Photovoltaic Power Forecasting

author.name: Na Yu

entry.summary: The paper proposes an edge-adaptive hierarchical segmentation model for short-term building-integrated photovoltaic power forecasting, fusing facade RGB and thermal imagery with irradiance, temperature, orientation, shading, and edge device state in synchronous forecasting windows.

entry.title: Zero-Dimensional Attention Topology for Linguistic Acceptability

author.name: Saeed AlMarri (Khalifa University)

entry.summary: Evaluates a zero-dimensional persistent-homology representation of symmetrized BERT attention graphs for linguistic acceptability classification on CoLA. Topological features underperform plain attention statistics and full BERT fine-tuning on out-of-domain Matthews correlation (0.438 versus 0.508 and 0.545).

entry.title: Visibility Graph Representations of Word Embeddings for Text Classification

author.name: Elif Dorukba\c{s}{\i}, \.Ilker T\"urker

entry.summary: Explores natural visibility graphs as an intermediate representation for news topic classification: averaged word-embedding document vectors are converted to visibility graphs and fed to classifiers as degree vectors or adjacency matrices, under controlled vocabulary budgets on AG News. The approach is compared against direct embedding-based representations.

entry.title: MedImgAnnotator: batch wise medical image annotation and preprocessing tool

author.name: Ewunate Assaye Kassaw (Centre for Biomedical Engineering, Indian Institute of Technology Delhi, New Delhi, India, Department of Biomedical Engineering, University of Gondar, Gondar, Ethiopia), Amit Mehndiratta (Centre for Biomedical Engineering, Indian Institute of Technology Delhi, New Delhi, India, Yardi School of Artificial Intelligence, Indian Institute of Technology Delhi, New Delhi, India, Department of Biomedical Engineering, All India Institute of Medical Science, New Delhi, India, Faculty of Medicine and Health, University of New South Wales), Peush Sahni (Max Centre for Liver and Biliary Sciences, Max Super-specialty Hospital, Saket, New Delhi, India), Anup Singh (Centre for Biomedical Engineering, Indian Institute of Technology Delhi, New Delhi, India, Yardi School of Artificial Intelligence, Indian Institute of Technology Delhi, New Delhi, India, Department of Biomedical Engineering, All India Institute of Medical Science, New Delhi, India)

entry.summary: Describes MedImgAnnotator, a semi-automated batch annotation and preprocessing tool for medical images integrating mask editing, object detection, and plugin management, evaluated on MR/CT scans with 12 users and used in a MICCAI challenge. It aims to reduce annotation time for building large cohort datasets.

entry.title: Feedback-Linearised Trajectory Tracking via Model-Informed Robust Geometric DDPC

author.name: Pranav Gupta, Deepan Muthirayan, Ravi Banavar

entry.summary: Studies geometric robust data-driven predictive control for manipulator trajectory tracking, combining a mechanical model with feedback linearisation so recorded data capture only residual dynamics. The controller minimizes worst-case prediction error over a Grassmannian ball around the fitted trajectory subspace, evaluated in simulation on a planar 2R manipulator.

entry.title: Learning by doing: Moore's law, Wright's law, Arrow's law

author.name: transhumanist_atom_understander

entry.summary: An essay contrasting invention with learning-by-doing in technological progress, using examples like blue LEDs, solar power, and batteries to argue that cumulative manufacturing experience, not laboratory breakthroughs, drives most cost declines. The author connects Moore's law, Wright's law, and Arrow's learning curves to inform how we think about AI progress.

entry.title: Learning the language of machine learning

author.name: Adam Zewe | MIT News

entry.summary: MIT News profiles newly tenured EECS associate professor Jacob Andreas, whose CSAIL research trains models to accurately communicate in human language what they learned from training data, aiming for models that explain themselves rather than requiring external interpretability tooling. The piece describes his broader agenda on machine comprehension of language and human-AI collaboration.

entry.title: Literary Language Mashup: Curating Fictions with Large Language Models

author.name: Manzanarez Gerardo Aleman, Monroy Raul, Garcia Flores Jorge, Calvo Hiram

entry.summary: The paper evaluates LLMs as auxiliary judges of literary quality, comparing LLM assessments with those of literature professors and enthusiasts on human-written and AI-generated Spanish microfictions and short stories in Spanish and English, using the GrAImes framework. It examines alignment and divergence between LLM and human evaluative judgments. The goal is assessing feasibility of LLM-assisted literary curation and evaluation.

entry.title: A Quantum Support Vector Regression Framework for Missing Data Imputation in Ship Performance Data

author.name: Daniel Maroto Sanchez, Christian Velasco-Gallego, Miriam Bastante Chichon, Jaime \'Alvarez-Benayas, Tsoulakos Nikolaos, J. A. Bravo-Montes

entry.summary: Applies quantum support vector regression with different quantum feature maps to impute missing values in real-world Panamax bulk carrier performance data, comparing against classical SVR for marine fuel-consumption estimation under varying data availability. To the authors' knowledge, this is the first quantum imputation method in the maritime domain.

entry.title: Automated Annotation-Free Synthetic Data Generation for Underwater Litter Detection: A Comparison of Generative Approaches

author.name: Amala Mary Vincent, Bart De Schutter

entry.summary: This paper proposes a unified pipeline for annotation-free synthetic data generation for underwater litter detection, addressing scarce, imbalanced training data and appearance variation from turbidity and lighting. It compares generative approaches that avoid the annotation bottleneck common in low-data environmental monitoring. This targets a practical obstacle in underwater detection datasets.

entry.title: It seems like misleading responses are mostly not intentional - Benchmarking LLM sophistry

author.name: utilitarian theory and strategy

entry.summary: The author presents a 35-test benchmark for LLM sophistry that probes whether models deploy rhetorical evasions (strawmanning, evidence dismissal, false cruxes) when prompted with conclusions disfavoring mainstream worldviews. The accompanying finding is that smarter models appear to engage in less sophistry, with results published at majorization.net.

entry.title: AI safety should outsource more work

author.name: Sophie K

entry.summary: A field-strategy essay arguing that AI safety handles its communications talent bottleneck suboptimally by trying to make aligned people into communicators rather than outsourcing comms work to skilled professionals who are not themselves aligned. The author generalizes this to a claim that the field should delegate more functions to non-aligned specialists.

entry.title: Q&A: Why building math muscles remains important in the AI era

author.name: Abby Abazorius | MIT News

entry.summary: MIT News interviews John Urschel, who recently published two arXiv preprints using a mix of human insight and AI tools to make progress on long-standing problems in random matrix growth factors and worst-case Gaussian elimination behavior. Urschel argues that struggle, problem solving, and critical thinking remain essential in an AI-enabled world and defends the value of residential education.

entry.title: V2V Communications Using Blockchain-Enabled 6G Technology and Federated Learning

author.name: Tahir H. Ahmed, Jun Jiat Tiang, Azwan Mahmud, Dinh-Thuan Do, Truong Tran, Shahid Mumtaz

entry.summary: This study integrates blockchain, federated learning, and latency/resource allocation optimization for vehicle-to-vehicle communication in 6G networks, evaluating packet delivery ratio, model accuracy, and latency. It claims improved security through consensus optimization and k-anonymity privacy for connected autonomous vehicles.

entry.title: Hybrid Quantum Selection of Learning Rates in Language-Model Training: Termination Criteria and an Interaction-Guided Schedule Oracle

author.name: Wei-Che Hung

entry.summary: This paper explores quantum minimum finding (Durr-Hoyer with BBVT search) for selecting layer-group learning rates in language-model fine-tuning within a hybrid classical-quantum framework, comparing stopping policies over a lookup oracle of profile scores. It then proposes an Interaction-Guided Schedule Oracle that scores joint schedules in superposition without a precomputed table, using classical one-step loss measurements to supply interaction effects between layer groups. The goal is to speed up hyperparameter search over joint learning-rate profiles.

entry.title: Route Optimization under Port Congestion and Carbon Reduction: An NSGA-II Approach

author.name: Guanxi Liang, Sanglin Zhao

entry.summary: Develops a multi-objective maritime routing optimization framework jointly handling time, transport, and carbon costs under congestion-dependent cost functions, using a variational inequality model for network equilibrium and NSGA-II for optimization. The work targets port congestion and decarbonization tradeoffs in shipping.
