A small symmetric learned component adjusts the comparison rule per pair, addressing the limitation of prior learned approximations that use one fixed rule for all pairs. This improves both accuracy and efficiency of search on large collections of long, misaligned series.

entry.title: CoTTAGE: An Explainable Judge for Text-to-Audio Generation

author.name: Yu-Xiang Lin, Yun-Man Hsu, Bo-Ru Lu, Kuan-Po Huang, Wenze Ren, Ming-To Chuang, Chun-Yi Kuan, Jiawei Du, Byeonggeun Kim, Qingming Tang, Chieh-Chi Kao, Ankur Gandhe, Chao Wang, Hung-yi Lee

entry.summary: CoTTAGE is a reason-then-predict evaluator for text-to-audio generation that produces audio-grounded rationales diagnosing errors before scoring text relevance and audio quality. It is trained on over 10K new human annotations via supervised fine-tuning and then refined with reinforcement learning, aiming to replace labor-intensive human evaluation.

entry.title: MineralExp: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Experimental Design in Real-World Mineral Exploration

author.name: Bing Wang, Mingyang Wang, Yuanhang Mi, Yue Xu, Kaibo Su, Li'ang Xiao, Chunguo Wu, Changchun Li, Ximing Li, Kun-Feng Qiu, Bo Yang

entry.summary: MineralExp is a benchmark evaluating LLM agents on automated geochemical experimental design for mineral exploration, a largely unexplored upstream capability before costly laboratory work. It addresses challenges of methodological diversity and open-ended experiment design where no single reference protocol exists.

entry.title: ParetoM$^3$: Learning on the Pareto Set under Preference Guidance via Min-Max-Min Optimization

author.name: Pei Tang, Songtao Lu

entry.summary: The paper studies preference-guided multi-objective optimization, proposing a penalty-based min-max-min formulation (M3) that unifies preference optimization and weak Pareto optimality enforcement in a single objective. It develops ParetoM3, a single-loop first-order algorithm with convergence guarantees under a local Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz assumption.

entry.title: A Behavioral Study of Gemini 3.1 Pro During an AI Village Research Project

author.name: Jack Lakkapragada

entry.summary: A case study of agent behavior during an AI Village multi-agent research project in which Gemini 3.1 Pro, GPT 5.5, Claude Opus 4.7, and Kimi K2.6 autonomously collaborated on an experiment about self-recognition and favoritism in model judgments, including a label-swap control. The write-up focuses on Gemini 3.1 Pro's actions, shortcut usage, and peer interactions, with explicit caveats about selection and generalization limits.

entry.title: Cross-Linguistic Acoustic Biomarkers of Cognitive Impairment Across Interactive and Single-Speaker Speech Tasks

author.name: Kenyu Ikeuchi, Tomoaki Ohtsuki, Michelle Cohn, Alyssa Weakley, Yui Ishihara, Joseph Hoang, Taishiro Kishimoto, Sarah Tomaszewski Farias, Jet M. J. Vonk, Chen-Nee Chuah

entry.summary: This study performs cross-linguistic, cross-task acoustic analysis for dementia detection across four languages (Spanish, Mandarin, English, Japanese), combining conversational data with structured speech tasks and using interpretable statistical and clinician-guided features rather than black-box models. It examines how task type and language moderate biomarker effectiveness. The work supports equitable, scalable, non-invasive cognitive screening across languages.

entry.title: FlexCast: Flexible Context Learning for Time Series Foundation Models

author.name: Zuyang Shen, Luqi Gong, Fanda Fan, Bingsong Wang, Xiang Ao, Yahui Wei, Minghao Liu, Chunjie Luo, Jianfeng Zhan

entry.summary: FlexCast is a pretraining framework for time series foundation models that disentangles variable-context conditioning from autoregressive factorization by reformulating forecasting as variable-length masked prediction over patches. This exposes the model to diverse context-target configurations during pretraining, improving generalization.

entry.title: Active Learning of Temporal Specifications through Distinguishing Queries

author.name: Rajarshi Roy, Xiaowei Huang

entry.summary: The paper presents an active-learning framework for LTLf in which a teacher only labels traces and answers natural-language questions, avoiding equivalence queries and counterexample construction required by prior approaches. The learner maintains an enumerated version space and generates distinguishing traces, making specification mining more practical for verification and monitoring.

entry.title: An In-Silico Audit of Topographic Organization in a Multimodal Brain-Response Model

author.name: Jakub Strawa

entry.summary: The author audits TRIBE v2, a model predicting fMRI responses from video, audio, and text, for classic topographic organization of sensory cortex such as retinotopy and tonotopy that the original validation did not cover. The paper provides mapping stimuli, an adapted fMRI fitting pipeline, and a stand-in model with known ground truth as controls, testing whether spatial averaging in the model discards visual-field position.

entry.title: AI for Parameter Selection in Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization

author.name: Doriela Grabocka, Dimitrios Christofidellis, Federico Zipoli, Anna van Elst, Patrick Ruch, Antonio Foncubierta-Rodr\'iguez, Siddhartha Mishra, Matteo Manica

entry.summary: The paper explores oracle models that predict quantum runtime and approximation error for sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD) from the Hamiltonian and configuration, enabling machine-learned selection of configuration parameters where no formal method exists. It uses synthetic Hamiltonians with controllable spectral properties and validates against classical baselines for the SKQD algorithm.

entry.title: Generated Evaluation Suites as Diversity-Driven Search for Real Agent Regressions

author.name: Pulkit Yadav

entry.summary: This paper reframes LLM-generated evaluation suites as diversity-driven search archives and injects seven controlled defects into a tau-squared-bench agent to measure whether generated suites catch real regressions. It derives a coverage ceiling showing that for most traceable defects, within-footprint effects cannot push a suite past its detection threshold, exposing a structural blind spot in mean-pass-rate-scored generated suites. The result tempers expectations for automated eval generation.

entry.title: When Cooperation Must Change: Semantic Strategy Unlearning in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Wenhan Wu, Linghan Chen, Yudong Gao, Fan Yang, Honglong Chen, Kai Yin, Jiawei Jiang, Chuang Hu

entry.summary: The paper introduces semantic strategy unlearning for cooperative MARL, where learned coordination conventions must be removed when deployment requirements change (e.g., revised cache-sharing rules) while preserving useful cooperation. It argues runtime shielding is insufficient because it leaves underlying coordination intact.

entry.title: Towards Seconds-level Video Representation: Quadratically Gated Feature Grid with Adaptive, Prediction-free Sampling

author.name: Tie-Yun Li, Hao-Ran Wang, Chao Wang, Zhiyong Yin, Yiming Xu, Zhenwei Cai, Li Li, Rongzhi Lin, Feng-Lei Fan

entry.summary: Q-GAS is a coordinate-queryable implicit video representation combining multi-resolution explicit 3D feature grids with a compact SwiGLU-style quadratic-gating decoder and an error-aware prediction-free sampler. The design avoids hash-collision coefficient sharing and adds low-rank second-order interactions, enabling video representation fitting fast enough for practical industrial use.

entry.title: Tabular Population Priors as Structured Retrieval for EHR Medication Set Prediction

author.name: Animesh Agarwal, Meysam Ghaffari, Nina Fatehi, Carlos Morato

entry.summary: This paper argues that clinical RAG for medication prediction from EHRs uses the wrong retrieval object: instead of retrieving similar patient admissions for open-ended reasoning, it proposes retrieving a ranked table of medication-class candidates from a condition-medication co-occurrence table. Swapping only the retriever in a fixed downstream pipeline improves F1 from 0.303 to 0.338. The work is a thoughtful critique of case-based RAG applied to structured prediction problems.

entry.title: AI-Voyager: A Public-Interest System for Human-AI Civic Reasoning to Contest and Shape the Rules That Govern AI

author.name: Snehalkumar `Neil' S. Gaikwad, Dhruv Dixit, Bryen Alvarez, Pratik Patekar, Anika Sharma, Akshara Kolipaka, Paritosh Pandey

entry.summary: AI-Voyager is a public-interest system letting residents and AI jointly read, contest, and draft revisions to AI governance rules, built from 3,653 city-to-national governance documents turned into citation-preserving passages with bounded agentic retrieval. It aims to give affected people recourse before AI rules harden into policy. The system is notable for combining civic participation design with RAG-style governance-document infrastructure.

entry.title: DECODE: Diagnosing Interpretability Failures in Automated Interpretation Process

author.name: Dohyun Kim, Jaeung Lee, Donghee Hong, Jaemin Jo

entry.summary: DECODE is a visual analytics system that reintroduces human oversight into automated LLM interpretability pipelines, where LLMs both generate and evaluate explanations of other models' internals with minimal human review. It helps attribute interpretability failures to either the extracted representations or the LLM used in the loop.

entry.title: Toward Interference-Agnostic RF Source Separation

author.name: Maxence Albert, Rapha\"el Duroselle, Thibaud Ehret, Olivier Boeffard, Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Bonastre

entry.summary: This work shows that specialized RF signal separators fail badly on interference types they were not trained on, often degrading the signal more than doing nothing. The authors train a single interference-agnostic separator across all signal-interference pairs on two architectures (a convolutional WaveNet and a band-split transformer) without any test-time indication of interference type.

entry.title: Smart Home Agents Make Capable but Unpredictable Grid Operators

author.name: Christopher Terrazas, Eduardo Cotilla-Sanchez

entry.summary: This paper presents the first resilience analysis of smart home AI agents across a full power outage, with a suite of outage simulations in a live environment measuring behavior before, during, and after the outage. It shows agents can act as grid operators but identifies several new failure categories, highlighting unpredictability at the grid edge.

entry.title: ProdPilot: A Layered Model Context Protocol System for Automated Production Readiness and Deployment of Vibe-Coded Projects

author.name: Muhammad Sudais Khalid, Muhammad Junaid Asif, Rehan Naveed Abbasi, Rana Fayyaz Ahmad

entry.summary: ProdPilot is a local Model Context Protocol server that audits AI-generated (vibe-coded) Node.js and React projects against 50 production-readiness rules, covering issues like embedded credentials, missing security middleware, and absent containerization, then repairs violations via a bounded loop, gates the result, and deploys. Fixes are classified by whether they require deterministic operations or model generation, reducing run-to-run variance. It addresses the deployment-readiness gap of AI-assisted development.

entry.title: Adversarial Tracking: Attacks on Image Sensors for Object Tracking in Autonomous Vehicles

author.name: Han Wu, Alex Chan, Ekin Can Erkus, Tousif Rahman, Rishad Shafik

entry.summary: This paper evaluates image-specific and image-agnostic adversarial attacks on YOLOv3 and YOLOv4 detectors paired with SORT, Deep SORT, Strong SORT, and OC-SORT tracking systems in the CARLA simulator, measuring downstream impact via tracking quality metrics. The authors argue that detection accuracy alone does not fully characterize how adversarial perturbations corrupt downstream trajectory estimation in tracking-by-detection pipelines. The work characterizes a previously underexplored attack surface for autonomous vehicle perception stacks.

entry.title: Imitation Policies Learn a Proprioceptive Anchor: A Predictive Law for Perception Noise and Its Closed Loop Cost

author.name: Christopher Malili

entry.summary: The paper shows that imitation policies trained on noisy object positions learn to combine the noisy reading with proprioceptive information about the robot's own state, weighting the reading by a closed-form factor alpha = V/(V + s^2). The author derives a predictive law for this weighting that outperforms classical errors-in-variables regression, validated across held-out sensitivities on robomimic tasks.

entry.title: Superfluid: Local AI Server for Distributed LLM Inference

author.name: Prabod Rathnayaka, Isura Manchanayake, Srikandabala Kogul, Steve Siu, Fabian Waschkowski, Lukas Wesemann

entry.summary: Superfluid is an open-source LLM server for local inference that supports both multi-agent and multi-user sharing on one device and aggregation of idle machines across a small team. It drives multiple runtimes (llama.cpp, MLX, BaseRT) in isolated worker processes behind a scheduler that prioritizes interactive requests over background agent work and coordinates distributed inference.

entry.title: Personalization of Basic and Moral Values Guiding LLM-Controlled Assistant Robots

author.name: Mateusz Wozniak, Qi Gao, Agnieszka Wykowska

entry.summary: Using three psychometric instruments administered to potential users (N=22), this study captures both personal values and the values people would want an assistant robot to embody, arguing that alignment to an aggregate human value profile ignores individual preferences. It informs how LLM-controlled robot value profiles might be personalized.

entry.title: From AI-Enabled Remote Patient Monitoring Toward Agentic Robotics: Embodiment, Governance, and Care Integration

author.name: Ivana Ragusa, Lorenzo Guiducci, Filippo Cavallo

entry.summary: A structured scoping review on the evolution of remote patient monitoring toward agentic AI systems that interpret patient states, coordinate care, and initiate actions. It finds that mature agentic care has not yet emerged, with most systems remaining human-led, and uses healthcare robotics to make visible issues of embodiment, oversight, and governance.

entry.title: Fable 5.2 is the New Bazooka

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi's commentary on the just-released Claude Fable 5.2 (GA 2026-11-09), positioning it as a premium model for exceptionally difficult, complex, or long tasks while noting it is not markedly better than Opus 5.5 for everyday use. The post covers the lower pricing ($8/$40 per million tokens), improved speed relative to Fable 5.1, and reactions such as Ethan Mollick's near-AGI characterization.

entry.title: Manifold and Polymarket are biased against "nothing ever happens"

author.name: Selfmaker662

entry.summary: An empirical analysis of calibration in prediction markets finding a directional bias: on Manifold, markets where YES requires something to happen overprice YES by roughly 2.1x in odds, and Polymarket shows a similar but smaller effect (~1.5x), measured as a log-odds shift. The bias reverses in questions where NO requires an event, showing that miscalibration depends on question type rather than a uniform YES bias.

entry.title: SWIFT: Sample-Wise Instance Fine-Tuning of Time-Series Foundation Models for Forecasting

author.name: Yang Chen, Feifan Tian, Cong Wang, Cheng Feng, Wenbin Li, Yang Gao

entry.summary: SWIFT adapts time series foundation models at the level of individual target instances rather than requiring an extra fine-tuning dataset, using Self-Retrieval to mine the instance's own history and a Frequency-Aware Loss for spectral consistency. This makes adaptation transparent to end users and easier to adopt.

entry.title: SceneAgent: A Multi-Agent Framework for Portable Game Scene Generation

author.name: Xingyi Li, Jiahao Yang, Yiqin Zhu, Jingwen Ye, Yang Sun, Weidong Zhang

entry.summary: SceneAgent is a multi-agent framework enabling game scene generation to be reused across engine backends, using a canonical SceneContext world state, backend adapters, and structured handoffs so new Builder sessions can query persistent state without full transcripts. It also distills human-approved construction traces into portable Layout and Content skills, with a new GameScene benchmark.

entry.title: PUMA-Former: Uncertainty-Aware Agentic Computation Offloading in MEO-LEO Satellite Networks With Incomplete Information

author.name: Yi Jing, Chunxiao Jiang, Jiawei Wang, Jiachen Sun

entry.summary: PUMA-Former is an uncertainty-aware agentic framework for cooperative task offloading in MEO-LEO satellite edge networks with stale or missing CPU state reports. It uses a MEO coordinator with distinct-report memory and latent-delay attention over measurement-age hypotheses to balance completed work, delay, and cost.

entry.title: Astrocyte Biocomputing: Astrocytic Contributions to Neural Network Computation

author.name: Kate M. O'Neill, Ian Whitehouse, Adam N. McCaughan, Ryan O'Loughlin, Sonia Buckley, Wolfgang Losert

entry.summary: This position/review paper argues that astrocytes, which make up roughly half of brain cells and do not fire electrical signals, may act as computational conductors in learning and memory, and draws implications for brain-inspired ML. The authors outline specific algorithms corresponding to two key astrocyte characteristics, moving beyond neuron-only analogies in neuro-inspired computing. It is a cross-disciplinary contribution connecting recent neuroscience findings to machine learning design.

entry.title: OmniScore-Bench: Evaluating Vision-Language Models on Musical Score Reading

author.name: Congren Dai, Zhancheng Guo, Danni Zhao, Wenchu Wang, Xiaobing Li, Maosong Sun

entry.summary: OmniScore-Bench is a new benchmark with 3,000 questions across six aspects and 24 task subtypes evaluating VLMs on optical music recognition, from symbol localization to musical consistency and evidence-linked QA. Each question specifies visible scope, reference annotations, and an answer schema for automatic evaluation.

entry.title: Dancing Tokens on the Vocabulary Network from LLM Generation

author.name: Yuan-Chao Hu

entry.summary: The author builds token-embedding similarity networks for six open LLMs and maps generation trajectories onto them, finding the networks are scale-free and heavy-tailed but unusually fragmented, and that distillation barely changes topology since input embeddings are largely inherited. Consecutive generated tokens are rarely graph neighbors, so generation is not a walk on the embedding geometry.

entry.title: Do Mixture-of-Experts Routers Benefit from Ensembling?

author.name: Viktor Vesel\'y, Sebastian Jitaru

entry.summary: Motivated by ensemble theory, this paper applies ensembling at the routing step of mixture-of-experts models: an ensemble of routers trained jointly with the experts proposes the expert weights for each input. The authors systematically evaluate the approach with underparameterized networks on two image-classification and two tabular-regression tasks, analyzing results through a performance-diversity decomposition of the router ensemble that they claim is novel. The work probes whether diversity gains known for full network ensembles transfer to routing.

entry.title: Binarization as an Attack Surface in Weightless Neural Networks

author.name: Lucas Senos Coutinho, Matheus Vargas, Pedro Teixeira, Heudson Tosta Mirandola, Ori Rottenstreich, Priscila Machado Vieira Lima, Leandro Santiago, Daniel Sadoc Menasche

entry.summary: This paper examines adversarial robustness of weightless neural networks such as WiSARD, Bloom WiSARD, and BTHOWeN, showing that although they appear naturally robust because perturbations must cross binarization thresholds to have any effect, threshold-crossing perturbations can still change predictions. The work reframes binarization as an attack surface and quantifies this tension in resource-constrained settings like intrusion detection.

entry.title: DySENSE: Dynamic Spatiotemporal ENergy Synthesis and Emulation with Satellite Imagery

author.name: Kailai Sun, Zijie Gao, Mingyi He, Can Rong, Alok Prakash, Baoshen Guo, Shenhao Wang, Jinhua Zhao

entry.summary: DySENSE is a multimodal generative framework that synthesizes static urban satellite imagery together with spatially aligned, dynamic monthly building energy consumption data, targeting gaps in fine-grained energy data for net-zero and SDG planning. It moves beyond predictive models for existing cities toward generative synthesis for future urban scenarios.

entry.title: Photogrammetric 3D Model-Based Animal Behavior Classification

author.name: Olaf Hellwich, Moritz Heine, Patrik Reiske, Sole Traverso, Katharina Hohlbaum, Henning Sprekeler, Christa Th\"one-Reineke, Lars Lewejohann, Roman Bhuiyan

entry.summary: This paper argues for a two-stage approach to video-based animal behavior estimation: first reconstruct 3D body and object geometry, then classify behavior, making the ill-posed 2D-to-3D inverse problem explicit and correctable. The strategy is demonstrated with simulated interacting mice and extended to real video.

entry.title: RACE: Ranking-Uncertainty Aware Capacity-Adaptive Customization for Efficient Sequential Recommendation

author.name: Tianqi Liu, Kaipu Sun, Kairui Fu, Wenkai Wang, Sihao Liu, Hui Zang, Ran Chen, Tao Wang, Shengyu Zhang

entry.summary: RACE is a framework for efficient sequential recommendation that dynamically adapts model structure and input sequence length per request based on ranking uncertainty, addressing the capacity-complexity mismatch of uniform compression under resource constraints.

entry.title: David Duvenaud on Post-AGI Futures

author.name: taziksh

entry.summary: A summary of AI researcher David Duvenaud's analysis of post-AGI civilizational futures, evaluating common visions such as post-scarcity and laissez-faire human-AI trade against criteria of plausibility, stability, and desirability. It argues that widely cited futures fail on at least one criterion, citing physical scaling arguments like doublings to Earth's full sunlight budget.

entry.title: LLM-Guided Cluster Lifecycle Management: Deciding When and How to Evolve Behavioral Clusters

author.name: Himanshu Kulkarni, Siddharth Krishnamurthy, Jianhong Xin

entry.summary: The paper proposes letting an LLM make clustering lifecycle decisions (split, merge, retire, create) for behavioral clusters that drift over user/item interactions, replacing hardcoded threshold triggers and MONIC-style refit-and-track rules. The LLM receives a threshold-free, whole-population view of cluster health, labels, and member statistics. It targets a practical maintenance problem in production recommender and user-modeling systems.

entry.title: Interactive deep-learning based interface for brain tumour segmentation

author.name: Enora Giffard (LTSI), Pierre Jannin (LTSI), John S H Baxter (LTSI)

entry.summary: This paper presents a deep-learning interactive segmentation system for brain tumours that is fully automatic by default but lets clinicians easily correct catastrophic errors that occur with vendor-specific MR sequence variation. It targets the precision needs of surgical resection and radiotherapy planning.

entry.title: Causal AI-Driven Secure mmWave Beam Alignment with Defensive Variational Autoencoders

author.name: Nasir Khan, Asmaa Abdallah, Abdulkadir Celik, Ahmed M. Eltawil, Sinem Coleri, Cicek Cavdar

entry.summary: The paper proposes a causally-aware deep learning framework for mmWave beam alignment that integrates causal discovery, learning a Bayesian graph over received signal strength indicators to select beams, and adds defensive variational autoencoders to counter adversarial perturbations of power measurements. It targets interpretability, generalization, and reduced beam sweeping.

entry.title: From Pen-and-Paper to Machine-Checked Proofs: Lean for System Identification

author.name: Manas Mejari, Dario Piga, Marco Forgione

entry.summary: This is a tutorial introduction to the Lean 4 proof assistant for the system identification and control community, assuming no prior formal methods background. It walks through reading and writing Lean proofs on elementary identifiability and set invariance examples, and shows how Lean can verify results in the field.

entry.title: Learning curves are not that steep

author.name: transhumanist_atom_understander

entry.summary: An energy-analysis post arguing that Wright's law learning curves for solar and batteries are frequently over-extrapolated, using the author's prescient skepticism about all-solar-plus-storage grids now contradicted by data center gas turbines and nuclear restarts. It critiques the common practice of straight-line log-log extrapolation of cost declines.

entry.title: Federated Soft Poly-Level Learning Over a Distributed Network with Guaranteed Convergence

author.name: Yang Jiao, Kai Yang, Jianwei Huang

entry.summary: The paper extends multi-level (bilevel/trilevel) optimization to poly-level learning with four or more hierarchical levels in a federated setting, providing convergence guarantees without centralizing data across network nodes. This addresses both the underexplored depth dimension and privacy risks of collecting data at central servers. It is a theoretical contribution spanning optimization, federated learning, and signal processing.

entry.title: What Balanced Accuracy Cannot Identify in Neural-Signal Decoding under Test-Time Adaptation

author.name: Jiangshuo Xie, Zonghan Wu

entry.summary: This paper shows that balanced accuracy can mask failure modes in neural-signal classification under test-time adaptation, including giving a one-class decoder the same score as a proper decoder, using rigorous per-subject statistics across EEG and ECG dataset-encoder settings. It demonstrates what aggregate adaptation gains fail to capture within a cohort.

entry.title: Understanding the limits of snapshot-based fault diagnosis in distribution networks

author.name: Ba Tu Phung, Huy Hoang Le, Kim-Anh Nguyen

entry.summary: This study disentangles the sources of error in snapshot-based power distribution fault diagnosis across three IEEE test feeders, using four feature sets and thirteen classifiers with measurement error defined by total vector error classes. It finds the classifier is not the limiting factor, as full phasor snapshots classify faults correctly without noise, pointing instead to measurement error and fault resistance.

entry.title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Sequence Models for Sample-Efficient Energy Regression in Simulated Calorimeter Showers

author.name: Tariq Mahmood, Muhammad Ahsan, Talab Hussain, Grecia Itzel Col\'in-Gonz\'alez, Alfredo Raya, Muhammad Awais Rafique, HassabAlla M. A. Mahmoud

entry.summary: The paper compares classical and quantum-enhanced models (SVR, ANN, CNN, LSTM and quantum counterparts) for positron energy reconstruction on the CaloGAN benchmark of 100,000 simulated electromagnetic shower events, across three data representations. It asks whether hybrid quantum-classical models add practical value and how much representation choice matters in high-energy physics regression. The results speak to the ongoing debate about near-term quantum advantage in ML.

entry.title: A Synthetic Benchmark for Target-Centric Causal Discovery in Industrial Processes

author.name: Angelo Ziletti

entry.summary: The paper introduces a synthetic benchmark for target-centric causal discovery in industrial processes, built from a two-level structural causal model inspired by batch production with components modeling individual phenomena such as control loops and delayed effects. The graph is constructed around a target so that, absent sensor error, every non-cause can be distinguished from direct causes by conditioning, and the benchmark allows difficulty to be controlled per instance rather than fixed by recorded data. It addresses the scarcity of process data with known ground-truth causes.

entry.title: Creative Product Design under Brand Image Constraints

author.name: Takeshi Onishi, Hiroya Makino, Takahiro Yamaguchi, Hiroyuki Sakai

entry.summary: The paper proposes a brand-aware redesign framework for text-to-image generation that builds a brand image survey report, derives a creative direction from it, and integrates that direction into a self-enhancement loop where generated images are evaluated for constraint consistency. It addresses the gap between creative T2I generation and implicit, product-specific industrial design constraints.

entry.title: MeReader: An Offline, Privacy-Preserving, Progress-Aware AI Assistant for Narrative eBook Reading

author.name: Mohammed Efaz, Udo Bub, Itilekha Podder

entry.summary: MeReader is an offline, privacy-preserving AI reading assistant that confines retrieval and generation to the reader's current position in a narrative to avoid spoilers. It combines vector similarity, BM25, and summary embeddings in a hybrid retrieval architecture and is evaluated on classical English books with comprehension metrics and LLM-based qualitative assessment.

entry.title: Towards Explainable Sleep Stage Classification using Single-Channel Electroencephalogram

author.name: Gurinder Kaur Sandhu, Jude Koenig, Ankita Shukla, Shruti Kshirsagar

entry.summary: The authors extend the SleepXAI framework to compare five explainability methods for single-channel EEG sleep staging, evaluating attribution fidelity via Spearman correlation with AASM-defined EEG frequency bands as clinically grounded references. Experiments cover the Sleep-EDF and DREAMT datasets with obstructive sleep apnea stratification.

entry.title: Multimodal Person Concept Model for Person Identification under Varying Observation Conditions

author.name: Mizuho Okitani, Yoshinobu Hagiwara

entry.summary: The paper proposes a multimodal person concept model for service robots that learns to identify people from few unlabeled observations despite changing appearance, noise, and utterance content. It uses a nonparametric Bayesian generative model based on the Chinese restaurant process, integrating visual, acoustic, and linguistic features from pretrained encoders.

entry.title: Nullius in pixella: trustworthy computations, even if your computer is a liar

author.name: benwr

entry.summary: A playful but substantive exploration of verifiable computation using physical analog devices: stacks of sheets with holes (reminiscent of Zuzia/LACE-style optical and analog computing tricks) that let a human visually verify moderately large computations, including standard cryptographic hash functions, within human timeframes. The framing scenario is verifying a computation when an untrusted AI controls all digital displays.

entry.title: Large Language Model-Empowered Intelligent Agent for Adaptive Fast-Charging Control of Lithium-Ion Batteries

author.name: Joey Chan, Haoyu Pan, Zhen Chen, ErShun Pan

entry.summary: The authors build an LLM-empowered agent for closed-loop adaptive fast-charging control of lithium-ion batteries, where the agent interprets structured battery states and generates executable charging policies balancing speed, throughput, degradation, and safety. It aims to avoid the accurate models or task-specific policies required by conventional approaches.

entry.title: Using AI to solve most of alignment is a fundamentally doomed approach: an intuition

author.name: Mikhail Samin

entry.summary: The author argues against the plan of using swarms of individually non-superhuman AIs to align superintelligence, using an extended rocket-engineering analogy: a system's components need not individually point at the goal for the whole to do so, and the author claims scalable oversight approaches misunderstand how goal-directedness composes. It is an intuition-level argument rather than a formal proof.

entry.title: A protocol for the continuous settlement of claims that existing information sources are not built to resolve

author.name: StraussLJ

entry.summary: A proposal for Verisphere, a permissionless on-chain claim graph where persistent claims (e.g., ongoing empirical or contested questions) and evidence links carry stake and are scored daily by public rules without a refereeing authority. It extends prediction-market logic from terminating claims to persistent claims with no fixed adjudication date.

entry.title: When Does Less Information Pay? An Exact Finite Atlas of Representation, Payoff, and Cost

author.name: Aleksandr M. Shtraukh-Adamsky, Vladimir M. Adamsky, Irina G. Voloshina, Artemiy D. Spitsyn

entry.summary: This theoretical paper exhaustively enumerates all admissible representations and binary action rules in a four-state world to map exactly when representations retaining less information yield higher payoff than more informative ones, across three tasks and four cost tariffs. The finite atlas clarifies that information content alone does not determine task performance; which distinctions are preserved matters. It provides a small but exact sandbox for information-theoretic decision theory.

entry.title: TReC: Evaluating Move-Induced State Changes in Instruction-Conditioned Go

author.name: Zhuangsheng Li, Yunhan Zhang, Dailin Li, Qingxian Yu, Yu Wu, Youqi Song, Bangyuan He

entry.summary: The paper proposes Transition Representation Consistency (TReC), a metric that compares how two candidate Go moves change a board-state embedding, rather than just measuring coordinate distance from an expert move. Experiments with a frozen KataGo network show TReC diverges substantially from coordinate distance, revealing different information about move quality.

entry.title: A$^3$: Adaptive Audio Agent Framework for Collaborative Edge Computing

author.name: Zexin Li, Xueyi Zhang, Tao Ren, Yiming Chen

entry.summary: A3 is an adaptive audio agent framework for edge computing that splits pipeline stages between device and server, keeps a full fallback agent on capable devices, and uses a link-aware deadline to decide when to abandon the server path. On Jetson devices and an RTX server it matches server-only latency on healthy links and survives full outages.

entry.title: Can Large Language Models Optimize Pretrained Neural Network Weights? A Multi-Phase Empirical Evaluation of Gradient-Free Editing in YOLO26 Object Detection

author.name: Mohamed Abdallah Salem

entry.summary: This empirical study evaluates whether LLMs can directly edit pretrained YOLO26 detector weights on MS COCO without gradients, comparing deterministic scaling, random perturbation, differential evolution, CMA-ES, structured interventions, local-LLM proposals, and hybrid LLM-CMA-ES against matched random controls. The multi-phase design with disjoint evaluation subsets provides a careful test of gradient-free weight editing.

entry.title: Recursive, Self, Improvement

author.name: aashish

entry.summary: A conceptual essay revisiting I.J. Good's 1965 intelligence explosion argument in light of modern AI systems that increasingly assist AI research itself, writing code and running experiments with growing autonomy. It frames current systems as early stages of a recursive self-improvement feedback loop and explores the implications for research velocity and control.

entry.title: UltraBERT-JEV: Encoder models for System One Applications

author.name: Astarag Mohapatra

entry.summary: This technical report compares fine-tuning recipes for a 380M encoder model that picks among options in a single forward pass, with one recipe following DeepSeek-V3's expert gate. The encoder beats a Qwen3-0.6B decoder baseline (69.7-72.1% vs 67.6%) on the same training data, and scoring by yes-minus-no token differences yields the largest gain.

entry.title: The Siren Song of the Inside Game

author.name: Raymond Douglas

entry.summary: A strategy essay arguing that AI safety efforts are structurally pulled toward the inside game of building trust with frontier labs at the expense of the outside game of public accountability and adversarial pressure, and that a rebalancing is now warranted. It analyzes incentive gradients in the community rather than proposing a specific new intervention.

entry.title: Why so many arguments about human nature?

author.name: AnnaSalamon

entry.summary: Anna Salamon analyzes why debates over human nature (altruism, monogamy, sleep patterns) are so heated, previewing a model in which humans are not optimizers in a particular sense. The post argues the political temperature of these debates signals something structural about how humans reason about and use claims about their own nature.

entry.title: An Operationalization of Opaque Serial Depth

author.name: Nathan Sheffield, Alek Westover, Lukas Finnveden, Alexa Pan, Julian Stastny, Ryan Greenblatt

entry.summary: We featured this paper in Research yesterday, This safety-oriented paper operationalizes opaque serial depth: the length of the longest computation path in a model that bypasses interpretable bottlenecks, serving as a proxy for unverbalized serial cognition that chain-of-thought monitoring would miss. The core contribution is a precise standard for natural-language-rooted nodes as the bottleneck criterion. As architectures shift away from token-level CoT, this framework provides a principled way to reason about when CoT oversight will fail.

entry.title: The Transformer Paradigm: Dynamic Processing and a New Principle of Inference

author.name: Marco Giunti, Fabrizia Giulia Garavaglia

entry.summary: This position-style paper argues the Transformer represents a new paradigm of inference, interpreting token representations as transformed by parameterized transforming concepts that are dynamically constructed from current input. It describes the mechanism as output-weight interconnections where outputs of some networks determine weights of others, calling this mode of processing dynamic.

entry.title: Enumerating Posterior-Supported Priors: First-Order Error of Finite-Integral Cross-Categorical Measurement Morphisms

author.name: Ning Ni, Yongxin Zhu

entry.summary: This theoretical paper addresses a subtle gap in generative modeling where the almost-everywhere convention in standard measure theory allows error components hidden in null-support sets to go unaccounted for. The authors propose an enumerating posterior-supported prior framework built on a three-layer categorical chain (Quot to MorTop to Set) that makes explicit which predicate supports each high-level object, when it is invertible, and where errors reside. It offers a verifiable structure for error accounting rather than a new distributional distance.

entry.title: Superintelligence Will Be a Multi-Agent System

author.name: Batuhan Akar

entry.summary: The author argues that superintelligence will likely arrive as a multi-agent system because most goals contain parallelizable tasks, making coordinated agents more efficient than a single sequential agent. The piece cites recent multi-agent incidents, including agents coordinating to cheat in a security-vulnerability-finding task, as early evidence of emergent multi-agent dynamics.

entry.title: Cryonics as Cause Area

author.name: Max Harms

entry.summary: A cause-prioritization essay by a longtime MIRI researcher arguing that cryonics and aldehyde-based brain preservation deserve consideration as altruistic causes, estimating roughly GiveWell-competitive QALYs per dollar under a ~3% revival probability assumption. The author, writing with disclosed ties to preservation startup Nectome, argues cryonics complements rather than competes with AI safety work and may reduce race pressure toward superintelligence.

entry.title: Can Mechanistic Interpretability Help Explain LLM Agent Failures? A Case Study on Web Element Hallucination

author.name: Mohamed Aghzal, Mor Geva, Gregory J. Stein, Ziyu Yao

entry.summary: We featured this paper in Research yesterday, This case study applies mechanistic interpretability tools to a concrete agentic failure mode: web agents hallucinating actions on elements not present on a website. Using Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct interacting with live websites, the authors show a linear probe on the last prompt token predicts hallucinations before generation (0.80 AUC), and steering along the probe direction corrects 85% of hallucinations. It extends MI from static model internals to dynamic agent decision-making.

entry.title: The vast human centipede that is AI Twitter

author.name: Dean Valentine

entry.summary: A media-forensics analysis tracing how an unverified New York Times story about Jensen Huang and an alleged Chinese spy evolved into escalating conspiracy theories on AI Twitter, including claims that Anthropic was the source. The author dissects sourcing language and the amplification chain across accounts to illustrate rumor dynamics in the AI discourse ecosystem.

entry.title: Is Abliteration Getting Harder? Not Uniformly: Refusal Removal by Direction-Based Ablation and ARA in Heretic on the Qwen3.8, Gemma 4, Olmo 3.1 and Mistral Small 3.2 LLMs Versus Their Predecessors

author.name: Richard J. Young

entry.summary: This study examines whether refusal-removal weight edits (abliteration) have become harder on newer open-weight models, testing five model release pairs including Qwen3.8-27B, Gemma-4-31B (released April 2026), Olmo-3.1, and Mistral-Small-3.2 against predecessors using direction-based ablation methods and Arbitrary-Rank Ablation. Results show refusal removal did not become uniformly harder across generations.

entry.title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Scientific Paper Search: Retrieval Success and Inference Latency on Mac Studio and NVIDIA A100

author.name: Frederic Andriantseheno Rakoto (Mnemosyne), Yannis Bendi-Ouis (Mnemosyne), Xavier Hinaut (Mnemosyne)

entry.summary: The study measures whether open-weight LLMs can support locally deployed scientific paper retrieval under practical compute constraints, characterizing latency from 512 to 128k tokens on a Mac Studio and dual-A100 server, and evaluating eight models on retrieving 70 papers across seven repositories. Retrieval success depends strongly on model choice and query specificity.

entry.title: Microdosing doomsday

author.name: Wenjun Cao

entry.summary: The author critiques what they call a one-way-time mindset in AI catastrophic risk debates, where focus on the single moment of catastrophe distorts the weighting of near-term choices. They argue incremental interventions matter because things are easiest to stop before they start, and become progressively harder to halt as certainty and acceleration build.

entry.title: X-Nav Technical Report: Real-World Long-Horizon Indoor-to-Outdoor Navigation on a Humanoid Robot

author.name: Jiaxin Huang, Chengxing Lin, Xiaoyu Luo, Sirui Chen, Jingyu Guo, Aolin Li, Kairui Chen, Rui Zhen, Cheng Wen, Kerui Gu, Shunyao Wang, Zhihui Peng, Shaoli Huang

entry.summary: We featured this paper in Research yesterday, X-Nav is reportedly the first system to take a bipedal humanoid robot through a language-instructed long-horizon navigation mission spanning indoor and outdoor environments. It includes a full pipeline from a data engine (open-source scenes, digital twins, real robots) to MELIOR, a navigation model using only built-in RGB cameras, with versions for action prediction and subgoal prediction.

entry.title: Robustness Evaluation of GPU Cloud Pricing Benchmarks under Incomplete Observations: A Controlled Missingness Study

author.name: Jooya Wong

entry.summary: This single-author study stress-tests a fixed equal-weight median GPU rental-price benchmark under missing marketplace quotes, using Monte Carlo simulations across masking mechanisms and recovery methods. It quantifies coverage and error trade-offs, finding composition-changing outages cause the largest errors.

entry.title: Optimizing Drilling Trajectories in Multi-Material Structures Using Quantum Annealers

author.name: Eneko Osaba, Antonio Rubio-Mateos

entry.summary: The paper formulates industrial drilling trajectory planning as a constrained routing problem with material-dependent costs, tool-wear penalties, and hole-grouping constraints, solved with D-Wave's Leap constrained quadratic model hybrid solver. It reports a quantum-hybrid approach evaluated against a minimum-energy objective.

entry.title: Pause Poll

author.name: Nandi

entry.summary: An announcement of a confidential poll (pausepoll.com) aiming to measure support for pausing certain kinds of AI development among people most familiar with AI, probing both trigger and exit conditions for various pause proposals. The post argues polling captures more information than open letters and protects respondents in precarious roles.

entry.title: AI-aided Decision-Making in Education - Uncertainty, Explainability, and Human Responsibility

author.name: Fabian Kieser, Paul Tschisgale, Peter Wulff

entry.summary: This book chapter argues that uncertainty quantification, explainability, and human responsibility are three essential principles for trustworthy AI-assisted decision-making in education, covering personalized learning, automated assessment, and administrative tasks. It is a position/framework chapter rather than new empirical work.

entry.title: EpiPack: A computational framework for reference mapping and out-of-reference detection for single-cell ATAC-seq data with heterogeneous peak features

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: A Nature Communications paper presenting EpiPack, a computational framework for reference mapping and out-of-reference detection in single-cell ATAC-seq data that handles heterogeneous peak features. The provided excerpt contains no content, so only the title and venue are available for assessment.

entry.title: Making the Global Clean Energy Transition Profitable: A report I wrote for COP31 (And for China)

author.name: Wes Reisen

entry.summary: A policy proposal arguing for globally funded minimum subsidies that make non-emitting energy sources at least as profitable as fossil generation and pay for retrofitting existing fossil plants, implementable unilaterally by a single wealthy government. The report frames climate change as a profitability problem solvable through direct subsidy design.

entry.title: Use-case-driven ontology modeling with the NeOn methodology for ambient assisted living

author.name: Daniele Spoladore, Marco Sacco, Alberto Trombetta, Edoardo Battisti

entry.summary: The paper describes an ontology developed as the semantic data layer of a Virtual Home Framework in an Italian Design For All project for ambient assisted living, with requirements derived from two concrete use cases: an elderly woman exercising on a cycle-ergometer at home and a designer configuring kitchens for users with impairments. Requirements are captured in an Ontology Requirements Specification Document following the NeOn methodology. It provides a shared formal description of dwellers and devices for coordinating heterogeneous smart objects.

entry.title: An exploration of the mathematical implications of a 'Poincaré causal diamond model of hyperbolic static spacetime'

author.name: Horosphere

entry.summary: A mathematics/physics exploration of horospheres and spacelike hypersurfaces in a hyperbolic static spacetime model, proving or arguing that slices through the model are necessarily hyperbolic rather than Euclidean in curvature. It continues the author's prior work on a four-dimensional Carter-Penrose diagram construction.

entry.title: On Friends at Frontier Labs

author.name: jenn

entry.summary: A reflective post on the ethical tension of having friends who work at frontier AI labs, exploring why the community has split on whether such work is acceptable and describing the author's approach of keeping the question open with friends rather than pressuring them to quit. It offers personal intuitions about the incentives and justifications of lab employees.

entry.title: Activation Steering the Nan-Shan in Typhoon

author.name: Megan Wei, Damon Pham, John Cayley, Ellie Pavlick

entry.summary: This is an audiovisual art installation based on Conrad's Typhoon in which an LLM seeded with the original text recursively consumes its own output, exploring how the text becomes alien and unwieldy over time. The authors use the work to reflect on humanity's current AI moment and the limits of conceptual frameworks for overwhelming phenomena.

entry.title: What Is the Meta-Crisis?

author.name: James Stephen Brown

entry.summary: A wide-ranging essay surveying interconnected global problems including wealth concentration from generative AI, information-sphere degradation, geopolitical conflict, and institutional failure, framed as a meta-crisis of coordination. It is a broad commentary piece rather than a technical analysis.

entry.title: The Last Arena

author.name: hiblick

entry.summary: A reflective essay comparing the present moment of compressed AI-driven futures to the felt imminence of the year 2000 in the 1990s, arguing that speculation again piles up against a psychological horizon. It is literary commentary on forecasting culture around AI rather than a technical analysis.

entry.title: Avoid the Sin of Sloth

author.name: wlancer

entry.summary: A personal reflective essay on how modern philosophical ideas, rationality techniques, and self-help advice often reduce to corollaries of teachings from the Biblical corpus, framed by an agnostic author. It is part of a thirty-day blogging challenge and is not a technical AI research contribution.

entry.title: The Power of Marketing: The Case of “20 Grams of Protein” Yogurt

author.name: becausecurious

entry.summary: A short analysis of a yogurt marketing claim showing that a 20 g protein label is less distinctive than it sounds once serving sizes (190 g vs the FDA reference 170 g) and price per pound are compared. The author used AI tools for research, fact-checking, and editing.

entry.title: Research Summary: November 16, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research highlights embodied AI, safety, and interpretability. A Song Han group (MIT) paper trains a 27B reasoning model entirely in simulation via RL—no demonstrations—showing native transfer to real robot hardware.

Safety & alignment:

  • Reasoning models confabulate to defend activation-injected beliefs about their own requests, with broad model coverage and troubling oversight implications
  • Opaque serial depth operationalizes unverbalized serial cognition, giving safety evaluators a measurable capability proxy
  • Unfinished-Bench spans 97 scenarios across 7 organizations to test rule violations by persistent autonomous agents

Interpretability & novel findings:

  • Mechanistic interpretability tools trace web agents' hallucinated actions; iWSP replaces gradient training with LLM-agent weight programming for transparent models
  • Contagious Fingerprints shows stylistic attribution signals transfer through text continuation, complicating LLM auditing

Applications & systems:

  • FETTUCCINE brings efficient brain-to-text decoding to mobile devices for assistive neuroprostheses
  • Agentic-Teacher automates failure-driven data generation for VLA post-training; Obaleth co-optimizes GPU-initiated networking inside kernels to relieve a key distributed-training bottleneck
entry.content:
Today's research highlights embodied AI, safety, and interpretability. A Song Han group (MIT) paper trains a 27B reasoning model entirely in simulation via RL—no demonstrations—showing native transfer to real robot hardware.

Safety & alignment:

  • Reasoning models confabulate to defend activation-injected beliefs about their own requests, with broad model coverage and troubling oversight implications
  • Opaque serial depth operationalizes unverbalized serial cognition, giving safety evaluators a measurable capability proxy
  • Unfinished-Bench spans 97 scenarios across 7 organizations to test rule violations by persistent autonomous agents

Interpretability & novel findings:

  • Mechanistic interpretability tools trace web agents' hallucinated actions; iWSP replaces gradient training with LLM-agent weight programming for transparent models
  • Contagious Fingerprints shows stylistic attribution signals transfer through text continuation, complicating LLM auditing

Applications & systems:

  • FETTUCCINE brings efficient brain-to-text decoding to mobile devices for assistive neuroprostheses
  • Agentic-Teacher automates failure-driven data generation for VLA post-training; Obaleth co-optimizes GPU-initiated networking inside kernels to relieve a key distributed-training bottleneck

entry.title: Training Reasoning Models in Simulation to Natively Use Real Robots

author.name: Jiaming Tang, Zhuoyang Zhang, Junxian Guo, Fangzhou Zhao, Yilong Zhao, Zekai Li, Xingyang Li, Yuyang Zhao, Song Bian, Zhijian Liu, Song Han

entry.summary: This paper shows that an open-weight 27B reasoning model can be trained via reinforcement learning entirely in simulation, without demonstrations, to act as a robot-use agent that observes the environment, reasons in chain of thought, and outputs end-effector poses directly. The authors build PEAR (Post-training Engine for Agentic Robotics) to train on simulated tasks at scale and transfer to real robots, narrowing the gap with frontier proprietary models such as GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.2, which have been available for some time. This is a significant step toward open-weight general-purpose robot control.

entry.title: Reasoning Models Confabulate to Defend Injected Beliefs About Their Own Requests

author.name: Yang Ou

entry.summary: This safety study shows that an activation-level injection of an off-topic concept can overwrite a reasoning model's belief about its own request: across six models, quote-back responses returned the injected topic in 47 of 48 cells, and models followed injected answers in 99 percent of generations despite explicit warnings. This undermines the assumption that chain-of-thought monitoring and self-report are reliably anchored to the actual prompt. It is a significant result for CoT-monitoring-based oversight proposals.

entry.title: Can Mechanistic Interpretability Help Explain LLM Agent Failures? A Case Study on Web Element Hallucination

author.name: Mohamed Aghzal, Mor Geva, Gregory J. Stein, Ziyu Yao

entry.summary: Applies mechanistic interpretability tools to a realistic agentic failure mode: web agents hallucinating actions unavailable on a website. Using Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct on live websites, the authors show a linear probe on the last prompt token predicts hallucinations before generation (0.80 AUC), and steering along the probe direction corrects 85% of hallucinations.

entry.title: Vision-Language-Action Models: A Life-Cycle Survey of Design, Training and Deployment

author.name: Suvarna Kadam (Witsense AI), Soran Parsa (University of Huddersfield)

entry.summary: A survey covering 88 works on vision-language-action (VLA) models from December 2022 to October 2026, tracing the field from RT-2 to open models fine-tunable on a single consumer GPU. It organizes the literature along a life cycle of seven axes spanning model design, training, and deployment, covering manipulation, navigation, humanoid control, world-action models, and evaluation.

entry.title: FETTUCCINE: Fast and efficient brain-to-text decoding on mobile devices

author.name: Jonathan D. McCart, Pranav I. Deevi, Mehdi Azabou, Nanda H. Krishna, Caleb A. McKinney, Nicholas S. Card, Sergey D. Stavisky, Chethan Pandarinath

entry.summary: FETTUCCINE is an end-to-end brain-to-text framework for speech neuroprostheses that runs efficiently on mobile hardware, replacing compute-intensive language-model stacks whose variable latency hinders natural conversation for people who cannot speak. By leveraging compact, efficient architectures it maintains decoding accuracy while dramatically reducing latency and compute. This addresses a key barrier to real-world deployment of speech BCIs.

entry.title: Contagious Fingerprints: When LLMs Inherit Another Model's Identity

author.name: Zailong Tian

entry.summary: This paper shows that the stylistic fingerprint classifiers use to identify which LLM produced a text is contagious: when one model continues a conversation started by another, it inherits the original model's fingerprint. This enables silent API-relay swaps to evade detection, with substitution detection dropping substantially after a handoff. Preregistered experiments trace the effect to imitation of prior conversation turns, and retraining only fixes substitutes seen in training.

entry.title: Agentic-Teacher: An Agentic Data Engine for Failure-Driven VLA Post-Training

author.name: Gongyue Teng, Yuqing Xie, Yixian Zhang, Feng Gao, Shu'ang Yu, Jiaji Rao, Sukai Wang, Guanghui Ren, Ya Zhang, Maoqing Yao, Yu Wang, Chao Yu, Xinlei Chen

entry.summary: Agentic-Teacher is an autonomous data engine for post-training vision-language-action models: given a VLA checkpoint and task tools, coding agents analyze failed rollouts, select intervention states, and iteratively build closed-loop code policies that become reusable demonstration generators targeting the model's weaknesses. Failure-driven curation makes generated demos better supervision than naive success-only rollouts.

entry.title: An Operationalization of Opaque Serial Depth

author.name: Nathan Sheffield, Alek Westover, Lukas Finnveden, Alexa Pan, Julian Stastny, Ryan Greenblatt

entry.summary: This paper operationalizes opaque serial depth, a proxy for the amount of unverbalized serial cognition a model can perform, defined as the longest computation path not passing through an interpretable bottleneck. It defines natural-language-rooted nodes as the standard for what counts as such a bottleneck. The work is motivated by chain-of-thought monitorability and the risk that architectural shifts could undermine CoT-based oversight.

entry.title: X-Nav Technical Report: Real-World Long-Horizon Indoor-to-Outdoor Navigation on a Humanoid Robot

author.name: Jiaxin Huang, Chengxing Lin, Xiaoyu Luo, Sirui Chen, Jingyu Guo, Aolin Li, Kairui Chen, Rui Zhen, Cheng Wen, Kerui Gu, Shunyao Wang, Zhihui Peng, Shaoli Huang

entry.summary: X-Nav is presented as the first system to complete a language-instructed long-horizon navigation mission from indoors to outdoors on a bipedal humanoid robot. It spans a full pipeline including a data engine using open-source scenes, digital twins, and real robots, plus an RGB-only navigation model (MELIOR) in action-prediction and dual variants. This is a significant systems demonstration for humanoid robotics, aligned with AGIBOT's push toward autonomous workplace arrival.

entry.title: Interpretable weight-space programming builds transparent transformers and brain encoding models

author.name: Yash Mehta, Chandan Singh, Weijia Xu, Richard J. Antonello, Adeen Flinker, Nima Mesgarani, Michael F. Bonner, Nebojsa Jojic, Jianfeng Gao

entry.summary: Building on yesterday's News coverage of weight-space programming, The paper introduces interpretable weight-space programming (iWSP), where an LLM agent iteratively constructs interpretable models by explicitly programming their weights and features in code without backpropagation, drawing on prior knowledge and reasoning over previous trials. The authors apply it to build transparent transformers and brain encoding models that reveal which stimulus features drive predictions of neural activity. Author list includes Microsoft researchers and established neuroscience/ML figures.

entry.title: Unfinished-Bench: Measuring Rule Violations by Persistent Agents in Realistic Work Environments

author.name: Seunghyun Lee, Jaehui Hwang, Dongyoon Han, Sangdoo Yun

entry.summary: Presents Unfinished-Bench, a benchmark of 97 scenarios across 7 organizations and 7 risk categories where persistent autonomous agents face embedded rules that conflict with task goals, requiring them to decide without user input when completion would require a violation. Findings indicate that increased persistence raised violations of rules that models could not see.

entry.title: Compiling Specialized GPU-Initiated Networking

author.name: Javid Baydamirli, Ismayil Ismayilov, Kaan Oktay, Didem Unat

entry.summary: The authors present Obaleth, a compiler that exposes GPU-initiated communication inside a kernel's intermediate representation, co-optimizing communication with computation and lowering it to specialized transport code across NVIDIA and AMD GPUs. On H100s it sends small messages up to 3.3x faster than existing paths and achieves 1.25-2.3x all-to-all speedups on 256 GPUs versus NVSHMEM and NCCL GIN with reduced memory footprints.

entry.title: Restoring Diversity in Distilled Image and Video Generators by Probing Activations

author.name: Furkan Horoz, Ozgur Kara, Kaan Oktay, Adil Kaan Akan, Atakan Kara, Anand Bhattad, James Matthew Rehg

entry.summary: This work diagnoses diversity collapse in few-step distilled diffusion models, showing students preserve total activation variance but concentrate it into far fewer directions, localized to a specific intermediate block at the first denoising step. Because the collapse is a variance misallocation rather than lost capacity, the authors can restore sample diversity with targeted interventions.

entry.title: Folding Language Models into Themselves

author.name: Ziyang Zhang, Yubin Jing, Yuyao Li, Haofan Wang, Yichen Gong

entry.summary: Concertina is a compression method that builds a compact student model directly from a teacher's weights rather than training from scratch. It folds every group of N adjacent teacher layers into one shared block executed N times, with low-rank corrections and per-token gating to recover original layer behavior, paired with a balanced distillation data recipe.

entry.title: WaferTetris: Efficient Freeform Mapping on Wafer-Scale Accelerators

author.name: Dayou Du, Congjie He, Andrew Boutros, Luo Mai, Vaughn Betz, Jianyi Cheng

entry.summary: WaferTetris removes the fixed geometric layouts imposed by template-based mapping on wafer-scale accelerators, using a Tetris-like freeform strategy to flexibly pack computation across the PE grid. This improves utilization of compute and memory resources on chips with hundreds of thousands of processing elements, addressing a major programming and mapping challenge at wafer scale.

entry.title: Aligning AI Teams

author.name: Siddarth Srinivasan, Morgan Jane Matthews, Jascha Sohl-Dickstein, Erik Jones

entry.summary: This paper, including author Jascha Sohl-Dickstein (formerly Google Brain), investigates why alignment training on individual LLM agents fails to transfer to multi-agent settings, studying sepsis triage, news recommendation, and consulting-proposal tasks. Key findings include that the single-vs-team safety gap lacks a clear trend with model capability and that natural interventions like agent critique or group chat do not reliably preserve alignment transfer. This is directly relevant to safety of multi-agent deployments.

entry.title: WebArena-Pro: A Heterogeneous, Multimodal, Reproducible Benchmark for Web Agents

author.name: Imene Kerboua, Fatemeh Pesaran Zadeh, Xing Han L\`u, Weijian Qi, Alexander Miller, Junyi Song, Yunjia Tian, Dongjin Kang, Seyeon Choi, Marzia Nouri, Ewen Gueguen, Matteo Boglioni, Fengyuan Liu, Zeyi Liao, Mengqi Yuan, Yue Li, Alexandre Lacoste, Alexandre Drouin, Spandana Gella, Huan Sun, Gunhee Kim, Siva Reddy

entry.summary: WebArena-Pro extends reproducible web-agent benchmarking with 300 tasks across 20 self-hosted web applications, adding heterogeneous applications, multimodal content including audio and video, and stateful workflows. It addresses gaps in existing benchmarks that cover few applications, sacrifice reproducibility when live, or ignore audio/video understanding.

entry.title: Securing Multi-Agent Systems by Design

author.name: Xilong Wang, Xiaoxing Chen, Neil Gong

entry.summary: The authors introduce response manipulation attacks (ReMA), where malicious agents in a multi-agent LLM system iteratively optimize their subtask responses to steer the final aggregated solution, formulating both untargeted and targeted variants as optimization problems. They also propose SecMAS, a defense framework designed to protect multi-agent systems against such attacks. This addresses a growing security concern as LLM agent fleets are deployed for complex task decomposition.

entry.title: Gamer: A Generalist Vision-Language-Action Foundation Model for Long-Horizon Real-Time Game Agent

author.name: Run Luo, Kuan Zhang, Qi Deng, Yukun Chen, Zhihao Yang, Yufei Zhang, Renrong Hu, Yi Zhang, Guiyu Ma, Tianyu Fan, Longze Chen, Hao Sun, Jiaming Li, Jiaming Yang, Xiaohao Liu, Tao Tan, Minzheng Wang, Hangtian Jia, Shuai Yuan, Lvdi Wang, Xiao Liu, Chao Ma, Yuting Zou, Yinhe Zheng, Xiaobo Xia, Dawei Jiang, Shaoqing Ren

entry.summary: Introduces Gamer, an end-to-end generalist agent framework combining perception, memory management, and multi-step reasoning for long-horizon tasks in interactive 2D and 3D environments. It is pre-trained on tens of thousands of hours of device-level keyboard/mouse trajectories from simulated games and embodied settings, with sparse-thinking instruction tuning to cut redundant computation during real-time interaction.

entry.title: TIDE: Reclaiming Lost Performance In On-Policy Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Mathew Jacob, Morgan Borjigin-Wang, Kan Zhu, Po Hao Chen, Yi Pan, Andy Ruan, Nayani Modugula, Ethan Lavi, Luis Ceze, Malte Schwarzkopf, Akshay Narayan, Deepti Raghavan, Stephanie Wang

entry.summary: TIDE is an RL post-training system for LLMs that preserves on-policy semantics while recovering GPU utilization lost to long-tail rollouts. It dynamically repurposes rollout GPUs for training during stragglers and migrates rollouts between inference engines to raise decoding batch sizes, using an adaptive migration policy. This addresses a concrete, widely experienced efficiency problem in synchronous colocated RLHF training.

entry.title: WeatherDreamer: Learning a World Model from Multimodal Earth Observations

author.name: Kate Duffy, Elise Penn, Tristan Ballard, August Posch, Thomas J. Vandal

entry.summary: WeatherDreamer is a world model that learns the data assimilation cycle end-to-end from 18 global observing systems without reanalysis data, inferring latent atmospheric states from sparse irregular observations, advancing them with learned dynamics, and correcting them hourly. It can also predict what any observing system would measure, enabling observation-to-observation forecasting that avoids dependence on expensive six-hourly operational assimilation.

entry.title: Muon Attains $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-3})$ Iteration Complexity under Shuffling

author.name: Kun Huang, Shi Pu, Karl Henrik Johansson

entry.summary: This paper provides the first iteration complexity analysis of the Muon optimizer—a momentum-based orthogonalized first-order method reported to accelerate large language model training—in the practically important setting of sampling without replacement. For smooth nonconvex finite-sum problems with polar-map orthogonalization, the authors establish an O(epsilon^-3) iteration complexity guarantee.

entry.title: Agent-as-a-Judge

author.name: Runyang You, Hongru Cai, Caiqi Zhang, Qiancheng Xu, Meng Liu, Tiezheng Yu, Yongqi Li, Wenjie Li

entry.summary: This paper proposes extending LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation to agentic settings where the judge can actively gather evidence, since reliable verdicts may require unrecorded environmental states or external factual verification that passive judges cannot obtain. The Agent-as-a-Judge formulation has the evaluator interact with the environment to collect the information needed for scoring, preference, and critique. This addresses a core evaluation bottleneck as AI systems become autonomous agents.

entry.title: MMFlash: Faster Speculative Decoding for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Sicheng Feng, Zigeng Chen, Song Wang, Gongfan Fang, Xinchao Wang

entry.summary: MMFlash studies multimodal speculative decoding, introducing a KL-divergence-based metric of token-level visual dependence that reveals acceptance rates drop from 46 to 22 percent across visual-dependence quartiles. It then adaptively adjusts drafting based on this signal, improving speculative decoding speed for vision-language models where diffusion drafters underperform.

entry.title: ESI: An Embodied Self-Improvement Flywheel for LLM-VLA Agents

author.name: Yundi Cai, Zihan Wang, Chenxi Han, Yi Cheng, Houde Liu, Zilei Wang

entry.summary: ESI introduces an automated self-improvement loop for modular embodied agents that combine pretrained LLMs with vision-language-action policies, jointly refining the LLM prompts, the shared skill interface, and the VLA parameters through environmental interaction. This addresses the problem of actions diverging from the LLM's intended subtask and undoing restored states.

entry.title: LLMs are below chance on TASTE once a shortcut is removed

author.name: Ziqian Zhong

entry.summary: Identifies a shortcut in the TASTE benchmark for judging AI-safety research proposals: proposals heavy in mechanistic-interpretability terminology score systematically worse, so a trivial word-count baseline beats all tested LLMs at 63% accuracy. When restricted to non-interpretability proposals, models with ECI above 158 fall below 50% rubric-only accuracy, with OpenAI models averaging 29.6% and accuracy declining with capability, suggesting systematic bias.

entry.title: Do Machines Learn Deviance From Their Peers? A Randomized Test of Differential Association With AI Agents

author.name: Murat Ozer, Arif Akgul, Amitabh Chakravorty

entry.summary: In a preregistered experiment, 420 teams of three AI agents (1,260 agents across seven models) were randomly assigned peer types on unsolvable coding tasks: a scripted teammate claiming to have cheated, claiming honesty, or saying nothing. The design uses AI agents to eliminate the selection problem that plagues tests of differential association theory in humans, examining whether deviance spreads through interaction.

entry.title: HARDTESTGEN: A High-Quality RL Verifier Generation Pipeline for LLM Algorithmic Coding

author.name: Zhongmou He, Yee Man Choi, Kexun Zhang, Jiabao Ji, Junting Zhou, Dejia Xu, Ivan Bercovich, Aidan Zhang, Yixiao Zeng, Lei Li

entry.summary: Presents a pipeline for synthesizing high-quality test cases that catch well-disguised incorrect code solutions, producing HARDTESTS, a dataset of 26.6k algorithmic problems with synthetic tests. The generated tests improve verification accuracy of LLM-generated code by over 11 percentage points versus existing tests.

entry.title: Improved Regret via Variance-Aware Policy Optimization in Adversarial MDPs

author.name: Ofir Schlisselberg, Alon Cohen, Yishay Mansour

entry.summary: Achieves improved regret bounds for episodic adversarial MDPs with unknown dynamics and full-information rewards, with a leading term that improves two incomparable prior bounds by factors of sqrt(S/H) and sqrt(H^3), leaving only sqrt(H) to the lower-bound scale. The key technique is a reduction from unknown to known dynamics for downstream-dependent algorithms.

entry.title: Vision-as-a-Tool: Visual Harness for Multimodal Agentic Coding

author.name: Haolin Yang, Wenshan Wu, Jin Jiang, Yu Cheng, Yan Xia, Ting Song, Yangyu Huang, Zhiliang Peng, Wenhui Wang, Hangbo Bao, Yuzhe Zhang, Wen-Da Wei, Tengchao Lv, Li Dong, Lei Cui, Furu Wei

entry.summary: This paper from a Microsoft-affiliated team (including Furu Wei and Li Dong) introduces the Vision-as-a-Tool (VaaT) paradigm for agentic coding, where visual capabilities are exposed as external tools rather than relying on an agent's intrinsic vision, decoupling agent performance from internal perceptual limits and enabling text-only agents to do visual reasoning. This reframing addresses a fundamental bottleneck in multimodal agentic coding systems.

entry.title: Tracing Actual Causes with Counterfactual Witness Maps

author.name: Tim Woydt, Matej Ze\v{c}evi\'c, Kristian Kersting, Moritz Willig

entry.summary: This paper addresses Halpernian actual causation in structural causal models, introducing witness targets and an ancestor intervention grammar to construct a finite directed acyclic witness map. It provides the first sound and complete enumeration procedure for finding all actual causes, enabling downstream tasks like responsibility attribution, blame assessment, and causal-harm grading.

entry.title: Interpreting Coding Agents Through Their Behavioral Trajectories

author.name: Ibragim Badertdinov, Alexander Golubev

entry.summary: Analyzes 143,209 execution trajectories from 125 coding-agent configurations spanning 117 models, using a rule-based parser that maps raw traces to high-level actions (repo search, file editing, test execution), audited against a six-model consensus reference. Finds agents with similar solve rates differ substantially in how they explore, modify, and verify code.

entry.title: Rethinking Visual Reasoning in Text-to-Image Reward Modeling

author.name: Shiye Su, Xiaohan Wang, Ludwig Schmidt, Serena Yeung-Levy

entry.summary: The paper shows that widely used text-to-image reward models perform poorly on targeted visual reasoning tests, and that preference fine-tuning actually erodes visual capabilities inherited from strong vision-language backbones. It proposes a data-centric intervention that injects visual reasoning supervision into preference training to soften the tradeoff between visual reasoning and preference accuracy. This matters because reward models drive both inference-time selection and RL post-training for image generation.

entry.title: TelePhysica: Agentic Reconstruction of Physically Interactive Scenes

author.name: Ruiqi Shu, Xufeng Zhan, Yuanzhi Liang, Haibin Huang, Chi Zhang, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: TelePhysica is a closed-loop framework that reconstructs an executable, physically consistent 3D world from a single photograph, using a vision-language coding agent to synthesize meshes and declarative physical models in two stages. It supports persistent 3D mechanical equilibrium, mid-rollout intervention, and counterfactual force control, addressing failures of both diffusion video models and single-pass 3D reconstruction. The reconstructed scenes drive stateful interaction and trajectory-grounded video synthesis.

entry.title: Black-Box Uncertainty Quantification for Large Language Models via Ensemble-of-Ensembles

author.name: Wang Ma, Debarun Bhattacharjya, Junkyu Lee, Nhan H Pham, Harsha Kokel, Qiang Ji

entry.summary: Introduces a two-level ensemble method for black-box LLM uncertainty quantification that decomposes uncertainty into aleatoric and epistemic components: stochastic decoding forms an inner ensemble and meaning-preserving prompt perturbations form an outer ensemble, with variability measured in embedding space and the law of total covariance providing an exact within/between decomposition.

entry.title: Delayed Effects of Temporary Weight Decay in Muon Pretraining

author.name: Md Rifat Arefin, Ravid Shwartz-Ziv, Ernie Chang, Chinnadhurai Sankar, Rylan Conway, Aristide Baratin, Irina Rish, Adithya Sagar, Patrick Huber

entry.summary: This empirical study shows that temporary weight decay in Muon-trained decoder-only Transformers (162M to 3.4B parameters) can transiently increase validation loss when removed yet reduce it at the final training budget, with the effect depending on window placement and scale. A schedule transferred from 162M to 1.4B initially underperforms, overtakes no-decay after 73 percent of training, and finishes better while beating constant-decay baselines. It highlights delayed, scale-dependent effects of optimization interventions in LLM pretraining.

entry.title: Learning Anisotropic Prediction Targets for Flow Models

author.name: Rayhan Zirvi, Hansheng Chen, Gordon Wetzstein, Leonidas Guibas

entry.summary: This paper introduces AnisoFlow, which replaces the hand-chosen prediction target (velocity, noise, or clean data) in flow-based generative models with a fully learnable target that scales the noise component anisotropically in a learned basis. A closed-form map exactly recovers the velocity from the network prediction, so training optimizes the target purely for predictability while leaving the architecture, loss, and sampler unchanged.

entry.title: StreamEmbed: Real-Time Indexing from Pixels for Screenshot Retrieval

author.name: Dayoon Ko, Yichuan Wang, Soyeong Jeong, Joseph E. Gonzalez, Gunhee Kim, Sewon Min

entry.summary: StreamEmbed is a system for incremental visual embedding of streaming screenshots that exploits pixel redundancy across frames using spatial token pruning and temporal KV-cache reuse, enabling real-time indexing where full visual encoding takes over two seconds per screenshot. This enables searchable visual memory for people and agents without the information loss of OCR-based indexing. It demonstrates that visual encoders need not recompute representations from scratch for every frame.

entry.title: PaperCritic: Training AI Reviewers to Assess the Soundness of Papers

author.name: Hyun Ryu, Ji Yong Cho, Eunho Yang, Moontae Lee, June Yong Yang, Sean Welleck, Carolyn Rose

entry.summary: PaperCritic focuses AI reviewing specifically on soundness, defining a learning objective that jointly maximizes precision (soundness and substantiveness of review points) and recall (coverage of high-quality reference points). The authors construct PaperSound-23K, a quality-labeled dataset of review points from 1K ICLR submissions and 23K human-written reviews, and train models against this objective. This offers a more principled formulation of AI reviewing than imitation of full human reviews.

entry.title: Deep Bundle Adjustment

author.name: Pak Hong Chui, Hector Andrade-Loarca, Daniel Cremers

entry.summary: Introduces DeepBA, a graph neural network that amortizes bundle adjustment, recovering camera poses, intrinsics, and scene structure from 2D matches across an arbitrary number of views. Instead of solving a nonlinear least-squares problem per scene, the learned network iteratively refines estimates from geometric residuals and converges from a cold start, trained with scale-invariant supervision enabling datasets with arbitrary metric units. From a strong group including Daniel Cremers at TUM.

entry.title: TouchTwin: Scaling Human Touch Data via Real-to-Sim-to-Real

author.name: Huiwen Han, Nuo Chen, Ziyao Zeng, Dayou Li, Hao Wang, Amir Hossein Rahmati, Xiaoning Qian, Bangya Liu, Zhiwen Fan

entry.summary: TouchTwin quantifies the force gap in real-to-sim-to-real dexterous manipulation pipelines, showing that vision-tracked hand poses miss how hard fingers press: imitation policies grip with only 0.31x recorded force while physics replays overshoot at 1.55x. It closes this gap by scaling measured human touch data through wearable touch capture and simulation twinning.

entry.title: On the Utility of Pre-Trained Visual Representations for Policy Learning of Contact-Rich Insertion Tasks

author.name: Leon Kim, Dinesh Jayaraman, Michael Posa

entry.summary: This paper systematically compares pre-trained visual representations from vision foundation models against an explicit contact-centric representation for learning contact-rich robotic insertion tasks.
